Gain the skills to become a confident and capable Registered Nurse. Experience world-class learning with workshops, online classes and diverse clinical placements to prepare you to make a real difference in the healthcare sector.

Nursing is the science of professional caring and offers opportunities to promote and restore health, prevent illness and alleviate suffering. You'll learn how to make critical decisions, coordinate care and educate patients. Through diverse clinical placements, you will develop advanced healthcare, advocacy and leadership skills.

Highlights of studying the Bachelor of Nursing
  • Future-proof your skills through the latest technology and teaching approaches.
  • Study in our on-campus simulation nursing wards and high-tech labs.
  • Take part in interactive workshops, simulated practice, online learning and varied clinical placements.

  • Enhance your skills through evidence-based care, focusing on nursing as a profession, while gaining exposure to various nursing specialties and receiving integrated employment support.
  • We produce the highest-quality graduates in the profession, supported by our culture of excellence in teaching, research and clinical practice.
Exciting clinical placements from the get-go

Undertake work-integrated clinical placements with a difference. Choose from a range of placements in rural, remote and overseas locations and be supported by our expert team of practising professionals.

Honours

The Bachelor of Nursing (Honours) (2094) is available as an additional year of study.

description:
Join a medical program driven by a commitment to providing exceptional healthcare for all communities. Through dynamic team-based learning, hands-on clinical skills sessions, and immersive clinical placements, you'll gain the expertise, confidence and compassion needed to thrive as an intern. Graduating as a skilled, caring and capable medical professional, you'll be ready to make a lasting impact in the medical field and contribute to a healthier future for all.

Immerse yourself in clinical experiences from the outset through our General Practice Longitudinal Program (GPLP), as well as community and in-hospital settings. Take part in extensive clinical placements and community work experiences at leading hospitals and clinics across South East Queensland and Northern New South Wales, ranging from rural settings through to the Gold Coast University Hospital and the Sunshine Coast Hospital and Health Service. 

This program is delivered in collaboration with Rural Medical Education Australia (RuralMedEd) at the Toowoomba location.

Highlights of studying the Doctor of Medicine at Griffith 
  • The Doctor of Medicine is accredited by the Australian Medical Council. 
  • Learn how to serve diverse populations through community-focused care. 
  • Teaching includes masterclasses led by visiting experts, renowned national leaders with practical, first-hand experience in their fields. 
  • Develop communication and clinical reasoning skills essential for effective patient assessment, while learning about the art and science of medicine in its wider social and ethical context. 
  • Master your skills in our wide variety of teaching environments, including cutting-edge facilities, virtual reality and learning simulations. 
  • Gain a comprehensive understanding of diverse healthcare settings, including First Peoples Health and the unique needs of both rural and metropolitan communities. 
  • Develop an understanding of the importance of lifelong learning and learn how to be resourceful in seeking information and adapting to new technologies. 
Integrated, practice-ready learning  

Benefit from a curriculum that emphasises the integration of foundational concepts with clinical applications. Our innovative, evidence-based approach includes case-based tutorials and practical lab and clinical skills training, conducted alongside students from other healthcare disciplines to mirror real clinical settings. Capstone courses are designed to prepare you for clinical training and internships, ensuring you become a practice-ready medical graduate. 

The Doctor of Medicine is an AQF Level 9 Masters Extended degree, which means it's a postgraduate qualification that provides advanced professional training.  

MD/PhD pathway 

This pathway will allow a small number of MD students (5 to 10 students) to complete the first two years of the program before commencing two years of full time PhD work in clinical research in a range of fields such as neuropsychiatry, pathology, neurology, primary healthcare, health economics, cardiology, Indigenous health, medical education and medical ethics. The program will incorporate clinical/bedside teaching plus reintegration to the MD component while doing the PhD research project. Candidates would then recommence the normal MD program to complete Medicine 3 and Medicine 4 of the MD whilst completing the PhD part-time. Students will be eligible for PhD scholarships. 

Pathways to Medicine information sessions

Register to join our annual Pathways to Medicine information session. Visit the website to view the most recent webinar recording and explore pathways to medicine and scholarship information.

The Brisbane South (Nathan) offering of this program is scheduled to be delivered at the Treasury Building at our Brisbane City campus in 2027. If scheduled opening is delayed, courses may be delivered all or in part at our other Brisbane locations.

Queensland's #1 university for both AI research and economics. (ShanghaiRanking's Global Ranking of Academic Subjects 2026)

Step into the future of business with a degree designed for tomorrow's leaders. The Bachelor of Business equips you with the skills, values and knowledge to thrive in a rapidly changing economy. You'll learn to think differently, embrace innovation and champion ethical, sustainable and inclusive practices that are shaping the next generation of business professionals.

Highlights of studying the Bachelor of Business
  • Built for the new economy, the Bachelor of Business integrates sustainability, inclusivity and ethical business practices from day one.
  • From your second year, you'll specialise by choosing from a wide variety of majors.
  • You may choose from a wide range of double degrees, combining Business with another area of study to match your career goals.
  • Gain practical experience while you study through initiatives such as the Griffith Tax Clinic or our Student-Managed Investment Fund.
  • Enhance your professional development with BusinessPLUS, giving you access to exclusive workshops, events, mentoring and career support. 
Foundation first year 

Your first two trimesters set you up for success with six discovery subjects. These foundation courses focus on the critical skills needed for business and apply them to real challenges. You'll explore problem-solving, decision-making and business strategy through the lens of sustainability and inclusiveness, while building the confidence to adapt to change and identify opportunities in evolving industries.

Industry connections and internships 

This degree has been designed with input from business leaders and draws on our cutting-edge research. You'll benefit from academics who teach, research and work in industry, ensuring your studies are relevant to current business challenges. With access to Griffith Business School's 150+ industry partners, you can build valuable professional networks through internships, consulting projects and workshops.

Global opportunities and future-ready skills 

With the option to add a language major or study abroad, you'll graduate ready to work across borders and cultures. We're committed to preparing you for an international career. Our focus on practical learning means you'll leave with more than just a degree - you'll have the professional skills, confidence and networks to succeed in the business world of today and tomorrow.  

Majors

You'll choose your major in second year, with the option to boost your career potential by completing two majors. With a huge range of majors available on-campus and online, you can tailor your learning to your interests and study from wherever works best for you.

Behavioural Science

Blend economics, psychology and social marketing to understand how people and institutions make decisions. Graduates use evidence-based tools to design better policies, products and services, and are well-prepared for roles in government, consultancies and behavioural insights teams.

Business Analytics

Harness data, quantitative methods and technology to generate actionable insights and drive smarter business decisions. Graduates are equipped for roles in analytics, strategy, operations and business intelligence across a wide range of industries.

Employment Relations (online only)

Study workplace law, industrial relations and human resource strategy to manage complex employment environments in the public and private sectors. Graduates are prepared for careers in HR, workforce planning, policy and industrial advocacy.

Events

Plan and deliver large-scale events across sport, tourism, media and culture. Develop skills in project management, stakeholder engagement, budgeting and logistics. Graduates are well-prepared for careers with event and conference organisers, sporting bodies and entertainment companies.

Financial Crime Investigation and Compliance

Combat money laundering, fraud and regulatory risk in a field the World Economic Forum estimates costs the global economy more than $1.45 trillion annually. Graduates are ready for careers in financial crime compliance, sanctions management, anti-money laundering, forensic accounting and regulatory advisory.

Human Resource Management

Accredited by the Australian HR Institute (AHRI). Learn recruitment, talent development, performance management and organisational change. Graduates work across sectors including business management, counselling, workforce planning and policy.

Innovation and Entrepreneurship

Launch and grow your own venture. Develop the mindset, tools and networks needed to succeed as a founder, intrapreneur or serial entrepreneur. Graduates are prepared for self-employment, high-growth start-ups or leadership roles within innovative organisations.

International Business

Navigate global trade, cross-cultural management and international strategy. Griffith is a pioneer in international business education, and graduates leave with the skills and knowledge to succeed in the modern global economy across private, public and non-government sectors.

Logistics and Supply Chain Management

Manage the flow of goods, services and information across global supply chains ¿ from procurement and supplier relationships to inventory management, warehousing and last-mile delivery. This major is accredited by the Chartered Institute of Procurement and Supply

description:
Begin your journey to becoming a doctor. Unlock your potential and take the first step toward a transformative career in medicine. You will gain the foundational knowledge and skills required for success in medical school and the healthcare sector.

This degree, designed for high-achieving secondary school leavers, offers a direct pathway into the Doctor of Medicine (5099)*.

Highlights of studying the Bachelor of Medical Science
  • Build your foundation for medicine by studying core sciences including chemistry, biology, anatomy, physiology, microbiology, genetics and biostatistics.
  • From second year, you will advance into specialised disciplines such as immunology, infectious disease, pharmacology, and biochemistry, connecting this knowledge to clinical contexts.
  • Develop skills related to health and science communication, where you will learn to evaluate and communicate complex health and scientific information to diverse audiences.
  • Learn in labs and interactive virtual environments with the latest technology and tools in our state-of-the-art medical facilities.
  • The medical sciences job market is set to grow +6.5% by 2028. With the growth of the healthcare sector and a shortage of highly skilled medical scientists, Griffith graduates will experience demand for their services in Australia and overseas.
Applied clinical skills 

Collaborate with leading healthcare and research institutions and gain practical experience with clinical and laboratory placements. You'll engage in practical applications through labs, case-based learning and problem-solving activities that develop your clinical reasoning.

Start your journey to becoming a doctor  

Graduates of this degree who meet the GPA requirements will gain provisional entry into Griffith's Doctor of Medicine (5099). If you progress to the Doctor of Medicine, you'll be preparing for a career in specialist clinical practice, primary care medicine, preventive health, medical or translational research and healthcare services.

*The Doctor of Medicine is an Extended Masters program (AQF Level 9).

description:
Take your first step towards a rewarding career in dentistry. Develop a strong foundation in our cutting-edge health facilities and gain clinical experience with real patients as you build the skills to excel in this essential profession.

On successful completion of this degree, you'll be eligible for entry to the Master of Dentistry (5703) to complete your training.

Highlights of studying the Bachelor of Dental Health Science
  • Study the science behind the human body and oral health, including anatomy, physiology, biochemistry, pathology, and microbiology.
  • Develop practical dental skills, clinical techniques and professional practice knowledge right from your first year.
  • Learn from practising educators who have also led and contributed to globally significant research.
  • Our dedicated spaces for dental researchers make Griffith University the first choice for students studying dentistry and oral health.
Clinical training and experience with real patients 

Gain experience in our state-of-the-art simulation labs before applying your skills in the Griffith Dental Clinic, where you'll work alongside registered dentists and dental specialists. With 117 modern dental chairs and over 6,000 patient appointments each year, you'll have extensive opportunities to develop your clinical expertise.

Rural student access

Through our Rural Priority Access Scheme, Griffith University sets aside Commonwealth supported places in the Bachelor of Dental Health Science specifically for students from rural backgrounds. To check your rural geographic eligibility, visit griffith.edu.au/rural-priority.

Honours

The Bachelor of Dental Health Science (Honours) (2126) is available through an additional year of study for students who want to take their education to an advanced level and produce original research. It includes an additional one year of full-time study, or two years part-time and offers a pathway to higher degree research. Honours is an attractive credential for potential employers.

description:
Help people recover, move better, prevent injury and live healthier lives. 

At Griffith, you'll study at Australia's leading university for elite athletes* and graduate as a skilled, confident and compassionate physiotherapist. Physiotherapy is about more than rehabilitation - it's about empowering people to reach their potential by managing pain, restoring function and preventing future injury.

With extensive clinical placements and an honours program that sharpens both clinical and research expertise, you'll graduate ready to make a meaningful impact across health, sport and community sectors. 

Highlights of studying the Bachelor of Physiotherapy (Honours)
  • Strong focus on evidence-based practice and interprofessional collaboration.
  • Explore how the body moves through biomedical, physical and behavioural sciences.
  • Develop practical skills in musculoskeletal, neurological and cardiorespiratory practice.
  • Graduate with a degree accredited by the Australian Physiotherapy Council (APC), ready to apply for registration with the Physiotherapy Board of Australia.
  • Your training will open doors to dynamic career pathways, from everyday practice to involvement in large-scale sporting and international events, like the Brisbane 2032 Olympic and Paralympic Games.
  • Use your honours year as a launchpad for postgraduate study, such as a master's degree or PhD, or to pursue advanced research opportunities.
Professional placements

Gain hands-on experience through full-time supervised placements in hospitals, private practices, community health centres and aged care facilities across Australia. You'll work with patients in settings from intensive care and rehabilitation to sports medicine and community clinics, supported by expert clinicians and award-winning teachers. These experiences will equip you with the confidence and practical skills to step straight into professional practice. 

World-class facilities, industry connections, life-changing careers

Physiotherapy is a rapidly growing profession, and Griffith is known for producing graduates who are ready to make an impact from day one. You'll learn in our state-of-the-art Griffith Health Centre and the Gold Coast Health and Knowledge Precinct, with access to purpose-built labs, simulation spaces and professional-grade equipment. Train alongside elite athletes using world-class facilities and benefit from the guidance of both staff and strong industry connections, preparing you for a career that truly changes lives.

*Griffith had more athletes at the 2024 Paris Olympics than any other Australian university.

Help people recover, move better, prevent injury and live healthier lives. 

At Griffith, you'll study at Australia's leading university for elite athletes* and graduate as a skilled, confident and compassionate physiotherapist. Physiotherapy is about more than rehabilitation - it's about empowering people to reach their potential by managing pain, restoring function and preventing future injury.

With extensive clinical placements and an honours program that sharpens both clinical and research expertise, you'll graduate ready to make a meaningful impact across health, sport and community sectors. 

Highlights of studying the Bachelor of Physiotherapy (Honours)
  • Strong focus on evidence-based practice and interprofessional collaboration.
  • Explore how the body moves through biomedical, physical and behavioural sciences.
  • Develop practical skills in musculoskeletal, neurological and cardiorespiratory practice.
  • Graduate with a degree accredited by the Australian Physiotherapy Council (APC), ready to apply for registration with the Physiotherapy Board of Australia.
  • Your training will open doors to dynamic career pathways, from everyday practice to involvement in large-scale sporting and international events, like the Brisbane 2032 Olympic and Paralympic Games.
  • Use your honours year as a launchpad for postgraduate study, such as a master's degree or PhD, or to pursue advanced research opportunities.
Professional placements

Gain hands-on experience through full-time supervised placements in hospitals, private practices, community health centres and aged care facilities across Australia. You'll work with patients in settings from intensive care and rehabilitation to sports medicine and community clinics, supported by expert clinicians and award-winning teachers. These experiences will equip you with the confidence and practical skills to step straight into professional practice. 

World-class facilities, industry connections, life-changing careers

Physiotherapy is a rapidly growing profession, and Griffith is known for producing graduates who are ready to make an impact from day one. You'll learn in our state-of-the-art Griffith Health Centre and the Gold Coast Health and Knowledge Precinct, with access to purpose-built labs, simulation spaces and professional-grade equipment. Train alongside elite athletes using world-class facilities and benefit from the guidance of both staff and strong industry connections, preparing you for a career that truly changes lives.

*Griffith had more athletes at the 2024 Paris Olympics than any other Australian university.

Queensland's #1 university for law and criminology. (ShanghaiRanking's Global Ranking of Academic Subjects 2026)

Be the lawyer the world needs and prepare to tackle the unique challenges of our modern, high-tech, globalised society. Gain progressive, practical experience and support for your legal career, as well as access to opportunities and networks to shape your professional path. At Griffith, you'll learn the theory of law as a tool for social justice and change.

Highlights of studying the Bachelor of Laws (Honours)
  • Develop in-depth knowledge of legal principles and practices, including connections between law, ethics, Indigenous issues and international perspectives.
  • Learn essential legal skills in negotiation, critical analysis, advocacy and legal writing.
  • Cover a range of topics in crime, contracts, property, corporate law, torts and legal theories.
  • Learn from practicing legal educators, researchers, judges in residence and a range of industry partners.
  • The Bachelor of Laws (Honours) is an AQF Level 8 degree, which means you'll gain advanced skills in research and critical thinking, stronger career recognition and more pathways for further study. 
Practical experience

Griffith Law School welcomes you to the profession from the commencement of your study. Our dedicated community of professionals and alumni open doors to mentoring and industry internships, so you're job-ready sooner.

You'll have access to practical experience from your first year through moots, court visits and industry networking. You'll also have the chance to gain experience in a structured environment, working with real clients and cases through the Griffith Legal Clinic program in areas like family law, criminal advocacy, legal writing, refugee law and many more.

Griffith Innocence Project

Award-winning and unique to Griffith, the Griffith Innocence Project gives you the chance to make a real impact. This practical program teaches you how to identify and address procedural failures in the criminal justice system, while working alongside students, lawyers and academics to help free innocent people imprisoned in Australia.

description:
Unlock discoveries shaping the future of health. Biomedical science helps society through applying new scientific knowledge to medicine and healthcare. In this degree, you'll develop skills and knowledge in clinical and biological sciences, and how to harness them to improve the diagnosis and treatment of disease.

Students who enrol in this degree at Brisbane South (Nathan) will have a science-focused curriculum. If you wish to study at the Gold Coast, you should apply for the Bachelor of Biomedical Science (1094) and will have a health-focused curriculum.

Highlights of studying the Bachelor of Biomedical Science 
  • Be introduced to the fields that underpin biomedical science from your first year.
  • Explore more advanced aspects in your second and third year, including genetics, biochemistry, cell biology, anatomy, physiology, immunology, microbiology, infectious disease, pharmacology and neuroscience.
  • Learn through lab-based training in cutting-edge facilities, with simulated teaching environments and virtual reality technology.
  • With close links to leading clinics and labs, you'll gain first-hand experience with a broad range of placement opportunities.
Learn through multidisciplinary teamwork 

Study alongside students from the full range of clinical health areas, giving you the skills and knowledge you need to thrive in the kind of teams you may work in after you graduate.

A pathway to medicine 

If you intend to apply for postgraduate study in the Doctor of Medicine (5099), this degree provides excellent foundational knowledge to support your application, as well as a solid foundation for a career in biomedical research. This degree also provides opportunities for you to articulate into masters degrees in health and science professions.

Honours 

Honours is available as an additional year of study for students who want to build on their understanding of health and the methods for researching, diagnosing and treating disease.

description:
Gain the skills to become an accredited dietitian and nutritionist, helping individuals and communities improve their health and wellbeing. Study dietetics to become a trusted expert in nutrition, providing evidence-based, personalised care across a variety of roles for people of all ages and health goals.

This degree provides the flexibility to advance your professional practice skills or to complete a dissertation in your final year of study.

Highlights of studying the Bachelor of Nutrition and Dietetics (Honours) 
  • Learn the science behind the body and food, including chemistry, anatomy, physiology and biochemistry.
  • As you progress, you'll dive into advanced studies in nutrition and dietetics.
  • In Australia, all dietitians are nutritionists, but only dietitians can provide medical nutritional therapy to individual patients. Graduates of this degree will hold both qualifications.
  • Join a supportive student community with peer mentors and career advisers to help you succeed.
Gain experience with industry experts  

Learn through experience in state-of-the-art facilities, including a purpose-built teaching kitchen and a nutrition clinic at the Griffith Health Centre. You'll be guided by Accredited Practising Dietitians with strong industry connections and supported throughout your degree, benefiting from Griffith's five-star rated teaching quality*.

Professional placements 

In the final stage of your degree, you'll complete over 20 weeks (100+ days) of full-time professional placements across Queensland and/or interstate. You'll put your skills into practice, build valuable industry connections, and work alongside future doctors, nurses, physiotherapists and other health professionals in advanced simulated clinical settings.

description:
The Brisbane South (Nathan) offering of this program is scheduled to be delivered at the Treasury Building at our Brisbane City campus in 2027. If scheduled opening is delayed, courses may be delivered all or in part at our other Brisbane locations.

Queensland's #1 university for AI research. (ShanghaiRanking's Global Ranking of Academic Subjects, tied position, 2026)

Build your future in a rapidly evolving industry. Develop strong technical expertise in programming, systems, networks, cyber security, data, AI and software development, alongside a major specialisation that prepares you to tackle real challenges and succeed in a wide range of rewarding IT careers.

Information technology remains the foundation of the digital world and AI is transforming both how organisations operate and how IT professionals work. In this degree, you'll develop the core IT skills employers continue to value, while building the confidence to work with intelligent technologies used across modern organisations. You'll learn how to apply technologies like AI as practical tools to improve business outcomes, innovation and decision-making.

Highlights of studying the Bachelor of Information Technology
  • Gain valuable hands-on experience from day one. Learn in purpose-built labs designed to simulate real industry experience, including our virtual and augmented reality, gamification and robotics labs, Cyber Range, Big Data Visualisation Lab and Cisco Networking Lab.
  • Specialise in a major and gain deep, practical skills in high-demand fields.
  • Use AI and automation tools to enhance problem-solving and productivity in real-world scenarios. 
  • Develop the technical judgement to evaluate AI-generated outputs, understand limitations and apply AI appropriately, effectively, responsibly and ethically.
  • Build the communication and collaboration skills that help turn technical expertise into real-world impact.
  • Gain invaluable experience through internships, including opportunities for paid placements. Many projects and placement opportunities reflect how AI is used in industry to deliver smarter, data-driven solutions.
  • Opportunity to develop apps and solutions for real clients through our App Factory.
Industry experience that opens doors

What sets this degree apart is the emphasis on real-world experience. You'll have the chance to work with start-ups, government bodies or major corporations through internships that are often a pathway into long-term employment.

Through our App Factory, you could be paid* to develop apps for clients, gaining valuable insights and industry-ready skills before you graduate. You'll also gain experience applying AI in various contexts, supporting decision-making, improving efficiency and solving complex business challenges. These experiences help you apply your technical knowledge in practical settings and understand how modern IT solutions are developed, tested and delivered for real users.

IT skills for the AI era

Learn how to use AI to support your study and professional practice, including exploring ideas, improving productivity, testing solutions, analysing information and communicating technical work. You'll work with AI as a tool, while developing the technical foundations needed to understand, evaluate and improve technology. This means you won't simply rely on AI, you'll learn how to use it well, with the judgement, responsibility and ethical awareness expected of modern IT professionals.

Learn from experts shaping the future of tech

We have a wide range of industry contacts and partnerships that help you build your professional network. Our Industry Advisory Board includes representatives from highly reputable private and public sector organisations, ensuring our degree remains aligned with evolving industry needs and employer expectations. This also provides opportunities to connect with and learn from experienced industry professionals while developing the AI capabilities that are increasingly required across a broad range of IT roles.

Study alongside world-class researchers who are using digital technologies to shape national outcomes, protect vital cyber infrastructure and solve contemporary IT problems - from using satellite data to detect bushfires, to working with national agencies on cyber security, or applying big data to political forecasting. Their work demonstrates how AI can be applied to solve real problems across industries and their experience, research and expertise directly informs your learning.

Majors
Networks and cyber security

Develop the expertise to design, manage and secure modern networks and digital systems. Learn core networking principles, cloud architecture and secure software development. Build hands-on skills in ethical hacking, digital forensics and enterprise network configuration. You'll explore security best practices, threat detection and system hardening to defend against cyber threats. You'll also consider how AI is used in both cyber defence and cyber threats and how to protect AI-enabled systems. Graduate ready for in-demand roles in cyber security, network engineering and cloud infrastructure.

Software development

Gain the skills to design and build high-quality software solutions across a range of platforms. Learn object-oriented programming, algorithms, and software architecture to develop robust, scalable applications. Explore full-stack web and mobile development using modern frameworks and tools. You'll also dive into interactive environments through game and XR development and apply user-centred design principles to create engaging, effective software. You'll use AI-assisted development tools and explore how intelligent features can be integrated into modern applications. You'll graduate ready to lead in software

Advance your digital expertise with the Master of Information Technology. This degree provides the technical knowledge and practical skills needed to lead in today's fast-moving digital world.

You'll build a strong foundation in system design, project management, and information technology strategy before specialising in your choice of major. Whether you're streamlining complex data, securing networks, or building innovative software, this degree will equip you with the tools to drive transformation across industries.

Highlights of studying the Master of Information Technology
  • Choose from three majors to tailor your study to your career goals.
  • Build key skills in programming, IT planning, systems integration, and digital infrastructure, and learn how to apply them in diverse organisational settings.
  • Learn from expert academics and industry professionals with strong ties to business, government, and emerging tech sectors.
Develop the skills to lead in a digital-first world

This degree prepares you for leadership roles across industries including health, finance, education, logistics, and government. You'll graduate with the skills to manage IT projects, develop software systems, analyse complex data, and implement secure, scalable solutions that meet the needs of modern organisations.

Apply your knowledge in real scenarios

Work on real IT challenges, designing and delivering practical solutions that mirror industry expectations. Build a professional portfolio and gain confidence applying your skills in dynamic digital environments.

Majors

Data Analytics: Turn data into insight and strategy. You'll be equipped with the tools to manage, analyse and visualise large datasets. Learn to apply predictive models and machine learning techniques to solve real problems in areas like business, health, and public services.

Networking and Cyber Security: Design and protect the digital systems organisations rely on. This major covers secure network architecture, cyber defence techniques, cloud systems, and ethical hacking. You'll graduate with practical skills to assess vulnerabilities and defend critical infrastructure.

Software Development: Build the next generation of digital tools and applications. This major focuses on advanced programming, software design, cloud development, and agile project management. Learn to develop scalable solutions for enterprise and consumer environments.

description:
Build your professional skills and gain the supervised experience required to take the next step toward becoming a registered psychologist. The Master of Professional Psychology integrates advanced coursework with an external placement, preparing you to assess, diagnose and support clients using evidence-based psychological practice.

Designed as the fifth year of the 5+1 pathway to general registration as a psychologist, this degree supports eligibility for provisional registration with the Psychology Board of Australia and prepares you to undertake a +1 internship.

Highlights of studying the Master of Professional Psychology
  • Build your skills in ethical practice, psychological assessment, case formulation and therapeutic intervention across diverse client groups and settings.
  • Learn to assess, diagnose and formulate psychological presentations.
  • Build your capability in evidence-based therapies for common and complex mental health conditions.
  • Gain practical experience through supervised placements and simulation-based learning.
  • Strengthen skills in evaluating client outcomes and intervention effectiveness.
  • Complete a postgraduate qualification that supports your pathway to general registration in just one year of full-time study.
Professional placement and practice experience

Complete 300 hours of professional placement across internal and external settings, including supervised clinical environments. These experiences allow you to apply theory in practice, work directly with clients and build confidence in psychological settings. Placements may take place across a range of locations, providing exposure to diverse populations and service contexts.

description:
Queensland's #1 university for marine and ocean engineering. (ShanghaiRanking's Global Ranking of Academic Subjects 2026)

Study environmental science at Griffith and gain the scientific knowledge, practical experience and confidence to tackle some of the most pressing challenges of our time. This degree blends strong scientific foundations with hands-on learning, preparing you for a career where you can make a genuine impact on the environment and society.

Whether your goal is to better understand natural systems or actively protect them, you'll graduate with skills, scientific rigour and informed decision-making expertise in environmental management. At Griffith, you'll learn in a living lab as our campuses are surrounded by bushland, waterways and marine ecosystems, giving you direct exposure to real environmental systems with sustainability and environmental responsibility embedded throughout your studies.

You'll explore environmental challenges from social, physical and biological perspectives, supported by an interdisciplinary curriculum spanning ecology, chemistry, data science, management and policy. Learning takes place well beyond the classroom, with extensive fieldwork, lab activities and immersive field trips in unique natural environments.

Highlights of studying the Bachelor of Environmental Science
  • With more than 50 years' experience training environmental scientists, Griffith understands industry and government needs, ensuring you graduate career-ready.
  • Gain extensive hands-on experience through labs, ecological surveys, data modelling, applied research, field trips and professional placements with government, NGOs and industry partners.
  • Learn the tools and technologies used by industry, aligning your skills with employer expectations and easing the transition into the workforce.
  • Study in living lab environments across our campuses and complete an unforgettable capstone research experience on Heron Island.
  • With supportive lecturers, tailored academic support and strong industry and research connections, you'll feel supported every step of the way as you build the career-ready skills employers value.
  • The degree's accreditation with the Environment Institute of Australia and New Zealand (EIANZ) enhances employability, professional recognition and access to exclusive opportunities.
Build strong foundations and graduate career-ready 

Your degree begins with core science courses before progressing into environmental data analytics, geographical information systems, management and anthropology. In your final year, you'll complete a capstone experience, choosing from a research project, extended fieldwork or an industry placement-allowing you to apply your learning to real environmental problems.

Majors 

Flexible study options mean you can complete a double major and still graduate in three years. Choose from a range of majors to tailor your degree and align your studies with your career goals:

Ecology and Conservation - explore ecosystems, biodiversity and conservation science through practical ecological surveys and monitoring. Available at Gold Coast and Brisbane South (Nathan).

Environmental Chemistry - investigate the chemical processes that shape natural systems and pollutants, with advanced lab and analytical skills. Available at Gold Coast and Brisbane South (Nathan).

Soil and Water Science - study the management of Australia's critical soil and water resources through fieldwork, catchment studies and ecology. Available at Brisbane South (Nathan) only.

Urban and Social Environments - examine the relationship between people, cities and nature, with a focus on sustainability, planning and community engagement. Available at Gold Coast and Brisbane South (Nathan).

Honours 

From the end of your third year, eligible students can transfer into an honours program and complete an independent research project, strengthening pathways into research, leadership roles or further study.

description:
Public health professionals play a critical role in improving population wellbeing, shaping health policy, and responding to complex global health challenges. Griffith's Master of Public Health equips you with the knowledge, analytical skills and practical capabilities to design, deliver and evaluate public health programs that make a real-world impact. 

You'll learn how social conditions, environments and systems shape health - and how to apply this understanding to reduce inequities, prevent disease and improve health outcomes across complex and varied community and policy contexts.

This program is ideal if you're seeking to advance your career in health policy and planning, build population-level expertise to complement clinical or allied health experience, pursue public health roles locally or internationally, or transition into public health from a health or science background. 

Highlights of studying the Master of Public Health 
  • Gain a strong foundation in population health, epidemiology and health policy 
  • Apply analytical and epidemiological skills to plan, implement and evaluate population-based interventions 
  • Analyse population health data to support evidence-based public health decision making 
  • Explore international and global health contexts, including equity, community engagement and human rights 
  • Design and evaluate health promotion and disease prevention programs across diverse settings 
  • Communicate public health evidence effectively to inform practice, policy and stakeholders 
  • Build practical skills through applied assessment tasks, case studies and project-based learning that reflect current public health practice. 
Lead change with purpose 

Griffith is ranked #1 in Australia and #2 globally in the United Nations' Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)*, so as a Master of Public Health graduate you'll be prepared to deliver life-changing outcomes for individuals and communities across Australia and internationally.

description:
The redesigned, fully online Griffith MBA will commence in Trimester 1, 2027, offering a fresh and flexible way to advance your career. If you're ready to start sooner, you can begin your Griffith MBA studies in 2026, available on-campus or online. 

Our MBA is for leaders ready to create meaningful change. It offers a practice rich curriculum to elevate your career and sharpen skills that matter. You'll need to think differently, apply your learning in real-time and make decisions to drive impact. You'll engage with CEOs, industry leaders and innovative organisations in a range of unique projects, stretching your critical leadership skills. 

Co-designed with leading academics and industry experts, the Griffith MBA continues a strong focus on responsible leadership, sustainable business practices and having a global perspective. You'll develop strategic insight and an ethical mindset to lead any organisation through complexity and drive innovation. 

This next generation MBA is delivered online to give ambitious professionals the flexibility to study without compromising their career development. 

Whether you want to be a senior leader, scale your own venture or influence policy and strategy, the Griffith MBA will help you step into the role of a bold, informed and ethical decision-maker. 

Highlights of studying the Griffith MBA 

  • Go global with select students given the opportunity to attend the European Summer School for Advanced Management, hosted at the University of Glasgow, Scotland. 
  • Build networks with optional weekend immersions available from 2027, where you'll be able to connect with peers, engage with industry leaders and attend masterclass-style sessions at Griffith's new Treasury Building location in the Brisbane CBD. 
  • Master effective leadership with insights across strategy, finance, sustainability, innovation and people leadership delivered by globally recognised academics and industry practitioners. 
  • Apply your learning with workplace-focused assessments that can be translated into organisational impact and entrepreneurial growth. 
  • Learn alongside a diverse cohort of professionals from a wide range of industries, enriching your perspectives and strengthening your leadership capability. 
  • Join a lifelong community with MBA for Life graduate-focused events, free mentoring and peer networks for continuous learning. 
  • Finish your degree quicker with the ability to recognise prior learning if you've completed Griffith's Graduate Certificate in Leadership and Business Management. 


Global recognition 

Griffith continues to lead in responsible business education with the world's number one sustainable MBA for six consecutive years*. Our commitment to sustainability, ethical leadership and future-ready business practice is recognised globally, being awarded a Tier 1 status in MBA programs worldwide**. 

Wherever you go, locally or internationally, we'll support you to achieve your goals with relevant, resilient and globally recognised capabilities.

The Brisbane South (Nathan) offering of this program is scheduled to be delivered at the Treasury Building at our Brisbane City campus in 2027. If scheduled opening is delayed, courses may be delivered all or in part at our other Brisbane locations.

Queensland's #1 university for law and criminology. (ShanghaiRanking's Global Ranking of Academic Subjects 2026)

For professionals from non-law backgrounds, this graduate entry law degree provides the chance to build on your existing expertise while developing the legal knowledge and skills to succeed in today's complex, globalised world.

We don't just prepare you to be a lawyer, we'll prepare you to be a leader who can drive change. Whether you're looking to move into a legal role within your current industry, or transition into a new career, Griffith Law School provides the knowledge, skills and connections to make your goals a reality.

Highlights of studying the Bachelor of Laws (Honours) Graduate Entry
  • Develop a deep understanding of core legal principles, from criminal law and contracts to constitutional law and torts.
  • Harness your existing expertise and apply your specialist knowledge to the practice of law, especially in areas like intellectual property and corporate, environmental and healthcare law.
  • Our curriculum connects law to broader societal issues including ethics, Indigenous rights and international perspectives.
  • Learn how to think critically, solve problems and communicate effectively through research, writing, oral advocacy and legal analysis.
  • Benefit from the expertise of practising legal educators, judges in residence and industry leaders who will guide you in shaping your legal career.
  • Even as a full-time student, you may be able to choose from different class times and access lectures online, making it easier to balance study with work and life.
Build connections that matter

Access personalised career development through mentoring, industry internships and networking with leading legal professionals and organisations. Work with real clients and cases through our Griffith Legal Clinics and build connections to fast-track your career.

description:
Make a difference in children's lives and contribute to the future of education. The Master of Primary Teaching offers an exciting pathway to becoming a qualified teacher, focusing on educating children from Prep to Year 6. This program is designed for those who hold a bachelor degree in another field and wish to transition into teaching. 

Highlights of studying the Master of Primary Teaching 
  • Combine theoretical knowledge with practical classroom experience to meet the diverse needs of young learners. 
  • Study foundational topics including childhood development, educational psychology, curriculum design and inclusive teaching practices. 
  • Focus on literacy, numeracy and strategies to foster positive student outcomes. 
  • Complete 60 days of supervised school placements, applying learning in real classrooms with guidance from experienced mentors. 
  • Develop skills to manage diverse classrooms, differentiate teaching, integrate technology and adopt innovative strategies. 
  • This postgraduate pre-service teacher education program is offered in intensive mode to enable completion in one and a half years or over two years full-time. 
Graduate ready to inspire the next generation 

This degree has a strong focus on ethical practice, cultural awareness, and understanding education systems and policies. With demand for qualified teachers continuing to grow, completing a Master of Primary Teaching opens rewarding career opportunities.

description:
The Brisbane South (Nathan) offering of this program is scheduled to be delivered at the Treasury Building at our Brisbane City campus in 2027. If scheduled opening is delayed, courses may be delivered all or in part at our other Brisbane locations.

Queensland's #1 university for AI research. (ShanghaiRanking's Global Ranking of Academic Subjects, tied position, 2026)

Step into one of Australia's fastest-growing and most in-demand fields with a Bachelor of Cyber Security. Master the tools and technologies that protect critical data, systems and networks across business, government and everyday life.

You'll develop a deep understanding of how cyber-attacks occur and how to stop them, through practical training, real-world simulations and industry experience. As AI becomes increasingly embedded in organisations and digital systems, you'll learn how to identify vulnerabilities, protect AI-enabled technologies and defend against emerging AI-driven threats.

Highlights of studying the Bachelor of Cyber Security
  • Train in cutting-edge facilities like our Cyber Range, a dedicated simulated environment where you'll defend against live cyber incidents and test your skills in realistic scenarios.
  • Learn from industry experts who bring cyber security experience from sectors including government, finance and national defence.
  • Build a strong foundation in IT fundamentals including programming, networking, data management and systems administration, before diving into advanced cyber security topics.
  • Explore how AI systems work, where they can fail and how cyber security professionals can protect against malicious use of AI technologies.
  • Complement your technical skills with the communication and leadership capabilities needed to succeed in the workplace.
  • Study with industry experts trusted by top financial institutions, including Westpac, to train their teams in combating financial crime.
  • Build practical experience and professional networks by completing an industry placement or project with leading industry partners. 
Specialised, in-demand cyber expertise  

Study industry-relevant topics like ethical hacking, digital forensics, cryptography, cyber defence, incident response and AI, keeping you at the forefront of emerging technology and global security trends. Developing expertise in these areas is essential to protect organisations from complex, evolving cyber threats and to meet the growing demand for skilled professionals.

Through courses like Trustworthy AI, you'll examine how AI systems and large language models can be exploited, learn how to identify and mitigate these vulnerabilities, and develop practical skills using AI tools for cyber security tasks such as social engineering analysis and information gathering. You'll also learn how AI is increasingly used as a hacking tool and develop the knowledge and skills required to defend systems, data and organisations against AI-enabled attacks.

Immerse yourself in the field before you graduate 

In your final year, you'll gain valuable in-field experience through a professional industry placement or research project, preparing you for a confident transition to the workforce. This may include projects focused on emerging cyber security challenges, including securing AI systems and technologies.

description:
Learn how medicines are developed, tested and used safely to improve lives and protect communities. This degree gives you the scientific expertise to understand how drugs and chemicals interact with the human body. With a strong focus on practical learning and real-world application, this degree prepares you for a career at the intersection of health, science and industry.

Through hands-on lab work and applied projects, you'll build a deep understanding of pharmacology, toxicology and drug development, gaining insight into how safer and more effective treatments reach patients and communities.

Highlights of studying the Bachelor of Pharmacology and Toxicology
  • Gain extensive experience in modern pharmacology, toxicology and analytical laboratories, developing practical skills valued by employers.
  • Learn from experts leading research in drug action, chemical toxicology, precision medicine and pharmaceutical science.
  • Build strong foundations in chemistry, biology, and anatomy before progressing into advanced studies of drug mechanisms, safety and efficacy.
  • Apply your learning to real challenges through project-based courses such as the BioHealth Project, working with industry, government or research partners.
  • Tailor your studies with electives that align with your interests across health, research, regulation or industry. 
Practical learning with real impact 

From your first year, you'll combine core health science courses with lab-based learning to understand how cells, tissues and organ systems respond to medicines and chemicals. As you progress, you'll study drug action, toxic responses, pharmaceutical analysis and specialised delivery systems, gaining experience with industry-standard techniques such as spectroscopy, chromatography and molecular analysis. Courses in evidence-based practice, biostatistics and epidemiology will strengthen your ability to interpret data and support safe and effective medicine use.

In your final years, you'll bring your skills together through applied research, industry-informed projects or an industry placement, building confidence, professional experience and career readiness.

Build a strong foundation for further study

This degree's focus on pharmacology will provide you with an excellent foundation if you're considering a degree in one of these areas:

  • Pharmacy: Bachelor of Pharmacy (Honours) (1614)

Master of Pharmacy (5661)
  • Medicine: Doctor of Medicine (5099)
  • Dentistry: Bachelor of Dental Health Science (1577)
  • Medical Research: Master of Health and Medical Research (5763)
    • Extend your expertise with honours 

    Eligible students can undertake an additional year of study in the Bachelor of Pharmacology and Toxicology (Honours) (2118), completing an independent research project under academic supervision.

description:
The Bachelor of Visual Arts will equip you with the historical, theoretical and practical knowledge to begin a career in the visual arts, either in Australia or internationally. In your first year, you'll undertake introductory courses in painting, sculpture, performance and installation, photography, drawing and contemporary Australian Indigenous art. First-year students may also undertake elective courses such as printmaking or jewellery and small objects.

In your second year, you'll select a major and tailor your studies with electives such as public art, international study tours, museum and gallery internships, or courses from other Griffith degrees. By third year, you'll deepen your expertise in your major while developing essential professional practice skills, including producing a major cross-disciplinary project and showcasing your work in an exhibition.

Majors 

Painting 

Gain a strong foundation in the technical, conceptual and historical aspects of painting as a contemporary art practice. Engage with key developments in modern and postmodern painting, explore interdisciplinary approaches and develop a personal body of work that culminates in the Queensland College of Art and Design (QCAD) Graduate Exhibition, showcasing your creative evolution and studio-based practice.

Sculpture, Performance and Installation 

Explore contemporary art through an interdisciplinary lens, combining elements of sculpture, installation, live performance, video and new media. Emphasising material experimentation, spatial awareness and conceptual development, you'll create ambitious, self-directed works that culminate in a final body of work showcased in the QCAD Graduate Exhibition.

Photography 

Engage critically and creatively with photographic practice through both traditional and experimental approaches. You'll explore themes like the body, materiality and the environment, using analogue, digital and cameraless techniques. You'll develop a unique visual style and create a polished portfolio for the QCAD Graduate Exhibition.

Highlights of studying the Bachelor of Visual Arts 
  • Learn in creative studio spaces at the Queensland College of Art and Design, with access to world-class facilities like galleries and purpose-built visual arts studios. 
  • Learn from and work alongside practising artists and industry experts who are pushing creative boundaries in Australia and around the world. 
  • This inclusive degree embraces individuals who are passionate about creativity and creation. 
  • Flexible study options including varied tutorial times and online access to lectures and course materials make it easier to balance your studies with work and life commitments.
  • Apply via portfolio submission and showcase your creative potential upfront.
Industry and expert connections 

Work on real projects for real clients, build your portfolio and establish critical contacts and networks before you graduate. Our industry partnerships and collaborations unlock unique opportunities like access to on-campus exhibitions, networking events, screenings, guest lectures and much more. Gain industry experience and prepare for your career by: 

  • working with guest artists, curators and arts workers through studio and other courses 
  • undertaking internships in galleries, libraries, events, archives or museums* 
  • producing and participating in exhibitions including our major QCAD Graduate Exhibitions 
  • completing professional industry projects through QCAD's LiveArt courses* 
  • embark on international study tours for course credit (including tours to Europe, the Americas, the Pacific, Indo-Pacific and North, East and Southern Asia). Visit Go Global Griffith to learn more.

*To experience this type of learning, you may need to enrol in specific courses, such as 2009QCA Public Art 1, or 2381QCA Griffith University Art Museum Internship. These courses may be either core or elective to your degree.

description:
The Brisbane South (Nathan) offering of this program is scheduled to be delivered at the Treasury Building at our Brisbane City campus in 2027. If scheduled opening is delayed, courses may be delivered all or in part at our other Brisbane locations.

Queensland's #1 university for AI research. (ShanghaiRanking's Global Ranking of Academic Subjects, tied position, 2026)

The Master of Cyber Security provides you with advanced technical expertise and strategic insight to safeguard critical systems and counter emerging threats across the digital landscape.

Combining core cyber security principles with advanced techniques in management, governance and digital investigations, this postgraduate degree prepares you to assess vulnerabilities, respond to attacks and deliver innovative solutions across business, government and infrastructure sectors.

You'll explore cyber security concepts such as risk mitigation, data privacy protection and governance as you develop skills in cryptographic algorithms, internet protocols and ethical hacking, making you a powerful force in the future of digital defence.

Highlights of studying the Master of Cyber Security
  • Utilise advanced techniques rooted in the MITRE ATT&CK (Adversarial Tactics, Techniques and Common Knowledge) framework to understand, simulate and defend against sophisticated cyber threats.
  • Gain advanced knowledge and practical skills in operating and managing a Cyber Security Operations Centre (CSOC) and responding effectively to cybersecurity incidents with industry-relevant tools, including Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) systems and firewalls.
  • Explore the digital forensic process and gain the advanced skills to uncover and analyse digital evidence across a spectrum of devices and environments.
  • Benefit from an industry-based placement within a commercial or industrial environment.
  • Graduate with a professional portfolio that showcases your ability to lead complex cyber security projects supported by AI solutions.
  • This degree is professionally accredited by the Australian Computer Society.
Be ready for what's next

Prepare for high-demand roles where technology, automation and cyber threats are constantly evolving. You'll graduate ready to protect critical infrastructure, lead security teams and design ethical, AI-enhanced defence strategies.

description:
As global travel continues to expand, organisations need managers who combine strategic business expertise with deep industry insight. This degree equips you with advanced management, leadership and operational skills to lead tourism, hospitality and events organisations in Australia and internationally.

Highlights of studying the Master of International Tourism and Hospitality Management
  • Develop advanced leadership and people management skills as you build expertise in tourism strategy, competitiveness and risk management.
  • Learn revenue management techniques including forecasting, pricing models and demand optimisation.
  • Explore sustainable and regenerative tourism practices that support communities and destinations.
  • Deepen your understanding of tourism product design, innovation and digital technologies.
  • Gain insights into hospitality operations, guest experience design and service excellence.
  • Eligible students may receive credit for approved recognised prior study and/or relevant professional experience, so you may gain a masters in as little as 1 year of full-time study.
Sustainable tourism and leadership in a changing industry

Explore the environmental, social and economic challenges facing global tourism. Courses in sustainable and regenerative tourism examine how destinations, operators and governments can balance visitor demand with community wellbeing and environmental stewardship. description:
Queensland's #1 university for law and criminology. (ShanghaiRanking's Global Ranking of Academic Subjects 2026)

Study the Bachelor of Criminology and Criminal Justice online at your own pace and gain practical, career-focused skills to help prevent crime and shape better justice outcomes. Lead change, promote justice and build a safer society, all on your schedule.  

This flexible, fully online degree is designed to equip you with the insights, tools and industry knowledge to make a real impact in communities and criminal justice systems across Australia. You'll explore the causes and consequences of crime, understand the experiences of victims and offenders, and examine how policing, courts and corrections respond to crime through a social justice lens. You'll also gain hands-on experience through work-integrated learning opportunities and learn from internationally recognised researchers and industry professionals. 

Highlights of studying the Bachelor of Criminology and Criminal Justice 
  • Study 100% online, on demand - designed to fit around your work and life. 
  • Learn from world-renowned experts in fields like policing, domestic violence, youth justice, and cyber crime. Explore major topics including criminal law, homicide, First Nations justice, family violence, and fraud. 
  • Build practical skills in crime prevention, research design, data analysis and policy evaluation. 
  • Examine real issues using insights from psychology, sociology, politics, social work and law. 
  • Participate in work-integrated learning opportunities with justice agencies and community organisations matched to your career aspirations. 
  • Benefit from dedicated academic support and interactive online learning tools to stay engaged and motivated. 
Learning that prepares you to make an impact 

Our strong links with justice organisations mean you'll learn how criminal justice systems really operate - from law enforcement to rehabilitation and prevention. Through hands-on projects, simulations and research activities, you'll develop the skills to critically evaluate evidence, assess policy and recommend change. You'll graduate with the practical and analytical expertise to contribute to safer communities and a fairer justice system. 

Learn from experts driving change in the justice sector 

Our teaching staff are leaders in their fields, bringing current research and front line experience into your virtual classroom. From examining cyber crime trends to improving support for vulnerable populations, Griffith researchers are shaping justice reform at local, national and global levels. Their insights and networks will help you understand the issues that matter and help you confidently step into professional roles that make a real difference. 

This degree is part of Griffith GO, our 100% online, on-demand degrees that let you start when you're ready, study at your own pace and learn from anywhere.

description:
Queensland's #1 university for law and criminology. (ShanghaiRanking's Global Ranking of Academic Subjects 2026)

Step into a career where psychology meets justice. This double degree gives you the tools to understand why people commit crimes and how to help prevent them. You'll study human behaviour, motivation and decision-making alongside the systems and structures that define crime and justice in society. Prepare for a meaningful career creating safer, fairer and more resilient communities.

Highlights of studying the Bachelor of Psychological Science/Bachelor of Criminology and Criminal Justice
  • Learn from industry leaders and renowned academics who advise governments and justice agencies.
  • Explore how thinking, emotion and social influences drive behaviour, from everyday decision-making to criminal acts.
  • Understand global trends in crime control and the latest evidence-based strategies for crime prevention and rehabilitation.
  • Gain insight and experience through industry projects, professional placements and research opportunities.
  • Build practical skills in psychological assessment, data analysis, policy evaluation and offender rehabilitation.
  • Take your learning global with the chance to join exchange programs and international study tours specifically designed to fit the degree's teaching objectives such as 3023CCJ Thailand Study Tour: Sex, Drugs, Violence and Imprisonment. 
A powerful combination of theory and practice 

In psychology, you'll explore cognition, emotion, personality and neuroscience. In criminology, you'll examine criminal behaviour, policing, corrections and social justice. Together, these disciplines will help you develop the analytical, communication and problem-solving skills to work across health, law enforcement and policy settings.

Double your opportunities

By combining two highly regarded degrees, you'll stand out in competitive fields such as policing, intelligence, rehabilitation and social services. Your ability to understand both individuals and systems will be valuable in roles that bridge psychology and justice, from supporting victims and offenders to shaping policy and reform.

description:
Australia's #1 university for nursing and midwifery. (ShanghaiRanking's Global Ranking of Academic Subjects 2026)

Designed for registered nurses, this postgraduate degree builds on your existing experience and provides the expertise needed to take on leadership, education, research and advanced practice roles in healthcare. With a strong focus on research, quality and safety and elevated clinical capability, this degree supports your progression into senior nursing positions.

Highlights of studying the Master of Nursing Science
  • Strengthen your understanding of research inquiry and evidence-informed practice.
  • Build capability in quality and safety within complex healthcare environments.
  • Prepare for advanced clinical practice through coursework focused on collaboration and critical decision-making.
  • Develop the leadership skills to support innovation and improvement across healthcare services.
  • Gain expertise in health education, curriculum design and student assessment.
  • Design, refine and complete a small-scale research project through a structured dissertation pathway with guided academic supervision.
Develop advanced skills for contemporary nursing practice

Deepen your knowledge in areas essential to modern healthcare. Study core courses in research inquiry, transformation and leadership, advanced practice in chronic health conditions and learning and teaching for health professionals. You'll also tailor your research development through options in quantitative and/or qualitative research or clinical trials.

Flexible learning designed for working nurses

This masters degree can be completed fully online or through a blend of online and on-campus learning. Whether you study full-time or part-time, you'll be supported by experienced staff who understand the needs of practising nurses.

Industry and expert connections 

Learn from highly awarded academics with strong professional networks across the health sector. Industry consultation ensures the program remains current, rigorous and aligned with employer expectations. Graduates are also eligible to apply for Higher Degree Research programs.

description:
This degree, offered by the Autism Centre of Excellence, has a multidisciplinary, whole of life focus. In the Masters, you will build on this knowledge and learn about critical issues in autism such as diagnosis, early intervention, mental health, communication and the importance of identifying strengths and challenges. You will gain comprehensive understanding and skills in research and practice for autistic individuals, that will enable you to work effectively with autistic learners and their families at home, in school, at work and in the community.

The Master of Autism Studies is a pathway to becoming a Developmental Educator. Developmental Educators are National Disability Insurance Scheme (NDIS) approved professionals who support individuals on the autism spectrum, those with other disabilities, and their families to achieve their individual developmental, social and learning goals.

This degree also addresses an area of acute need as determined by the Australian Department of Families, Housing, Community Services and Indigenous Affairs, Australian Department of Education, Employment and Workplace Relations, Queensland Department of Education and Training, and the Queensland Department of Communities, Child Safety and Disability Services.

description:
Make a real difference in your community. This degree prepares you to work with individuals, families and communities to help overcome challenges in areas such as health, housing, education, employment, disability or social connection. Use your skills to support and connect people and the resources they need, and work to make systems easier to navigate and more supportive.

Highlights of studying the Bachelor of Human Services 
  • Explore human services in Australia and build a strong foundation in social justice, empowerment and inclusion to help shape a brighter future for those you work with. 
  • Explore courses in human development, communication and counselling, social justice and diversity, ethics and case management. 
  • Learn from specialists tackling issues such as youth mental health, parenting and family support, while gaining hands-on human services experience. 
  • Career advice and support is built into your degree, so you'll graduate job ready. 
Practical experience that sets you apart 

Put your skills into practice through clinical placements in our on-campus clinics or with leading organisations like Queensland Health, Queensland Government, headspace and Lifeline.

Combine classroom learning with hands-on training 

Guided by experienced professionals, you'll complete 52 days of field placement across your second and third years. With opportunities in areas such as child protection, family support, mental health, youth justice, homelessness, domestic violence and disability and the option to take local, rural or international placements, you'll graduate ready to make a real impact.

Majors 

You'll select a major in:

Children, youth and family 

Support the wellbeing of children, young people and families through early intervention, advocacy and integrated service delivery. You'll explore childhood development, family dynamics and youth needs in diverse social and cultural contexts, with a strong focus on safety, equity and care. Courses cover child development, youth services and family violence, equipping you with practical tools to work in early years settings, community programs and family support services. You'll have the opportunity to undertake a supervised field placement, offering practical experience to build your confidence and professional capacity.

Criminal justice 

Explore the structures, practices and challenges within the criminal justice system, with a focus on rehabilitation, crime prevention and justice reform. You'll examine key areas such as corrections, restorative justice and responses to crime in diverse communities, including First Nations peoples. Gain practical experience through a supervised field placement, developing skills for roles in policy, community safety, youth justice or offender rehabilitation. With courses covering crime prevention strategies, lived experiences of justice and alternatives to traditional punishment, you'll be well-positioned to make a difference to how justice is delivered and experienced in society.

Disability, wellbeing and ageing 

Explore how individuals experience disability, ageing and mental health, with a strong focus on dignity, rights and inclusion. You'll examine contemporary approaches to disability practice, positive ageing and mental wellbeing, learning from both lived experiences and critical perspectives. Through a supervised field placement, you'll build the skills needed to work across diverse support settings, from aged care and disability services to mental health and community programs.

Policy, advocacy and research 

Prepare to drive social change by influencing policy, shaping services and advocating for equity and justice. Gain foundational knowledge in welfare systems, government and legislation, alongside practical research and data analysis skills. With a focus on leadership, advocacy, and critical thinking, you'll explore how to design evidence-informed interventions and influence decision-making at local and national levels. A supervised field placement allows you to apply your learning in policy and community settings.

Honours

The Bachelor of Human Services (Honours) (2092) is available through an additional year of study.

description:
The Bachelor of Animation is the ideal launching pad for you to play a significant role in the animation and visual effects industries in Australia and abroad. Animation at Griffith is ranked #1 in Queensland and 2nd in Australia and New Zealand*.

Highlights of studying the Bachelor of Animation
  • Bring your ideas to life by creating your own animations from concept to final render, using premium industry-recognised software and hardware.
  • Get hands-on experience in animation production, with opportunities to work on projects for real clients through LiveLab, our commercial multimedia studio.
  • Showcase your work at festivals, grow your portfolio, and start building industry connections that can open doors.
  • Boost your career prospects with study tours overseas, work placements and internships within our embedded animation studio model.
  • Collaborate with filmmakers and game designers, artists, illustrators and musicians from Griffith's Queensland College of Art and Design and the Queensland Conservatorium.
Industry links and global connections
  • Learn within a degree recognised as a Toon Boom Centre of Excellence and supported by global networks like CILECT, ASPERA and ATOM.
  • Benefit from international partnerships with APSA, NEP Group, BFA, World Congress of Science and Factual Producers and Gobelins School of Paris.
  • Gain experience through work placements, internships, mentorships and real projects with companies such as Ludo (Bluey), Pixel Zoo, AltVFX and Liquid Animation Studios.
  • Access exclusive masterclasses and guest lectures from leading experts including Disney, Lucasfilm, Marco Sinigaglia, character performance specialist Myrna Gawryn, WETA NZ and Gobelins Paris.
  • Build industry-ready skills and critical global contacts to launch a career in animation and related fields.

*Animation Career Review 2026

Majors

Art direction: Learn advanced techniques in conceptualisation, visual storytelling and art direction principles for impactful characters and story-worlds across animation, games and screen media.

Character animation: Learn advanced animation techniques, including character rigging, keyframe animation and motion capture integration for compelling character performances across various media and platforms.

Post-production: Acquire proficiency in post-production through creative application of advanced compositing techniques and green screen concepts, as well as mastering compositing workflows, colour correction and node-based compositing tools.

Virtual production and VFX: Discover how to create content with virtual production and its innovative methods including motion capture, LED wall technology, photogrammetry, camera tracking and virtual lighting through real-time game engines.

3D art and environments: Learn to interpret visual concepts and artistic styles to create appealing 3D characters, props, vehicles and environments for games, film and animation.

Writing and development: Write and develop ideas for any screen medium - from linear screenplays to narrative design. You'll also gain insights into global screen industry landscapes and audiences.
