Make a difference as a sustainability-driven professional. This double degree prepares you to respond to some of the biggest challenges facing organisations today including climate change, resource management and the growing demand for ethical and sustainable operations. By combining environmental science with business expertise, you'll make a real impact through sustainability and environmental problem-solving, graduating with practical skills valued across industry, government and research.

Highlights of studying the Bachelor of Environmental Science/Bachelor of Business
  • Gain a strong scientific foundation in areas like ecology, climate science, environmental chemistry and sustainable resource management while building essential business skills in analytics, strategy, communication and leadership.
  • Study in living laboratories where nature is your classroom, exploring how environmental decisions influence business success.
  • Learn through extensive fieldwork, hands-on labs, data analysis and real case studies.
  • Specialise by choosing from impactful majors in both environmental science and business, with flexible study paths that allow you to tailor your degree to your interests and career goals.
  • Learn the tools you'll use in your career by working alongside industry and government through placements, research projects, ecological surveys, the Industry Affiliates Program and initiatives like Griffith's Student-Managed Investment Fund and Tax Clinic.
  • Build strong professional networks through industry and research connections with environmental professionals, business consultants, policy specialists, NGOs and industry leaders via guest speakers, networking events and BusinessPLUS workshops.
  • Feel supported every step of the way with tailored academic support, approachable lecturers and modern facilities.
Build expertise in both environmental science and business

Your environmental science studies begin with core scientific courses before progressing into areas such as GIS, environmental data analytics, land management, biodiversity, water resources and climate change. You'll learn through practical experiences, including field trips, ecological monitoring, lab sessions, environmental modelling and professional placements. With 50 years of experience in training environmental scientists, Griffith ensures you graduate industry-ready.

In your business studies, you'll develop a clear understanding of how organisations operate and how sustainability influences strategy, risk and performance. You'll explore fields such as marketing, logistics, human resources, innovation, analytics or international business, with the chance to complement your skills through internships, consulting projects and global mobility opportunities.

description:
The Master of Clinical Dentistry is for qualified dentists aiming to enhance their clinical competencies in advanced general practice treatments.

Highlights of studying the Master of Clinical Dentistry
  • Three specialised majors - Implant Dentistry, Oral Surgery and Prosthodontics - provide a comprehensive curriculum that integrates academic learning with extensive clinical experience.
  • Combine seminars, journal clubs, supervised clinical practice, and a research project and immediately apply enhanced skills in practice.
  • As a graduate you'll be prepared to undertake advanced procedures within general practice, contributing to improved patient outcomes and advancing your career.
Majors
Implant Dentistry

Build advanced expertise in dental implantology, from diagnosis and treatment planning to surgical placement and restoration of dental implants for the replacement of missing teeth and the rehabilitation of oral function and aesthetics.

You'll explore the biological principles of osseointegration while developing hands-on skills in implant surgery and prosthodontics, including single implants, fixed prostheses and overdentures. With a focus on digital workflows such as CBCT imaging, guided surgery and CAD/CAM technologies, you'll learn to deliver precise, evidence-based and patient-centred implant care, including the management of complications and long-term maintenance of implant therapy.

Through a combination of theoretical instruction, simulation, and supervised clinical experience, you'll gain the competence to deliver safe, predictable and patient-centred implant treatment in modern clinical practice.

Oral Surgery

Advance your clinical capability in minor oral surgery and dentoalveolar procedures within a structured, practice-focused environment. You'll strengthen your skills in complex tooth extractions, preprosthetic surgery and the management of oral pathology, with an emphasis on patient safety and clinical decision-making.

Designed to bridge the gap between general dentistry and specialist training, you'll be equipped to confidently manage surgical cases and broaden your scope of practice.

Prosthodontics

Develop the skills to restore function and aesthetics through comprehensive prosthodontic care. Through theoretical learning and supervised clinical training, you'll gain experience in fixed and removable prosthodontics, including crowns, bridges, dentures and implant-supported prostheses, as well as full mouth rehabilitation for complex cases.

With a strong focus on occlusal management, treatment planning and digital technologies such as CAD/CAM and digital impressions, you'll graduate ready to deliver high-quality, patient-centred restorative outcomes in modern dental practice.

Implant Dentistry

Build advanced expertise in dental implantology, from diagnosis and treatment planning to surgical placement and restoration of dental implants for the replacement of missing teeth and the rehabilitation of oral function and aesthetics.

You'll explore the biological principles of osseointegration while developing hands-on skills in implant surgery and prosthodontics, including single implants, fixed prostheses and overdentures. With a focus on digital workflows such as CBCT imaging, guided surgery and CAD/CAM technologies, you'll learn to deliver precise, evidence-based and patient-centred implant care, including the management of complications and long-term maintenance of implant therapy.

Through a combination of theoretical instruction, simulation, and supervised clinical experience, you'll gain the competence to deliver safe, predictable and patient-centred implant treatment in modern clinical practice.

Oral Surgery

Advance your clinical capability in minor oral surgery and dentoalveolar procedures within a structured, practice-focused environment. You'll strengthen your skills in complex tooth extractions, preprosthetic surgery and the management of oral pathology, with an emphasis on patient safety and clinical decision-making.

Designed to bridge the gap between general dentistry and specialist training, you'll be equipped to confidently manage surgical cases and broaden your scope of practice.

Prosthodontics

Develop the skills to restore function and aesthetics through comprehensive prosthodontic care. Through theoretical learning and supervised clinical training, you'll gain experience in fixed and removable prosthodontics, including crowns, bridges, dentures and implant-supported prostheses, as well as full mouth rehabilitation for complex cases.

With a strong focus on occlusal management, treatment planning and digital technologies such as CAD/CAM and digital impressions, you'll graduate ready to deliver high-quality, patient-centred restorative outcomes in modern dental practice.

description:
Queensland's #1 university for law and criminology. (ShanghaiRanking's Global Ranking of Academic Subjects 2026)

Learn from global experts to advance your expertise in criminology and criminal justice. This masters degree is designed for current and aspiring professionals, and will equip you with advanced knowledge of crime, justice systems and evidence-based reform.

Highlights of studying the Master of Criminology and Criminal Justice
  • Explore criminology theory, emerging trends and innovative crime prevention strategies, while building analytical and research skills to address complex criminal justice challenges.
  • Choose quantitative or qualitative research training to strengthen your data analysis and evaluation capabilities.
  • Examine contemporary issues including cyber fraud, transnational organised crime and intelligence-led policing.
  • Build specialist expertise in areas such as forensic mental health, developmental crime prevention and correctional interventions.
  • Customise your degree to align with your career goals across law enforcement, policy, community services or research.
  • Gain practical experience through a community internship or applied research project.
Advanced skills for complex criminal justice environments

Deepen your understanding of how crime is defined, measured and prevented. Core courses in applied criminology theory, research and evaluation methods give you the tools to design rigorous studies, assess programs and translate evidence into effective policy and practice. You'll learn to critically examine the relationship between research, politics and public debate, to give you the confidence to contribute to reform discussions with informed opinions.

Elective options allow you to specialise in areas such as mental disorder and crime, forensic mental health interventions, developmental prevention, organised crime and cyber-enabled fraud. Through applied projects and collaborative problem-solving tasks, you'll strengthen your capacity to lead initiatives, advise senior decision-makers and deliver meaningful outcomes.

Real-world experience and professional growth

Take your learning beyond the classroom with community-based internships aligned to the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals or applied research addressing real criminal justice challenges. These experiences will broaden your professional network, grow your leadership capability and prepare you for senior roles.

description:
If you're motivated to contribute to a more sustainable future, this postgraduate degree can help you build the expertise to engage with environmental decision-making. You'll tackle complex sustainability challenges, contribute to policy and guide organisations toward responsible environmental practice.

Highlights of studying the Master of Environment 
  • Learn from academics and industry experts across climate adaptation, environmental planning, business sustainability and conservation practice.
  • Build advanced skills in environmental economics, pollution assessment, water resource management and environmental systems.
  • Work on practical projects that deepen your capacity to evaluate environmental impacts and design sustainable solutions.
  • Gain strong research capability through dedicated training in research design, data analysis and critical inquiry.
  • Tailor your study with a major and develop the ability to lead cross-disciplinary teams and support organisational change toward sustainability.
  • Gain credit for approved recognised prior study and/or work experience.
Deep expertise in sustainability and environmental management 

Learn how the environment, society and economy interact and how these relationships drive contemporary environmental issues. You'll explore the science behind pollutants, understand environmental risk and develop the tools needed to manage natural resources responsibly. Courses in environmental management systems and environmental and water economics give you the ability to design strategies that balance regulatory requirements with sustainable outcomes.

Solve complex challenges through research and applied learning 

Whether you're advancing your current career or pivoting into the sustainability sector, you'll strengthen your analytical and problem-solving skills through research training and real industry challenges. If you're interested in further study, you'll have the opportunity to complete a dissertation to support a pathway into doctoral research.

Majors

Climate Change Adaptation: Learn how to prepare communities, cities and ecosystems for a changing climate through practical, science-based strategies. Build skills in disaster management, urban resilience, public health and adaptation planning to create safer, more sustainable futures.

Environmental Policy and Planning - Brisbane South (Nathan): Shape how communities respond to environmental challenges by learning how policies are created, evaluated and put into action. Develop skills in climate-focused planning, community engagement and rights-based decision-making to drive sustainable outcomes.

Environmental Protection: Gain the expertise to safeguard ecosystems and manage environmental risks through practical knowledge in water, soil, waste and food systems. Learn to assess, remediate and manage natural and human-made hazards to support sustainable environmental outcomes.

Sustainable Business: Develop the skills to drive sustainability initiatives in organisations, integrating systems thinking, leadership and strategic decision-making. Learn to lead policy and organisational change that balances business goals with environmental and social responsibility.

If studying at Brisbane South campus, some subjects in the Environmental Policy and Planning and in the Sustainable Business majors will be taught at the Brisbane City campus.

As financial services become increasingly data-driven and digitally enabled, this masters degree builds your advanced technical, analytical and financial expertise, enabling you to succeed in fintech, banking, investment and beyond.

Designed for graduates from finance and IT backgrounds, you'll build on your knowledge of financial markets and increase your skills in programming, data analytics and emerging technologies such as AI, blockchain and cybersecurity.

  • Offered entirely online, with options to study full-time or part-time, with access to an active online community for support and collaboration.
  • The BusinessPLUS program is open to every Griffith Business School student. Get involved in events, meet professionals and start building your career network from day one.
  • Gain hands-on experience through internships like the six-week Global Asia Business Internship or join our Co-Design Incubator to solve real challenges in a team.
  • Love travel? With 120+ exchange partners in 70+ countries, you can take your studies overseas and experience business on a global scale.
Build connections from day one 

As part of your degree, you can take on a work-integrated learning course that lets you apply what you've learned in real-world settings and kickstart your career. With over 150 industry partners, Griffith Business School connects you to valuable opportunities and networks. Plus, through clubs, societies and other experiences, you'll grow your skills, boost your employability and make lasting connections.

Hands-on experience with real impact 

Step into Queensland's first student-managed investment fund, managing over $500,000 of investments in socially responsible, ASX-listed companies, where profits support Griffith student scholarships. You'll also have the chance to contribute to the Griffith Tax Clinic as a student advisor, working on real cases, building career-relevant skills and earning credit towards your degree.

Queensland's #1 university for law and criminology. (ShanghaiRanking's Global Ranking of Academic Subjects 2026)

Explore society, culture and justice while building a career in law. You'll engage with complex legal and social scenarios while preparing for diverse professional opportunities. This double degree equips you with the skills to practice law at a high level and the critical thinking, communication and cultural awareness that comes from a humanities education.

Highlights of studying the Bachelor of Laws (Honours)/Bachelor of Arts
  • Build a strong foundation in law, covering legal principles, ethics, advocacy, dispute resolution and research skills.
  • Gain practical experience through moots, court visits, the Griffith Legal Clinic program and the award-winning Griffith Innocence Project.

With our strong industry connections, you'll learn from practising legal educators, judges in residence, journalists, content creators and arts experts, giving you both theoretical insight and hands-on experience.

Develop the strategic and creative skills to thrive in a competitive marketing environment. In our online and on demand Bachelor of Business in Marketing, you'll explore new ways of thinking, designed for the next generation of marketing professionals. Blending creative strategy with data-driven decision making, this 100% online degree will equip you with the skills, values and knowledge you need for a career in marketing.

  • Build a strong foundation in essential business skills and strategies with a focus on sustainability, inclusion and equity.

description:
The Diploma of Engineering is a pathway program designed to help you transition into the Bachelor of Engineering (Honours). You'll develop foundational knowledge and skills in a supportive learning environment, setting you up for success in your future studies.

This is your chance to have an impact on the way the world works. You could have the opportunity to make your mark on major global systems and infrastructure or be at the forefront of localised urban projects. When you choose this degree, you'll be engineering from day one.

We're strong believers in `learning by doing', so this degree has a strong practical focus. You'll learn from teachers who are passionate about engineering and the difference it makes in the world, so you'll get to experience their energy in your studies.

You'll study academic foundations courses to develop a strong foundation in basic science and engineering principles, with additional support and access to a dedicated First Year Coordinator and (PASS) run by high-achieving students.

Industry and expert connections

We have a wide range of industry contacts and partnerships that help you build your professional network. Our Industry Advisory Board ensures that our degree is focused on what employers are looking for and provides opportunities to meet and learn from industry-leading professionals.

You'll also hear from the very best, with guest lecturers explaining their vision and the results of significant projects. You'll have direct access to them for questions and advice as part of our smaller more personalised experience.

If you continue on this pathway into the bachelor degree, you will have the chance to participate in hands-on learning opportunities, taking your skills to work with one of our industry partners here or overseas, undertaking a trimester-long project through our capstone Industry Affiliates Program.

description:
Develop advanced clinical skills for endorsement in clinical psychology. Designed for registered psychologists, this degree combines evidence-based coursework with extensive supervised practice to prepare you for complex clinical environments and diverse client needs.

Developed in consultation with industry, the program builds advanced capability in psychological assessment, case formulation and therapeutic intervention. You'll deepen your expertise across lifespan psychopathology, neuropsychology, health and disability, while strengthening your professional identity through ethical, reflective and client-centred practice.

Highlights of studying the Master of Clinical Psychology Practice
  • Build advanced clinical skills in psychological assessment, diagnosis and case conceptualisation.
  • Develop expertise in evidence-based therapies for complex mental health presentations.
  • Gain extensive supervised experience through clinical placements.
  • Learn from experienced, accredited clinical psychologists in real-world settings.
Extensive clinical experience and supervised practice

You'll complete 750 hours of supervised clinical practice across a range of settings, working directly with clients while receiving guidance from experienced clinicians. These placements allow you to apply advanced theory in practice, refine your therapeutic approach and build confidence in delivering high-quality psychological care.

Prepare for clinical endorsement and advanced practice

This program supports entry into the registrar program for endorsement in clinical psychology with the Psychology Board of Australia. Completion of this degree also meets the requirements for associate membership of the Australian Psychological Society's College of Clinical Psychologists.

You must have and maintain general registration as a Psychologist with the Psychology Board of Australia via the Australian Health Practitioner Regulation Agency (Ahpra) for the duration of the program.

description:
Designed for experienced health professionals and managers, the Master of Advanced Health Services Management builds high-level expertise in healthcare leadership, governance and system reform across health, aged and community care sectors.

If you're ready to move beyond operational management into senior and executive roles, this advanced degree provides the strategic, financial and policy capability required to lead complex health services in Australia and globally.

Highlights of studying the Master of Advanced Health Services Management
  • Build high-level capability in health services management, leadership and strategic decision making.
  • Examine contemporary challenges in healthcare management while strengthening your ability to influence performance, accountability and long-term sustainability.
  • Develop expertise in healthcare finance, budgeting and resource allocation.
  • Apply health economics to support value-based care and measurable service improvement.
  • Explore digital health, information systems and technology-enabled models of care.
  • Choose your study pathway (electives, dissertation or work-based learning) and develop your research capability to support progression to PhD study.
Prepare for senior health leadership

The advanced structure of this degree includes dedicated foundation studies in applied ethics and law, health system design, health services and information systems, and risk management in healthcare. Combined with courses in leadership, change management and strategic decision making in health, you'll gain a deep understanding of the policy environments, governance structures and performance frameworks that underpin healthcare systems. You'll be positioned to guide organisations through reform, workforce challenges and increasing service demand.

Research, industry or specialist focus

Tailor your degree to align with your professional goals. Select from a range of electives or undertake a substantial dissertation to build advanced research capability. You may also complete a structured work-based learning experience, translating theory into practice within a health service organisation.

Unlock the ability to understand human behaviour while mastering the law. This double degree equips you with the skills to analyse legal issues through the lens of psychology, giving you insight into what drives human decisions, actions and social systems.

Ideal if you want to make a meaningful impact in areas such as social justice, mental health advocacy, policy reform and legal practice, this degree prepares you for a wide range of careers that require both legal expertise and a deep understanding of people.

Highlights of studying the Bachelor of Laws (Honours)/Bachelor of Psychological Science
  • Learn from passionate teaching experts who bring contemporary legal reforms, case studies and research insights into the classroom.
  • Griffith Law School provides a professional legal curriculum covering ethics, legal theory, Indigenous issues and international perspectives.
  • Apply psychological theories to topics such as cognition, motivation, stress, health, criminal behaviour and group dynamics.
  • Develop key interpersonal, communication and counselling skills alongside core areas of psychological science.
Industry and practical experience 

From your first year, you'll gain hands-on experience through moots, court visits, research projects and structured industry placements. The Griffith Legal Clinic program allows you to work on real cases, developing skills in advocacy, legal writing and client engagement, while Griffith's psychology research opportunities give you practical experience in data collection, analysis and behavioural studies.

description:
Gain tools for mental health practice and help people achieve their goals. 

This postgraduate program provides mental health practitioners and case managers in diverse practice roles with the skills and knowledge to effectively manage programs that support their clients to achieve personal and system goals, as well as work more effectively with people with injury, disability, mental illness, and their significant others.  

This includes a wide range of human service and rehabilitation programs supporting diverse populations with complex needs, assisting clients to obtain and maintain employment and supporting people from diverse backgrounds with injury, disability or mental illness to find new ways to lead fulfilling and satisfying lives. 

You will be introduced to the values, theories, frameworks, principles and skills of person-centred planning, case management, and communication skills, and therefore become more efficient at determining individual need and planning, coordinating and procuring a range of appropriate services and supports to promote the goals of diverse clients. You'll also gain an understanding of mental illness, epidemiology and relevant theoretical frameworks, which is vital for informing quality mental health practice.  

Industry and expert connections  

Within this degree, you will engage with a multidisciplinary cohort of fellow students in this degree in a flexible online learning environment, where you will be exposed to a range of perspectives and have the opportunity to make new professional connections, while under the tutelage of our experienced academic staff.  

Flexibility

Study anytime, anywhere - This degree is available online through our Digital campus, giving you more room to fit university with your work and social life.

Pursue further study

The courses in this graduate certificate may be credited towards a related graduate diploma or masters degree. Griffith's innovative Credit Precedent Database allows you to find out what credit decisions have been made in the past, which will give you an idea of what you can expect.

Whether you're changing careers or expanding your business expertise, this degree will develop the technical, analytical and strategic skills needed to succeed in modern accounting and finance roles.

Designed for graduates from non-accounting backgrounds who want to build the knowledge and qualifications required to work as a professional accountant, this degree meets the academic requirements for Associate membership with CPA Australia and entry into the CPA Program, as well as the Chartered Accountants Australia and New Zealand (CA ANZ) Chartered Accountants Program, helping you take the next step toward professional accreditation.

Highlights of studying the Master of Professional Accounting
  • Gain a strong understanding of accounting principles, financial reporting, taxation and business law while developing the ability to analyse financial information and support informed business decision-making.
  • Develop skills in financial analysis, business analytics and quantitative tools used in modern accounting practice.
  • Strengthen your ability to interpret financial statements and evaluate business performance.
  • Gain strategic insight through courses in management accounting and organisational strategy.
Flexible entry for career changers

This degree includes a foundation component (Graduate Certificate in Commerce), allowing students without an accounting background to transition into the discipline.

Eligible students may receive credit for approved recognised prior study and/or relevant professional experience, so you may gain a masters in as little as 1 year of full-time study.

description:
The Brisbane South (Nathan) offering of this program is scheduled to be delivered at the Treasury Building at our Brisbane City campus in 2027. If scheduled opening is delayed, courses may be delivered all or in part at our other Brisbane locations.

Gain a competitive edge with the Bachelor of Advanced Commerce (Honours), designed for ambitious students who want to excel in the world of accounting, finance and economics. This degree grounds you in core commercial concepts then takes you further, building advanced analytical, technical and professional skills that employers demand.

We're part of the top 1% of universities worldwide who are accredited by both the International Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business (AACSB) and the European Foundation for Management Development Quality Improvement System (EQUIS). Griffith also holds a five-star rating for learning resources in accounting, business and management*.

Highlights of studying the Bachelor of Advanced Commerce (Honours)
  • Deepen your expertise through an honours research project that builds advanced analytical and investigative skills.
  • Gain skills in accounting, economics, finance, business statistics and modelling to excel in modern commercial environments.
  • Study your way with flexible options including fully online, on campus or hybrid learning.
  • Build valuable networks through our connections with more than 150 industry partners and exclusive programs like BusinessPLUS.
  • Expand your global outlook with access to more than 120 international exchange partners across 70+ countries.
Hands-on learning and advanced expertise

Learn from industry professionals and access practical insights that prepare you for real business challenges. In your honours year, you'll focus on a specialised area or industry of interest and undertake a research project guided by experts. This experience strengthens your ability to analyse data, evaluate evidence and present clear recommendations to stakeholders. With a strong focus on financial analytics and modelling, this degree will give you a competitive edge for roles in both the public and private sectors, where sound judgement and quantitative skills are essential.

*Good Universities Guide 2026

Majors

You can select from a variety of majors to tailor your education to your career aspirations:

Economics: Gain the skills to analyse real-world economic issues using both theory and data. You'll learn to evaluate policies and business decisions with tools like cost-benefit analysis, macroeconomic and microeconomic models, and econometric techniques. You'll be ready to apply these skills to global economic challenges, from open economy dynamics to empirical research projects.

Accounting: Learn how to analyse, interpret and report financial information for organisations across industries. You'll gain practical skills in managerial accounting, auditing, taxation, sustainability reporting and financial statement preparation, while learning to apply theory to real business decisions. You'll be equipped to support strategic planning, ensure compliance and provide insights that drive effective financial management.

Finance: Gain an understanding of how to analyse, manage and optimise investments in a global financial environment. You'll learn to evaluate derivatives, construct and manage investment portfolios, and assess global markets, while applying sustainable finance principles to make responsible financial decisions. Graduates are equipped to pursue careers in investment analysis, portfolio management, financial risk management and sustainable finance roles.

Financial Planning: Learn how to provide expert advice on personal finances, investments, superannuation and retirement planning. You'll develop practical skills in risk management, insurance, taxation and estate planning, preparing you to create tailored financial strategies for clients. You'll be ready for careers as a financial planner, wealth adviser or retirement and estate planning specialist.

Financial Crime Investigation and Compliance: Gain the skills to prevent, detect, and investigate financial crime across organisations and institutions. You'll gain expertise in forensic accounting, fraud and cybercrime, data analysis and visualisation, and environmental criminology to understand how crime occurs and how to stop it. You'll be prepared to work in financial crime investigation, compliance, fraud prevention or risk management within banks, government agencies and corporate organisations.

description:
Lead meaningful change across government, business and the not-for-profit sector. Increasingly complex global challenges require governments and organisations to seek out leaders with a combination of policy expertise, strategic thinking and ethical leadership. Designed for professionals wanting to influence decision-making and drive better outcomes, this masters degree equips you with the skills to design, implement and evaluate policy in complex environments.

Highlights of studying the Master of Public Policy and Leadership
  • Build advanced skills in policy analysis, development and evaluation.
  • Develop leadership capability for public, private and not-for-profit sectors.
  • Learn to influence decision-making through evidence, argument and persuasion.
  • Explore public participation, human rights and global policy contexts.
  • Strengthen expertise in ethics, governance and responsible leadership.
  • Eligible students may receive credit for approved recognised prior study and/or relevant professional experience, so you could gain a masters in as little as 1 year of full-time study.
Develop policy expertise and leadership capability

Build upon foundations in policymaking, research design and policy evaluation. Learn how to translate complex data into clear, actionable insights. Courses focus on real leadership challenges, helping you build the confidence to contribute to policy development at local, national and international levels.

Majors

With a choice of majors, you can tailor your learning to align with your career goals.

Administration and Management: Develop practical leadership and management skills for public sector and organisational contexts. Focus on accountability, financial oversight and values-based leadership to effectively manage teams, resources and performance.

Analysis, Policy Design and Impact: Build strong analytical capability to design, implement and evaluate policy. Learn quantitative methods, data analysis and performance measurement to deliver effective, evidence-based policy outcomes.

Integrity and Regulation: Examine governance, regulation and ethical practice in complex environments. Develop expertise in anti-corruption, compliance and regulatory frameworks.

Strategy and Change: Learn to lead transformation in complex systems. Develop skills in project management, organisational change, sustainability and strategic leadership to drive innovation and long-term impact.

description:
Queensland's #1 university for AI research. (ShanghaiRanking's Global Ranking of Academic Subjects, tied position, 2026)

Kickstart your scientific research journey and open doors to impactful careers. This degree is designed for high-achieving students ready to immerse themselves in science and research from the outset. This degree offers an enhanced, research-intensive experience that allows you to develop advanced scientific skills early, while shaping a study path aligned to your interests and career goals.

You'll learn through hands-on science in modern facilities and unique natural environments, supported by smaller class sizes, peer networks and approachable academics.

Highlights of studying the Bachelor of Advanced Science (Honours)
  • Develop advanced critical thinking, analytical and problem-solving skills, and learn to communicate research effectively to diverse audiences - capabilities highly valued by employers.
  • Begin your research journey early, with advanced studies courses in second and third year that build practical laboratory, fieldwork and data analysis skills.
  • Shape your degree your way by choosing both a major and an honours specialisation, supported by flexible electives.
  • Study science where nature is your classroom, with living laboratory campuses that provide access to bushland, waterways and marine ecosystems.
  • Gain hands-on experience through research projects, building strong technical capability and confidence from day one.
  • Prepare for PhD-level research and advanced scientific careers, with a strong foundation for leadership in academia, research institutes and industry.
  • Benefit from accessible campus locations, world-class facilities and intakes across trimesters 1, 2 and 3, allowing you to start when it suits you.
Build your network 

Through research projects, industry-aligned learning and expert supervision, you'll work alongside world-class scientists on cutting-edge research. Our strong industry and research connections open doors to networking, volunteering and real-world experience, strengthening your professional network and boosting employability.

Develop expertise and launch your career in science

In your final year, you'll complete an honours research project in your chosen specialisation, working closely with leading academics who will mentor you throughout the process. This capstone experience allows you to apply advanced research skills to a significant scientific problem, refine your expertise and demonstrate your capabilities, providing a strong platform for research-focused careers or further study.

The Bachelor of Advanced Science (Honours) equips you with the knowledge, experience and professional confidence to excel as a researcher or scientific leader, preparing you for careers in Australia and internationally.

Majors

Applied Mathematics - Available at Gold Coast and Brisbane South (Nathan) - Turn numbers into real solutions, from modelling natural systems to tackling engineering challenges, with skills that lead to careers in tech, science, data and beyond.

Archaeology - Available at Brisbane South (Nathan) - Uncover humanity's past through artefacts, landscapes and science, gaining hands-on experience that prepares you for careers in research, heritage and cultural analysis.

Biochemistry - Available at Gold Coast - Examine biomolecular structure, metabolism, cellular function and clinical processes while building practical laboratory skills through advanced biotechniques and organic chemistry.

Biochemistry and Molecular Biology - Available at Brisbane South (Nathan) - Explore the molecules of life, from genes to proteins, through lab-based learning that equips you for breakthroughs in health, agriculture and environmental science.

Chemistry - Available at Gold Coast and Brisbane South (Nathan) - Study the building blocks of matter with hands-on lab experience in organic, inorganic, physical and analytical chemistry, opening doors to pharmaceuticals, forensics and sustainability.

Clinical Sciences - Available at Brisbane South (Nathan) - Gain in-depth knowledge of the human body and disease with lab and anatomy experience, preparing you for health, research or postgraduate study.

Ecology - Available at Gold Coast and Brisbane South (Nathan) - Discover how species and ecosystems interact through fieldwork, lab studies and conservation practice, leading to careers in environmental management, research and consultancy.

Geography* - Available at Gold Coast and Brisbane South (Nathan) - Examine the links between people, place and planet, tackling global challenges with GIS, policy and fieldwork skills for careers in planning, sustainability and climate resilience.

Marine Biology - Available at Gold Coast - Dive into ocean science with hands-on fieldwork and lab studies on reefs, coasts and marine life, preparing you for roles in conservation, research and environmental management.

Microbiology - Available at Brisbane South (Nathan) - Explore the unseen world of microbes and their roles in health, ecosystems and industry, gaining lab and genomic skills for careers in biotechnology, medicine and research.

Physics - Available at Gold Coast and Brisbane South (Nathan) - Study the laws of matter, motion and energy with experiments and advanced topics in quantum and nuclear physics, opening pathways to science, tech and engineering careers.

*If studying at Brisbane South campus, some subjects in the Geography major will be taught at the Brisbane City

Highlights of studying the Master of Infection Prevention and Control
  • Learn from leading experts across Australia and internationally who contribute to policy, research and frontline infection prevention and control practice.
  • Explore global challenges including antimicrobial resistance, emerging infectious diseases, biosecurity, outbreak investigation, contact tracing, community infection control and pandemic preparedness.
  • Strengthen your leadership capability by examining change management, organisational culture and evidence-based quality improvement.

  • Develop specialist expertise in clinical infectious diseases and public health responses across diverse settings.

Leadership and advanced practice

Throughout your studies, you'll learn how to guide teams, influence decision-making and lead system-wide improvement in infection prevention and control. You'll enhance your ability to analyse risks, evaluate safety and quality strategies, and drive change that supports better care and healthier communities.

Evidence, research and innovation

Your research training will give you the skills to evaluate emerging evidence, interpret complex data and apply research insights directly to practice. These abilities position you as a trusted adviser capable of developing innovative prevention frameworks and contributing to new knowledge in the field.

description:
Advance your career in urban and environmental planning, where strategic thinking meets development and sustainability challenges. You'll be prepared for both traditional planning and environmental practice roles, and equipped with the skills to influence the future of cities, regions and natural environments.

With a strong focus on applied learning and multidisciplinary expertise, this program sets you up for a rewarding career addressing some of the most pressing issues facing communities today and into the future.

Highlights of studying the Master of Urban and Environmental Planning
  • This masters degree enables you to work as both a town planner and as an environmental planning professional.
  • Learn from leading experts in urban, regional and environmental planning, transport, community development and tourism.
  • Develop advanced skills in spatial analysis, policy development and strategic decision-making.
  • Explore real development challenges through studio-based projects, feasibility studies and scenario planning.
  • Build confidence using tools such as GIS, urban data analytics and evidence-based research methods.
  • Examine contemporary issues including climate adaptation, transport systems, urban growth, housing, environmental protection and community engagement.
  • Apply your knowledge through a research dissertation or work-integrated learning placement, building networks and strengthening your professional readiness.
Hands-on experience in planning and development

Across foundation, core and flexible modules, you'll work on complex planning problems, from preparing and analysing development proposals to crafting strategic regional plans. Through studio courses, you'll evaluate sites, negotiate constraints, balance environmental considerations and propose innovative solutions for future communities. You'll gain practical skills and experience in transport planning, community engagement, planning law, and working with Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities, strengthening your ability to respond to the challenges of contemporary urban development and environmental change.

Advance your expertise through research and engagement

Explore planning theory, understand the policy frameworks governing development and learn to integrate ecological, social, cultural, political and economic perspectives into your work. Courses in research design, urban data analytics and First Peoples and planning will broaden your professional capability and prepare you for roles that require critical thinking and ethical engagement.

Industry experience and research opportunities

Enhance your studies through practical industry experience and independent research. Work integrated learning offers 130 hours of professional experience with a planning or design practice, giving you hands-on experience with real projects. You may undertake a minimum 80-hour community internship with a not-for-profit organisation aligned with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals, combining academic learning with meaningful community impact. Alternatively, you may choose to complete a research dissertation under academic supervision, which may open opportunities for PhD study.

description:
Learn how to plan and design cities that respond to the challenges of modern life, from population growth and housing needs to climate resilience and sustainable transport. This degree equips you with the tools to influence how people live, move and connect and take advantage of the wealth of job opportunities available in this field.

Highlights of studying the Bachelor of Urban Planning (Honours)
  • Develop the technical, analytical and creative skills to understand the social, economic and environmental dynamics shaping urban growth - and turn your ideas into practical solutions.
  • Explore topics such as environmental planning, regional development, urban design, transport systems and community engagement, all underpinned by a strong understanding of planning policy and sustainable development.
  • Gain hands-on experience through design studios, real projects and site visits that bring planning theory to life.
  • Learn from leading academics and practising professionals with extensive experience in planning, design and policy.
  • Build valuable professional connections through networking opportunities and collaborative projects with industry partners.
Hands-on experience in sustainable planning

From your first year, you'll work on practical projects that explore real planning challenges facing cities today, from developing transport strategies to designing greener neighbourhoods. By applying planning theories to real-world contexts, you'll learn to balance social needs, environmental sustainability and economic growth in your designs and proposals.

Enhance your employability with an industry placement, gaining practical experience and insights into the profession before you graduate. In your final year, complete an independent research project guided by expert supervisors, providing a foundation for further study or entry into roles that value analytical and research expertise.

Take your expertise further

As a graduate, you may choose to pursue postgraduate research, with this honours program providing direct entry into higher degree research programs and opening doors to careers in planning research and policy development.

description:
Start your journey into the world of psychology with the Diploma of Psychological Science. Designed as a pathway into the Bachelor of Psychological Science or Bachelor of Counselling, this program gives you the foundation you need to succeed in your studies and future career. You'll build core knowledge and skills in a supportive environment while developing confidence to take on higher-level learning.

The Diploma of Psychological Science introduces you to the theory and practice of psychology, with a focus on mental health and wellbeing. You'll explore how biological, social and cultural factors influence human behaviour, while building practical skills in communication, counselling and research methods. With an emphasis on applying what you learn to real-world issues, you'll discover how psychology helps address challenges faced by individuals, families and communities.

Highlights of studying the Diploma of Psychological Science 
  • Study the same courses as your Bachelor of Psychological Science or Bachelor of Counselling peers. 
  • Develop skills in interpersonal communication, counselling and research methods. 
  • Access dedicated support, including peer-assisted study sessions run by high-achieving students. 
  • Learn from world-class researchers, including those from Griffith's Centre for Mental Health, who are working on projects from youth mental health to family wellbeing. 
A pathway with purpose 

Once you have successfully completed this diploma, you'll have the confidence to continue your studies and will be offered guaranteed entry into the second year of the Bachelor of Psychological Science (1012) or the Bachelor of Counselling (1548).

description:
Prepare yourself for a rewarding career in the healthcare sector with Griffith University's Diploma of Health Science, a program designed to lay the groundwork for success in health-related fields. Whether you aspire to pursue studies in health science, biomedical science, pharmacy, pharmacology & toxicology, or a related health degree, this diploma equips you with the knowledge, skills, and experiences needed to excel in your chosen path.

Delve into subjects crucial to understanding the complexities of human health and disease. Industry and expert connections

Griffith University's faculty members bring a wealth of experience in teaching and biomedical research. They have strong connections to all health disciplines and to industry professionals, ensuring that your education remains relevant and up to date. By learning from experienced professionals with strong ties to health sectors, government agencies, and non-governmental organisations, you gain valuable insights and networking opportunities that enrich your educational experience and enhance your future prospects.

description:
Refine your creative voice and further your career in music. Designed for emerging and established musicians, you'll undertake an immersive learning experience that combines advanced performance, creative practice and research with individual mentorship from leading practitioners.

Highlights of studying the Master of Music
  • Develop advanced skills in performance, composition, songwriting, conducting or music technology.
  • Learn through intensive one-to-one lessons, workshops and collaborative projects with expert musicians. You'll work closely with experienced mentors to refine your craft, explore new repertoire and develop original work across a range of musical styles and disciplines.
  • Build research capability through creative projects and exegesis (text analysis) or dissertation pathways.
  • Access industry-relevant experiences including internships, production projects and performance opportunities.
  • Tailor your degree with specialisations in artistic practice or pedagogy to suit your career goals.
  • Eligible students may receive credit for approved recognised prior study and/or relevant professional experience, so you can complete your masters in as little as one year of full-time study.
Advance your creative practice

Deepen your technical mastery while expanding your creative and critical thinking. The Queensland Conservatorium, Griffith University is one of Australia's leading music and performing arts schools with state-of-the-art facilities, renowned lecturers and intense creative immersion. In this environment you'll strengthen your ability to collaborate, innovate and adapt as you prepare to shape the future of music.

Majors

Pedagogy: Advance your music teaching practice with a focus on experiential learning and cross-genre training. You'll build practical skills across diverse styles, informed by both classical and contemporary approaches, while developing your own teaching philosophy. With specialised training in areas such as vocal pedagogy, you'll learn through lectures, one-to-one lessons and crossover sessions that expand your repertoire and teaching techniques across studio, classroom and ensemble settings.

Artistic Practice: Refine your creative and professional practice across performance, composition, songwriting, conducting or music technology. You'll receive personalised guidance through one-to-one lessons with expert practitioners, supported by workshops tailored to your discipline. Alongside developing your craft, you'll strengthen your research capability through creative projects and exegesis, enabling deeper exploration and articulation of your work.

description:
The Brisbane South (Nathan) offering of this program is scheduled to be delivered at the Treasury Building at our Brisbane City campus in 2027. If scheduled opening is delayed, courses may be delivered all or in part at our other Brisbane locations.

Queensland's #1 university for political science. (ShanghaiRanking's Global Ranking of Academic Subjects, tied position, 2026)

This degree is designed for future leaders, thinkers and changemakers who want to understand and influence the political and social systems that shape our world.

Explore critical global questions like:

  • how do political systems work and why do some fail? 
  • what role does diplomacy and international relations play in global conflicts?
  • how do laws get made and who really holds the power?
  • why do some leaders turn authoritarian and how can democracy survive in the face of such challenges?
Highlights of studying the Bachelor of Advanced Political Science and International Relations (Honours)
  • Deepen your understanding of politics, global systems, and diplomacy, examining the forces that shape nations and influence international cooperation.
  • Gain practical experience through internships, parliamentary placements, field trips and employability courses, building essential professional connections while you study.
  • Learn from leading political scientists, diplomats, and international policy experts, whose work informs national and global political debates.

Majors

International Relations: Explore how power, conflict, cooperation and ideology shape global affairs. You'll examine the forces influencing diplomacy, security, migration, foreign policy and global governance. Courses cover theoretical frameworks and great power politics, as well as emerging issues like terrorism, climate change and religious resurgence.

Political Science and Public Policy: Examine how power is exercised, how decisions are made and how political systems shape society. Explore key domestic and international issues like elections, governance, Indigenous politics, media influence and environmental policy. You'll gain a deep understanding of policy development, democratic systems and authoritarian regimes, with a strong focus on political dynamics. If you're passionate about influencing change, understanding political behaviour or shaping public debate, this major offers the tools to become a thoughtful analyst, policymaker or advocate in the public sphere.

Security, Conflict and Human Rights: Explore how global power struggles, political violence and human rights intersect. You'll examine key issues such as terrorism, authoritarianism, human rights in global politics and the role of international organisations in peacekeeping and conflict resolution. You'll analyse the security strategies of major powers like China, investigate the rise of populism and study how governments and movements respond to threats and crises.

description:
Use your professional practice and advanced research skills to complete an original dissertation of your choice to promote social change, human rights and social justice, with a Bachelor of Social Work (Honours).

This honours degree is also a 4-year program but differs from the Bachelor of Social Work (1372) by having a compulsory dissertation project that will be supervised by experienced social work academics in your final year of study.

In addition to examining the foundations of human behaviour and social work, you'll engage with advanced research methods, social work theory, leadership, and evidence-based approaches that shape policy and practice.

Prepare for a rewarding social work career, supporting individuals, families, groups, and communities across diverse settings-from counselling and advocacy to community development, including the ability to undertake research and program evaluation

Highlights of the Bachelor of Social Work (Honours)

  • Learn to interrogate community challenges while developing critical research skills to inform practice and drive social change.
  • Connecting theory with action, you'll develop the skills to ensure interventions are effective, ethical, and responsive to the needs of individuals and communities.
  • Gain hands-on experience through field placements supervised by qualified social workers, in major government and non-government organisations, including hospitals, child protection, mental health, domestic violence, and community services, while critically examining practice through a research-informed lens.
  • Learn from academic staff who are not only experienced practitioners but also active researchers shaping knowledge in fields such as mental health, domestic violence, child welfare, disability advocacy, homelessness, social policy, and social justice.

Real-world experience that prepares you for practice

You'll complete two professional field placements during your degree, gaining 1,000 hours of experience under the supervision of a qualified social worker. Whether you're working with a hospital team, a community organisation, or in child protection, domestic violence, disability services, or mental health, you'll build the skills to make a genuine difference in people's lives.

Research for impact

Undertaking a research dissertation, you'll stand out with in-demand research skills and pave the way for postgraduate study, including a PhD if you choose. Research skills are highly valued in the social work field, and graduates with these skills can engage in research and evaluation and contribute to new knowledge in many employment contexts.

description:
Queensland's #1 university for AI research. (ShanghaiRanking's Global Ranking of Academic Subjects, tied position, 2026)

Expand your career prospects with this double degree that blends scientific discovery with creative and analytical thinking. You'll gain a unique combination of practical scientific expertise, and the communication, cultural awareness and critical thinking skills that drive innovation across communities and industries. If you're curious about how the world works, passionate about ideas, or interested in solving real problems from multiple perspectives, this double degree offers the best of both science and arts disciplines.

You'll build strong foundations in scientific inquiry, data analysis and evidence-based reasoning while developing advanced communication, research and problem-solving skills. Studying science at Griffith means learning through hands-on experiences in living laboratories, where nature is your classroom and sustainability is embedded throughout your studies. This multidisciplinary mix means you won't just understand complex scientific issues, you'll also be equipped to interpret them, communicate them and apply them in social, cultural and global contexts.

Highlights of studying the Bachelor of Science/Bachelor of Arts
  • Build skills in ecology, chemistry, biochemistry, physics, clinical sciences, geography, microbiology and applied mathematics.
  • Shape your double degree your way with a flexible structure that lets you explore disciplines, switch or combine majors, and tailor your study to your interests and goals.
  • Boost your employability with strong industry and research connections, including internships, volunteering, study tours and other work-integrated learning opportunities. In your final year, you may take part in a capstone experience in research or fieldwork.
  • Strengthen your communication, cultural competency and critical thinking through your arts major.
  • Learn how scientific knowledge intersects with society and how it shapes global challenges, ethics, culture and the way people think and behave.
  • With intensive study options and year-round intakes, this degree can be finished in less time than a standard full-time study load, getting you into the workforce faster.

A flexible start with hands-on learning from day one

You'll start with a foundation first year that lets you explore both scientific and humanities disciplines before choosing your majors. You'll develop practical skills from day one through hands-on lab sessions and extensive fieldwork, learning science in unique natural environments and modern facilities.

You'll work with real scientific data, collaborate on projects that tackle contemporary environmental, health, technological and social challenges and learn alongside a supportive community of peers and academics. Your arts studies will help you interpret complex issues, engage diverse communities and communicate insights with clarity and impact.

description:
Work towards a career as an early years education specialist and make a meaningful impact during the most important period of a child's learning and development. Designed for qualified registered teachers, this graduate certificate expands your expertise so you can teach in preschool settings (1-5 years) and confidently support children in the early years of school (5-8 years).

With a strong focus on contemporary practice, inclusive education and practical experience, this qualification will strengthen your professional identity and prepare you for specialised early childhood roles.

Highlights of studying the Graduate Certificate in Early Childhood Education and Care
  • Extend your teaching qualifications to include preschool and early years settings.
  • Explore contemporary theories of child development, equity and diversity.
  • Build your knowledge of early childhood curriculum and pedagogy.
  • Engage in significant professional experience with children from birth to eight years old.
  • Develop confidence working with families, communities and multidisciplinary teams.
Explore the foundations of early childhood education 

Investigate the philosophies, histories and social influences that have guided early childhood education in Australia and around the world. You'll learn how children's rights, educator ethics and community context inform high-quality practice, and explore how teachers and children can co-construct meaningful curriculum that responds to children's interests, abilities and cultural identities. With knowledge of development, pedagogy and professional practice, you'll be prepared to support young learners during their formative years.

Build your expertise through early childhood placements  

Gain hands-on experience through an extensive professional placement program, where you'll participate in observation, planning, teaching and critical reflection in early childhood environments. These experiences are aligned with the National Quality Standard, the Early Years Learning Framework and the Queensland Kindergarten Learning Guideline, ensuring you graduate with skills that meet sector expectations.

description:
Tap into your strengths in the field of social and community services, where evidence-based practice meets advocacy, policy and frontline support. With flexible online study designed for working professionals, the Master of Human Services will prepare you to drive meaningful change across government and non-government sectors.

Highlights of studying the Master of Human Services
  • Build advanced skills in counselling, advocacy and leadership to support individuals, families and communities.
  • Develop a strong understanding of Australian law, social policy and the systems that influence human services delivery.
  • Strengthen your practice through contemporary research in mental health, disability inclusion and child and family wellbeing.
  • Learn alongside professionals from diverse backgrounds.
  • Undertake a research dissertation to deepen your expertise and prepare for a PhD or Master of Philosophy.

Through applied counselling training you'll build practical skills grounded in ethics and cultural responsiveness.

Examine how social policies are developed, learn strategies for effective advocacy and build leadership capability to establish and improve programs that promote equity, human rights and social justice. You'll study real scenarios so you can critically analyse systems, engage communities and lead reform.

Queensland's #1 university for political science. (ShanghaiRanking's Global Ranking of Academic Subjects, tied position, 2026)

Kickstart your career in political science, international relations and international law. This vertical degree is designed for ambitious students who want to fast-track their expertise in global governance, diplomacy and international legal frameworks.

Highlights of studying the Bachelor of Political Science and International Relations/Master of International Law
  • Graduate with both a bachelors and a masters degree in just four years. Gain advanced knowledge, strengthen your career prospects and reach advanced qualifications sooner.
  • Build a strong foundation in global politics and public policy before progressing into specialised international law studies that elevate your credentials and competitive edge.
  • Gain practical experience through internships, case studies and industry engagement.
  • Build cross-cultural capability and global awareness, skills and insights that are highly valued by employers.
A powerful combination of politics and international law

In your first two years, you'll explore how power, institutions and ideas influence global and domestic politics. Depending on your major, you may examine diplomacy, foreign policy and security, analyse elections and public policy, or investigate conflict, terrorism and human rights. You'll develop critical thinking, policy analysis and research skills that form the foundation of effective leadership in government and international affairs.

From year three, you'll transition into postgraduate-level international law courses. This integration of political science and international law prepares you to navigate complex international systems with confidence.

Career-ready with a global outlook

Career readiness is embedded throughout this degree. You'll engage in workshops, collaborative projects and case studies that connect theory to practice. These experiences help you build a professional network and develop the communication, negotiation and analytical skills essential in global careers.

Majors

Bachelor of Political Science and International Relations majors

International Relations: Examine how power, conflict and cooperation influence global affairs. Explore diplomacy, security, migration and foreign policy, alongside major power politics and emerging issues such as terrorism and climate change.

Political Science and Public Policy: Explore how political systems operate and how policy decisions are made. Analyse elections, governance and environmental policy, while building skills for careers in analysis, policymaking and advocacy.

Security, Conflict and Human Rights: Investigate the links between political violence, security and human rights. Study terrorism, authoritarianism and peacekeeping while analysing how governments and international organisations respond to global crises.

Advance your career in healthcare science and develop the specialised skills required to perform diagnostic testing in private and public health settings. Designed for graduates in physiology or related biomedical sciences, this graduate diploma strengthens your clinical knowledge while building your professional capacity to work in hospitals and health services.

Highlights of studying the Graduate Diploma of Clinical Physiology
  • Develop advanced knowledge of human physiology and pathophysiology across major organ systems.
  • Learn to evaluate organ function using clinical measurement and diagnostic testing techniques.
  • Gain expertise in biomedical instrumentation used to record and analyse physiological signals.

description:
Advance your expertise at the complex intersection of mental health and the criminal justice system. Delivered in collaboration with Queensland Health's Forensic Mental Health Service, this program is designed for professionals and graduates seeking specialist knowledge in how mental disorder, offending behaviour and systems of justice interact.

Highlights of studying the Graduate Certificate in Forensic Mental Health
  • Explore contemporary theories of mental disorder and criminal offending, including social, psychological and philosophical perspectives.
  • Develop skills in forensic mental health assessment, risk analysis and case-based decision making.
  • Build an understanding of mental health systems, criminal justice processes and policy frameworks.
  • Learn how to evaluate and apply risk assessment tools to inform safety, intervention and management decisions.
  • Strengthen your ability to interpret research and apply evidence-based approaches in forensic settings.
  • Study online, allowing you to balance professional and personal commitments, and complete a postgraduate qualification in just one year of part-time study.
Build specialist insight into forensic mental health practice

Explore the core foundations of forensic mental health, including how mental illness is defined, classified and understood across cultural and social contexts. You'll also examine key criminological and psychological theories of offending behaviour, alongside debates around free will, responsibility and environmental influence.

Drawing on real case scenarios, you'll consider how mental health and criminal justice systems interact in practice, including the impact of policy, diagnosis and service delivery on individuals and communities.

A strong focus on risk assessment will build your ability to interpret structured approaches used to assess the likelihood of harm and inform decision making across correctional, clinical and community settings.

A pathway into advanced forensic mental health study

Whether you're returning to study, transitioning from psychology, health, criminology or justice fields, or building toward the Master of Forensic Mental Health (5779), you'll develop essential academic skills including critical analysis, research literacy and academic writing, while gaining a strong foundation in forensic mental health theory and practice.

Flexibility

Study anytime, anywhere - This degree is available online through our Digital campus, giving you more room to fit university with your work and social life.

Pursue further study

The courses in this graduate certificate may be credited towards a related graduate diploma or masters degree. Griffith's innovative Credit Precedent Database allows you to find out what credit decisions have been made in the past, which will give you an idea of what you can expect.

description:
Advance your financial services career with a Master of Financial Planning. As demand grows for qualified and ethical financial advisers, this degree equips you with the advanced knowledge and practical skills to guide individuals and families through complex financial decisions. Covering investments, taxation, risk management and retirement planning, you'll be prepared to deliver evidence-based financial advice in an evolving regulatory environment.

Highlights of studying the Master of Financial Planning
  • Develop expertise in investment strategies, financial markets, taxation, wealth planning and portfolio management.
  • Explore behavioural finance to better understand client decision making.
  • Learn the legal and ethical responsibilities of professional financial advisers.
  • Apply financial planning principles to real client scenarios and integrated advice strategies.
  • Graduate with a degree accredited under the standards set by the Financial Adviser Standards and Conduct Unit (FASCU).
  • Eligible students may receive credit for approved recognised prior study and/or relevant professional experience, so you may gain a masters qualification in as little as 1 year of full-time study.
Ethical advice and long-term wealth strategies

Develop a comprehensive understanding of modern financial planning practice through specialised courses in investments, income tax law and personal risk management. Examine financial markets, asset allocation strategies and risk mitigation techniques while building the skills required to design effective financial plans.

This degree emphasises the ethical, behavioural and legal foundations of professional financial advice. You'll explore behavioural finance to understand how clients make financial decisions and learn strategies to support better long-term outcomes. You'll be prepared to guide clients through major life stages while ensuring wealth transfer, compliance and financial security are carefully managed.

Flexible pathways for career progression

The program includes a foundation component, enabling graduates from other disciplines to transition into financial planning. Professionals already working in financial services can also enter the program and progress directly to advanced study. Flexible online delivery allows you to balance study with professional commitments while building specialised expertise.

Queensland's #1 university for law and criminology. (ShanghaiRanking's Global Ranking of Academic Subjects 2026)

The Master of International Law Studies is designed for ambitious professionals and emerging scholars who want to understand how law operates across borders, cultures and international systems. You'll explore how global rules are made, contested, enforced and applied in real legal, political and commercial contexts.

Whether you're advancing your legal career or moving into an international-facing role, this degree will give you the expertise to operate effectively in a global environment.

Highlights of studying the Master of International Law Studies
  • Build strong foundations in public international law, global law principles and international negotiations.
  • Examine issues like human rights, criminal justice, environmental law, trade, intellectual property and armed conflict.
  • Develop practical skills for handling cross-border disputes, international family matters and global commercial litigation.
  • Be guided by academics and industry experts with deep experience in international courts, tribunals and policy environments.
  • Deepen your expertise through electives in global security, climate policy, international relations and cyber law.
  • Strengthen your research capability with advanced research methods and the option to complete an independent research project.
A degree that connects you to the global legal landscape

Engage with real international case studies, contemporary global challenges and the legal frameworks that govern them. You'll explore how international rules influence everything from humanitarian crises to trade disputes, environmental protection, technology and cross-border negotiations.

Flexible learning designed for ambitious professionals

Your study experience is adaptable, allowing you to tailor the degree to your career ambitions. Whether you want to deepen your research capability, step into policy development or advance your legal practice internationally, the flexible module lets you pursue research projects or choose electives that complement your professional goals. From cyber law to global corporate responsibility and climate change policy, you can build a portfolio of expertise that reflects your goals.

description:
Deepen your expertise in suicide prevention by exploring the complex social, psychological and cultural factors associated with suicidal behaviour. Learn and apply research-based strategies supporting prevention, intervention and postvention efforts. You'll also build the analytical skills to understand suicide from multiple perspectives and contribute to evidence-based responses across health, education and community sectors.

Highlights of studying the Master of Suicidology
  • Evaluate leading suicide assessment tools and their application in research and support contexts.
  • Explore contemporary intervention approaches used to support people experiencing suicidal distress.
  • Build strong research and critical analysis skills to investigate trends, risk factors and prevention strategies.
  • Choose a major to align your study with your career goals.
  • Eligible students may receive credit for approved recognised prior study and/or relevant professional experience, so you may gain a masters in as little as 1 year of full-time study.
Research-led learning in suicide prevention

With a focus on scientific enquiry, this degree emphasises research-informed knowledge and does not aim to educate and train students to be clinicians. The focus on research-based enquiry and investigation enables you to contribute to suicide prevention initiatives at local, national and global levels.

Majors

Tailor your studies through a major in:

Integrated Care: Build the knowledge and practical insight needed to support people experiencing suicidal distress within complex health and human service systems. Explore mental health and co-occurring conditions, consumer and carer perspectives, and culturally responsive practice, including working with First Peoples communities. You'll develop the skills to contribute to coordinated, person-centred approaches that improve outcomes across integrated care settings.

Community and Leadership: Develop the capability to evaluate, support and lead suicide prevention initiatives at community, policy and population levels. Examine public health approaches including epidemiology, ethical decision making, advocacy and community engagement.

Deepen your expertise in suicide prevention by exploring the complex social, psychological and cultural factors associated with suicidal behaviour. Learn and apply research-based strategies supporting prevention, intervention and postvention efforts. You'll also build the analytical skills to understand suicide from multiple perspectives and contribute to evidence-based responses across health, education and community sectors.

Highlights of studying the Master of Suicidology
  • Evaluate leading suicide assessment tools and their application in research and support contexts.
  • Explore contemporary intervention approaches used to support people experiencing suicidal distress.
  • Build strong research and critical analysis skills to investigate trends, risk factors and prevention strategies.
  • Choose a major to align your study with your career goals.
