Research-led learning in suicide prevention

With a focus on scientific enquiry, this degree emphasises research-informed knowledge and does not aim to educate and train students to be clinicians. The focus on research-based enquiry and investigation enables you to contribute to suicide prevention initiatives at local, national and global levels.

description:
Study the fast-paced, rewarding field of paramedicine, where you can make a real difference in people's lives. This degree equips you with the essential skills and knowledge to work as a paramedic in traditional and non-traditional settings.

You'll develop strong clinical decision-making, problem-solving and critical thinking skills, while gaining a deep understanding of the human body, paramedic practice and the care of diverse conditions, diseases and trauma.

Highlights of studying the Bachelor of Paramedicine
  • Our small student intake means more personalised support, more opportunities for active participation and meaningful interaction and a closer connection with teaching staff.
  • Our simulation facilities give you authentic, hands-on clinical experience using the same equipment as the Queensland Ambulance Service and other paramedicine organisations in Australia and overseas.
  • Graduate prepared to confidently respond to a wide range of situations, helping to improve health and wellbeing.
  • Open doors to international opportunities, allowing you to work in different countries and grow your career in paramedicine.
Practical paramedicine experience 

Experience a variety of clinical placements that build your hands-on skills across different healthcare settings. You'll complete ambulance placements-4 weeks at the end of your first and second years, and 6 weeks in your final year-on a four on, four off roster. Non-ambulance placements are also available, giving you a well-rounded understanding of healthcare challenges and helping you refine your professional practice.

description:
Australia's #1 university for nursing and midwifery. (ShanghaiRanking's Global Ranking of Academic Subjects 2026)

Begin your career with confidence at Australia's No. 1 university for midwifery*. This degree prepares you to work across all models of midwifery practice, developing the knowledge, empathy and clinical judgement needed to support women, newborns and families through every stage of pregnancy, birth and postnatal care.

You'll learn from experienced midwives and gain extensive experience through clinical placements. With a focus on safe, culturally responsive and patient-centred care, you'll graduate ready to make a real difference in the lives of women and their families.

Highlights of studying the Bachelor of Midwifery
  • Learn through a mix of online study and two-week on-campus intensive blocks with workshops, simulations and hands-on midwifery practice (around 70% of face-to-face sessions are available at both Gold Coast and Logan).
  • Gain valuable experience in our state-of-the-art clinics and labs at Logan and the Gold Coast, which also features Australia's first student-led midwifery clinic.
  • Provide advice, support and continuum of care for at least 20 women through pregnancy, birth and beyond. This highly rewarding unique journey requires flexibility and commitment.
  • Train with the latest technology, including birth simulations and our life-like birthing mum.
  • Collaborate with students and staff from different health areas, building teamwork skills in diverse maternity care environments. 
Practical clinical experience

Gain experience at leading hospitals and clinics across morning, evening and night shifts. Opportunities are available at Logan Hospital (and Beaudesert), Redlands Hospital, Gold Coast University Hospital, Toowoomba Hospital, Sunshine Coast University Hospital, Northern NSW Local Health District and midwifery private practices. International placements are also available.

Career-ready outcomes 

Benefit from the professional expertise and industry networks of our award-winning teachers, who are leaders in research, education and practice. With a strong track record of graduate success, you'll be workforce-ready, with industry connections, expert mentorship and practical learning ensuring you are confident and prepared for a successful career in midwifery.

Honours

description:
Do you want to uncover what drives people's thoughts, feelings and actions? The Bachelor of Psychological Science gives you a solid foundation in psychological theory, research methods and applications. You'll explore processes that shape human behaviour across a variety of contexts, from development and cognition to mental health and social behaviour.

With a flexible degree structure, you can shape your studies by choosing electives that complement psychology and open diverse career pathways, from business and HR to criminology, sport science and beyond.

Highlights of studying the Bachelor of Psychological Science
  • Study a mix of psychology disciplines, guided by experienced researchers and industry professionals.
  • Learn to design research studies, collect and analyse data and contribute to impactful research. 
  • Develop practical skills and explore concepts across counselling, communication, group facilitation and behaviour change.
Choosing the right psychology degree 

Griffith's Bachelor of Psychological Science and Bachelor of Psychology (Honours) share many of the same core subjects, so your choice depends on your study and career goals. Both degrees are fully accredited and build strong foundations to enter the workforce, or for the postgraduate study needed to pursue registration as a psychologist.

The Bachelor of Psychological Science offers flexibility and a solid three-year grounding in human behaviour and how we think, act and feel. The Bachelor of Psychology (Honours) (1014) is an integrated four-year degree designed for high-achieving students who want to complete their Honours year as part of their degree, gaining advanced research experience along the way.

Honours

description:
Gain the practical experience and industry connections that open pathways into medicine, research and allied health. Biomedical science plays a vital role in improving health outcomes, treatment and patient care. You'll build a deep understanding of human health and disease, while developing the practical skills, clinical insight and professional confidence needed for a wide range of health-focused careers.

If you study this degree at the Gold Coast campus, you'll follow a health-oriented curriculum with strong links to clinical practice and community health. If you wish to study at the South Brisbane (Nathan) campus, you'll undertake a science-focused program and should apply for the Bachelor of Biomedical Science (1031). Across both campuses, you'll benefit from authentic cadaver-based anatomy learning, lab-first teaching and close connections to hospitals and research centres.

Designed for students aiming for clinical, allied health or medical pathways, this health-focused degree gives you a strong foundation in human anatomy, physiology, pharmacology and disease processes. You'll explore integrated systems physiology, molecular genetics and the molecular basis of disease.

From your first year, you'll develop the confidence and practical competence to work confidently in real lab and health settings, designed to prepare you for clinical and health science workplaces. In your final year, the BioHealth Project capstone connects you with industry or community partners to tackle real health challenges, providing realistic, multi-pathway preparation for careers in medicine, physiotherapy, pharmacy and other health professions.

Highlights of studying the Bachelor of Biomedical Science
  • Build hands-on capability through laboratory training, cadaver labs and case-based learning.
  • Gain core biomedical knowledge from your first year, supported by approachable staff and a strong sense of learning community.
  • Progress to advanced studies in genetics, biochemistry, cell biology, anatomy, physiology, immunology, microbiology, infectious disease and pharmacology.
  • Learn in modern laboratories through competency-based training, supported by simulated environments.
A holistic approach to healthcare

Great healthcare is built on collaboration. You'll study alongside students from a wide range of clinical and health disciplines, developing the teamwork, communication and problem-solving skills essential for healthcare environments.

A pathway to medicine - and beyond

For students planning to apply for the Doctor of Medicine (5099), this degree provides strong foundational knowledge to support your application. Importantly, it also prepares you for a broad range of health and science careers, offering multiple pathways into allied health, clinical practice, research and postgraduate study, including masters degrees in health professions.

Honours

Honours is available as an additional year of study for students who want to further develop their understanding of health, disease and biomedical research methods - an ideal pathway into research-focused or specialised health careers.

Everyone remembers the teacher who believed in them - the one who recognised their potential, inspired confidence and helped shape their future. Become that teacher for your students and help create a brighter future for the next generation.

description:
Take the next step to becoming a registered pharmacist with the Master of Pharmacy, an accredited graduate-entry degree designed to prepare you for a rewarding career improving health outcomes through the safe and effective use of medicines.

Building on your undergraduate science or health science background, this degree delivers advanced knowledge in pharmaceutical science, clinical pharmacy practice and research to develop you into a confident, skilled healthcare professional.

Highlights of studying the Master of Pharmacy
  • Gain the academic qualification required for eligibility to register as a pharmacist in Australia.
  • Develop clinical expertise through placements in community, hospital and specialist pharmacy settings.
  • Learn from experienced pharmacists, clinicians and researchers actively shaping the future of medicine use and patient care.
  • Build advanced communication, problem-solving and decision-making skills through simulated and collaborative learning experiences.
  • Explore innovative drug delivery systems, quality use of medicines and evidence-based therapeutic management.
  • Enhance your understanding of health leadership, ethics and pharmacy management to prepare for diverse career pathways.
Graduate ready to make an impact in patient care

Through a mix of classroom learning, clinical placements and professional simulations, you'll gain the knowledge and experience needed to support patients across all stages of care. You'll graduate prepared to enter an internship program with the skills to improve medication safety, promote health literacy and deliver person-centred care.

While there are a number of accredited internship program providers, there are steps to be met (including provisional registration with the Pharmacy Board of Australia) before your internship can commence. Please see more complete information about internships on the pathway to registration.

The Master of Pharmacy is an AQF Level 9 Masters Extended degree.

From 1 January 2025, graduates who have completed the program requirements for this AQF Level 9 Masters Degree (Extended) program are able to use the qualification title 'Doctor of Pharmacy'. For more information visit the Australian Qualifications (AQF) Changes to the Issuance Policy - Masters Degree (Extended) Addendum 5.

description:
Discover your path to create impact. The Bachelor of Arts gives you the freedom to explore what matters to you while building the skills to create meaningful change in communities, workplaces and society. Choosing from a wide range of majors, including history, creative writing, sociology and more, you'll develop a deeper understanding of people, policy and cultures while preparing for a wide range of careers.

More than a collection of subjects, our Bachelor of Arts is built around a connected core journey designed to support you throughout your degree. You'll combine your interests with practical experience, industry engagement and career-focused learning, graduating with the confidence, adaptability and purpose to succeed in your chosen field.

Highlights of studying the Bachelor of Arts
  • Develop future-focused skills employers value, including communication, critical thinking, creativity, research, collaboration and problem solving.
  • Follow a structured core journey designed to help you connect your learning, build career awareness and develop professional confidence from day one.
  • Choose from a broad range of majors, encompassing history, literary studies, creative writing, sociology and much more, combined with electives and flexible study options to create a degree aligned with your interests and ambitions.
  • Explore social, cultural, political and environmental challenges while learning how to contribute meaningful solutions.
  • With one of the largest range of industry internships in Queensland, you'll gain practical workplace experience and connect directly with employers.
Turn your passions into impact

Your interests are the starting point for a degree with purpose. You'll examine issues connected to social change, sustainability, diversity, culture, technology and global challenges. Working with community and not-for-profit organisations, you'll learn how ideas can create positive change while building practical skills that translate into professional impact.

Career-ready from day one

Career development is embedded throughout your degree. Core courses such as Public Policy for Change and Industry Internship help you connect your interests to future opportunities while building the confidence to articulate the value of your degree to employers.

You'll also benefit from dedicated placement support for internships and industry projects with government agencies, community organisations, media organisations, communications agencies and other industry partners.

Future-ready skills in an AI-enabled world

As technology transforms the way we live and work, the Bachelor of Arts prepares you to work confidently alongside emerging technologies while strengthening the uniquely human skills employers continue to value. You'll develop AI literacy, ethical reasoning, digital capability, creativity, judgement, critical thinking and communication skills that help you adapt to changing workplaces and future opportunities.

Flexibility to create your future

Design a degree that reflects your goals, strengths and interests. With flexible study options and multiple intakes each year, you can tailor your studies through the majors and electives you select, as well as internships, study abroad opportunities and research experiences.

description:
Study one of Australia's largest and most highly recognised aviation degrees and launch your career in the exciting global aviation industry. The Bachelor of Aviation is an accelerated full-time two-year degree designed to get you career-ready sooner.

You'll build a strong foundation in the science and theory of flying while gaining the practical skills needed for a wide range of operational and managerial roles in aviation. The Bachelor of Aviation together with fully self-funded flight training with an external provider will allow graduates to work in the aviation industry as a commercial pilot.

Study core courses like aerodynamics, meteorology, aircraft systems, flight operations and navigation, safety management systems and the human factors (how people influence safety) in aviation, preparing you for the next step into professional flight training or other operational and managerial pathways.

Highlights of studying the Bachelor of Aviation
  • Accelerated two-year program to fast-track your aviation degree
  • Access advanced on-campus flight simulators for realistic training
  • Learn from industry experts and aviation researchers with global experience
  • Be prepared for pilot training or other operational or managerial roles in aviation.
Build skills and connections for your aviation career

You may choose to progress into flight school training with providers certified by the Civil Aviation Safety Authority (CASA), where you can accumulate flight hours and earn your Commercial Pilot Licence. We recommend flight training is undertaken after completing your degree. Our graduates are highly sought after, going on to fly for commercial airlines, freight operators, flight schools, rescue services, agricultural aviation and the Australian Defence Force.

Completing a Bachelor of Aviation before gaining your pilot licence gives you a strong foundation for a long-term career in aviation. It provides a competitive edge for airline graduate programs and leadership roles, while also offering flexibility to pursue other aviation pathways if your career goals evolve.

Take off with Aviation MATES 

As a Griffith Aviation student, you'll gain exclusive access to the Mentoring Aviators Through Educational Support (MATES) program, a supportive network that connects you with industry professionals, weekly guest speakers and dedicated student Flight Leaders. MATES helps you build personal connections, expand your professional network and gain real insights that will set you apart in the aviation industry.

  • Learn from industry experts and aviation researchers with global experience
  • Be prepared for pilot training or other operational or managerial roles in aviation.
Build skills and connections for your aviation career

You may choose to progress into flight school training with providers certified by the Civil Aviation Safety Authority (CASA), where you can accumulate flight hours and earn your Commercial Pilot Licence. We recommend flight training is undertaken after completing your degree. Our graduates are highly sought after, going on to fly for commercial airlines, freight operators, flight schools, rescue services, agricultural aviation and the Australian Defence Force.

Completing a Bachelor of Aviation before gaining your pilot licence gives you a strong foundation for a long-term career in aviation. It provides a competitive edge for airline graduate programs and leadership roles, while also offering flexibility to pursue other aviation pathways if your career goals evolve.

Take off with Aviation MATES 

As a Griffith Aviation student, you'll gain exclusive access to the Mentoring Aviators Through Educational Support (MATES) program, a supportive network that connects you with industry professionals, weekly guest speakers and dedicated student Flight Leaders. MATES helps you build personal connections, expand your professional network and gain real insights that will set you apart in the aviation industry.

description:
Unlock your potential in the world of forensic science, where rigorous scientific training underpins real-world criminal investigation. Our Bachelor of Forensic Science is Queensland's only dedicated and accredited forensic science degree, designed to give you the crime scene, laboratory and investigative skills trusted by employers. With a strong science-first approach and a focus on practical learning, you'll graduate as a confident, job-ready forensic professional.

You'll build strong foundations in chemistry and biology before applying them to forensic contexts - a critical advantage in a field where scientific accuracy matters. Study alongside a supportive student community, learn from approachable academics with real case experience, and connect directly with industry through guest lectures, networking events and professional bodies such as the Australian and New Zealand Forensic Science Society (ANZFSS). You'll gain a clear understanding of what forensic careers really involve and the multiple pathways available beyond traditional roles.

Highlights of studying the Bachelor of Forensic Science
  • Study Queensland's only accredited forensic science degree, developed to meet industry standards and employer expectations.
  • Build strong chemistry and biology foundations through a science-first curriculum, before applying your skills to forensic investigation.
  • Develop the practical lab and analytical skills employers demand through extensive hands-on experience in forensic biology and chemistry.
  • Learn to evaluate evidence objectively, using contemporary forensic analysis methods and emerging investigative technologies.
  • Learn from industry-leading academics who have provided expert evidence in Australian courts.
  • Gain experience through casework, reporting and moot court simulations.
  • Engage with the forensic profession through ANZFSS events, guest talks from police and private forensic labs and dedicated student careers evenings.
Hands-on experience in forensic investigation

From your first year, you'll develop a deep understanding of forensic investigation grounded in hard science. You'll study core courses in biology, chemistry, molecular genetics and forensic investigation before progressing into your chosen major. In second and third year, you'll refine your expertise through advanced lab work and applied forensic analysis, building a comprehensive, industry-relevant skillset.

Double your opportunities

The Bachelor of Forensic Science/Bachelor of Criminology and Criminal Justice (1706) double degree is also available. Combine forensic science with criminology to strengthen your understanding of legal and criminal justice systems and broaden your career opportunities across forensic investigation, regulation and law enforcement.

Forensic science majors

Forensic Chemistry: Apply chemistry to real-world investigations using industry-aligned analytical techniques. You'll gain experience across organic, inorganic, physical and analytical chemistry, working with cutting-edge instrumentation to analyse substances and trace evidence. With applications in toxicology, drug analysis and environmental forensics, this major prepares you for roles as a forensic chemist, toxicologist or analytical scientist. Royal Australian Chemical Institute (RACI) accreditation for this major signals standards-aligned training and enhances graduate credibility with employers.

Forensic Molecular Biology: Combine genetics and justice through advanced molecular and cellular techniques used in human identification and criminal investigation. You'll study DNA profiling, gene expression, protein science and molecular biology, gaining extensive lab experience through forensic applications. Graduates are prepared for roles such as forensic biologist, DNA analyst or molecular laboratory scientist.

description:
Deepen your expertise in educational leadership, policy, wellbeing and innovation. The Master of Education is designed for educators and professionals working across schools, tertiary settings, community organisations and government. Whether you're an experienced teacher, school leader, development officer or education professional, you'll strengthen your knowledge of contemporary education practice, research and reform.

Please note: The Master of Education is not designed to lead to initial teacher registration (Primary or Secondary) or accreditation as an Early Childhood Education and Care teacher. If your goal is registration or accreditation in one of these areas, visit: Master of Primary Teaching (5587), Master of Secondary Teaching (5700) or Graduate Certificate in Early Childhood Education and Care (3327).

Highlights of studying the Master of Education
  • Critically examine the purpose of education and explore how policy decisions influence learners, institutions and communities locally and globally.
  • Develop advanced knowledge of educational leadership, policy and research.
  • Build advanced research capability, analytical skills and strategic insight to lead improvement in complex learning environments.
  • Engage with key concepts from education psychology, philosophy and neuroscience to better understand how learners develop, while applying sociological perspectives to address equity, access and inclusion.
  • Flexible study options to support you to balance postgraduate education with professional commitments.
  • You may be eligible for credit for recognised prior study or work experience, allowing you to complete your degree in as little as 1 year full-time. See entry requirements below.
Majors 

Align your studies with your professional goals through a choice of majors.

Leading in Education: Develop a broad and critical understanding of leadership across diverse educational contexts, examining the relationship between leadership, systems and policy at local and global levels. Analyse change management strategies, evaluate programs and performance, and strengthen your research, communication and critical analysis skills.

Wellbeing in Education: Explore the powerful role of positive psychology in learning, teaching and professional practice by critically evaluating theories of wellbeing in educational settings. Assess leadership approaches that support resilience and mental wellbeing and investigate evidence-based responses to issues such as trauma, family violence and contemporary perspectives on childhood and adolescence.

Digital Learning in Education: Examine the ongoing digital transformation of education and its impact on teaching, learning and professional practice. Explore online networks, emerging technologies and AI, while engaging with critical discussions around AI ethics and the societal implications of digital innovation.

International Studies in Education: Gain advanced insight into globalisation and international relations within educational contexts. Analyse global discourses across education, policy and leadership and build expertise in high-level communication. You may have the opportunity to undertake an approved course at a partner university overseas.

Culturally Responsive Studies in Education: Engage with education through the lenses of ethics, cultural safety, social equity and justice. Apply strength-based and culturally responsive frameworks, deepen your understanding of Indigenous knowledges and philosophies, and extend your capability in cross-cultural practice and protocols.

description:
Prepare for a fulfilling career in secondary education and help shape the minds of the next generation. With a growing demand for qualified teachers across Australia, Griffith's Master of Secondary Teaching focuses on educating children from Year 7 to 12. This program is designed for those who hold a bachelor degree in another field and wish to transition into teaching. 

Highlights of studying the Master of Secondary Teaching 
  • Combine theory and hands-on experience to teach subject areas and manage secondary classrooms effectively. 
  • Study adolescent development, curriculum design, assessment, and classroom management. 
  • Develop critical thinking and engage with contemporary issues in education. 
  • Complete 60 days of supervised school placements with mentorship from experienced teachers to refine your teaching skills and strategies. 
  • This degree has an emphasis on the importance of differentiated instruction to meet the diverse needs of secondary students. 

You will need to identify two of the following Teaching Areas to form your study:

  • Biology# 
  • Business 
  • Chemistry# 
  • Design technologies 
  • Digital technologies 
  • Drama 
  • English 
  • Food and nutrition 
  • Geography 
  • Health and physical education 
  • History 
  • Instrumental music# 
  • Languages 
  • Mathematics 
  • Music 
  • Physics# 
  • Psychology# 
  • Visual arts 

# These teaching areas must be taken at a senior level and require a minimum of six subjects in each area in the undergraduate degree. 

If you've completed at least six psychology subjects in your bachelor degree, you can choose one of the teaching areas mentioned above at a senior level (provided you meet the subject requirements) and complete a specialist area in Learning Enhancement. This will give you the skills to support students with additional needs. You'll be qualified to work in secondary schools, either advising teachers on planning or teaching in special education settings.

description:
Study with Queensland's top-ranked university for criminology* and use your degree as a launch pad to join the fight for justice, contribute to a safer community and a better criminal justice system.

Learn from experts and industry leaders who bring their hands-on experience to your study. Our strong international research reputation means you will be taught by academics who are recognised worldwide in their various fields.

Highlights of studying the Bachelor of Criminology and Criminal Justice
  • Explore the causes of crime, how laws are made and broken, the impacts on victims, offenders and the justice system's response.
  • Analyse crime with a focus on social justice, including the roles of police, courts and corrections.
  • Draw on knowledge and insights from many fields of study including psychology, law, sociology, politics and social work.
  • Study topics like criminal law, homicide, First Nations justice, fraud and cybercrime, and domestic and family violence.
  • Learn how crime happens, ways it can be reduced and evidence-based strategies to keep communities safe. You'll also explore how research is used to measure impact and improve understanding.
  • Develop practical skills in data analysis and visualisation to understand and interpret patterns and clearly present information.
Industry connections to build your future

Engage in a wide variety of work-integrated learning experiences to help tackle issues faced by local communities. Our industry connections fuel our unique learning experiences to give you practical insight into the workings of the criminal justice system, as well as the opportunity to work with agencies matched to your career aspirations.

Experience matters

Join one of the largest communities of criminologists in the world and access the best minds in the industry. We're internationally renowned for applied research that makes a difference and for close collaborations with practitioners and employers. That knowledge feeds into the most up-to-date study content, giving you the best skills for an employment edge.

You'll develop career-ready skills and experience working on real projects, cumulating in a capstone course where you'll work with industry on a project relating to a current local community crime problem. You'll have the opportunity to apply for a professional placement experience throughout your degree and access one-on-one research mentoring by criminology experts through the Criminology Undergraduate Research Internship Program.

Advance your leadership potential with a Master of Business and gain specialist strategic expertise aligned to your career goals.   • Refine your professional identity, expand your networks and strengthen your ability to lead innovation within organisations.

description:
Queensland's #1 university for AI research. (ShanghaiRanking's Global Ranking of Academic Subjects, tied position, 2026)

Study science at Griffith and turn your curiosity into a career, with the hands-on experience, support and flexibility to make your degree your own. The Bachelor of Science is designed to help you think critically, solve complex problems and make discoveries that shape the way we live. With a wide choice of majors and electives, you can explore multiple disciplines or focus deeply on one area-from understanding the building blocks of life and protecting ecosystems, to exploring the universe or developing new technologies-with the freedom to switch or combine majors as your interests evolve.

Study science where nature is your classroom: our campuses are living laboratories, offering direct access to bushland, waterways and marine ecosystems, with sustainability embedded throughout your studies. Through strong industry and research connections, you'll have opportunities to build professional experience through placements, internships and innovative research projects. By the time you graduate, you'll have the knowledge, networks and job-ready skills employers value and the confidence to apply them.

  • Shape your degree your way with multiple majors and electives, flexible study pathways and the freedom to mix disciplines or customise your career direction.
  • Learn in world-class, accessible facilities with specialist equipment, advanced laboratories and field sites across living-lab campuses.
  • Develop practical, employer-valued skills from day one through hands-on lab work, field experiences, internships, placements and projects that tackle real scientific challenges.
  • Feel supported every step of the way with smaller classes, peer networks, approachable staff, tailored academic support and mentoring, with bridging courses available if you need to strengthen your science foundations.

  • Eligible students can pursue an honours year featuring a major research project, opening pathways to PhD study and research careers.
Tackle the world's biggest challenges

Learn alongside leading researchers while contributing to real scientific projects that make a difference. From advancing medical breakthroughs and tackling infectious disease, to developing quantum technologies and addressing global environmental challenges, you'll gain hands-on experience solving problems that matter, supported by strong industry and research partnerships.

Applied Mathematics - Available at Gold Coast and Brisbane South (Nathan) - Turn numbers into real solutions, from modelling natural systems to tackling engineering challenges, with skills that lead to careers in tech, science, data and beyond.

Archaeology - Available at Brisbane South (Nathan) - Uncover humanity's past through artefacts, landscapes and science, gaining hands-on experience that prepares you for careers in research, heritage and cultural analysis.

Biochemistry - Available at Gold Coast - Examine biomolecular structure, metabolism, cellular function and clinical processes while building practical laboratory skills through advanced biotechniques and organic chemistry.

Queensland's #1 university for economics. (ShanghaiRanking's Global Ranking of Academic Subjects 2026)

Step into the fast-paced world of commerce, where financial insight meets strategic thinking. Whether you want to advise global businesses, drive economic growth or manage your own enterprise, the Bachelor of Commerce equips you with the knowledge, confidence and practical experience to succeed in accounting, finance and economics.

Highlights of studying the Bachelor of Commerce
  • Learn the core skills that employers demand like financial literacy, data analysis, problem-solving and communication, while exploring key areas such as accounting principles, economic theory and business management.
  • Develop a future-focused mindset as you learn from industry leaders.
  • Gain experience through practical projects and real case studies to boost your employment prospects.
  • Our degrees are designed with business professionals, ensuring you graduate with current knowledge and skills that are directly relevant to the business sector.
  • Access programs like BusinessPLUS for mentoring, networking, professional development and work opportunities.
  • Broaden your horizons through international exchange or study tours with 120+ partner universities in 70+ countries.
Globally recognised

We're part of the top 1% of universities worldwide who are accredited by both the International Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business (AACSB) and the European Foundation for Management Development Quality Improvement System (EQUIS). You'll receive a globally recognised education that opens doors to opportunities in Australia and beyond.

Majors

Tailor your degree to your career goals by choosing from majors (or second majors) in:

Economics: Gain the skills to analyse real-world economic issues using both theory and data. You'll learn to evaluate policies and business decisions with tools like cost-benefit analysis, macroeconomic and microeconomic models and econometric techniques. You'll be ready to apply these skills to global economic challenges, from open economy dynamics to empirical research projects.

Accounting: Learn how to analyse, interpret and report financial information for organisations across industries. You'll gain practical skills in managerial accounting, auditing, taxation, sustainability reporting and financial statement preparation, while learning to apply theory to real business decisions. You'll be equipped to support strategic planning, ensure compliance and provide insights that drive effective financial management.

Finance: Gain an understanding of how to analyse, manage and optimise investments in the global financial environment. You'll learn to evaluate derivatives, construct and manage investment portfolios, and assess global markets, while applying sustainable finance principles to make responsible decisions. Graduates are equipped to pursue careers in investment analysis, portfolio management, financial risk management and sustainable finance roles.

Financial Planning: Learn how to provide expert advice on personal finances, investments, superannuation and retirement planning. You'll develop practical skills in risk management, insurance, taxation and estate planning, preparing you to create tailored financial strategies for clients. You'll be ready for careers as a financial planner, wealth adviser or retirement and estate planning specialist.

Financial Crime Investigation and Compliance: Gain the skills to prevent, detect and investigate financial crime across organisations and institutions. You'll gain expertise in forensic accounting, fraud and cybercrime, data analysis and visualisation, and environmental criminology to understand how crime occurs and how to stop it. You'll be prepared to work in financial crime investigation, compliance, fraud prevention or risk management within banks, government agencies and corporate organisations.

Honours 

Stand out with the Bachelor of Advanced Commerce (Honours) (1676), which includes an additional year of study designed to refine your research and analytical expertise. These are skills highly sought after in today's competitive job market. You can enrol from the start or transfer into the honours program if eligible.

description:
Prepare for a career as a clinical psychologist. Through a combination of rigorous coursework, applied research and extensive professional placements, you'll develop advanced assessment, intervention and therapeutic skills while building the professional confidence and ethical practice required of a registered clinical psychologist.

Highlights of studying the Master of Clinical Psychology
  • Complete over 1,000 hours of professional placements in Griffith University clinics and partner organisations, including rural, regional and external settings.
  • Gain direct experience managing therapeutic caseloads, both individually and in groups.
  • Develop expertise in assessment, diagnosis, formulation, neuropsychology and evidence-based interventions.
  • Apply advanced research methods to clinical projects, building skills in critical evaluation and independent research.
  • Learn from highly experienced academics and practising psychologists, with close supervision and mentoring.
  • Prepare for eligibility for full registration with the Psychology Board of Australia or entry into the Registrar program for clinical psychology.
Practical learning for clinical practice 

From your first placements in the Griffith University Psychology Clinic to external practicum experiences, you'll integrate theory and practice to develop competence in psychological assessment, therapy and professional decision-making. The degree's applied focus ensures you gain the clinical confidence, ethical awareness and practical expertise to provide high-quality care.

Provisional registration as a psychologist with the Psychology Board of Australia 

It is a requirement that students enrolled in this degree have and maintain either provisional or full registration as a Psychologist with the Psychology Board of Australia via the Australian Health Practitioner Regulation Agency (Ahpra) for the duration of the program.

This degree has been designed to meet the requirements for eligibility for full registration with the Psychology Board of Australia and entry to the Registrar program for the area of practice endorsement in clinical psychology. Completion of the degree also meets the requirements for associate membership of the Australian Psychological Society's College of Clinical Psychologists.

You may also wish to consider the Doctor of Philosophy in Clinical Psychology (6028) which has a substantially larger research component than the Master of Clinical Psychology.

description:
Want to help people and drive change at a local, national or global level? Feel passionate about social justice and human rights? Study our Bachelor of Social Work and be the change that helps people and communities when they need it most.

The Bachelor of Social Work equips you with the tools to turn your passion into a rewarding career. You'll learn how to work effectively with individuals, families, and communities, helping people navigate complex challenges and advocating for human rights and social justice. With a strong foundation in ethics, human behaviour, social policy and programs, you'll graduate prepared to lead positive change across sectors such as mental health, child protection, aged care, disability services, homelessness, First Nations support and more.

Highlights of studying the Bachelor of Social Work

  • Learn from teaching staff with deep industry expertise and experience in fields such as mental health, domestic violence, disability, child protection and advocacy.
  • Explore key areas of social work including counselling, group work, community development, social policy, ethics, program evaluation and human rights.
  • Gain strong foundations in human development, equity and diversity, and the social systems that shape people's lives.
  • Flexible options may be available for those already working in the field, including recognition of prior learning or workplace-based placements.

Real-world experience that prepares you for practice

You'll complete two professional field placements during your degree, gaining 1,000 hours of supervised experience in the sector. You'll be supervised by a qualified social worker for the duration of both field placements, providing you with the opportunity to strengthen your professional skills, apply your academic knowledge, and experience social work practice in the real world. Whether you're working with a hospital team, a community organisation, or in child protection, domestic violence, disability services, or mental health, you'll build the skills to make a genuine difference in people's lives.

Learn with purpose, graduate with impact

This degree will empower you to become a compassionate and capable practitioner who can navigate complex social issues and advocate for vulnerable populations. You'll be part of a profession committed to justice, inclusion, and ethical practice. You'll graduate ready to lead in diverse roles across the public, private and community sectors, at local and international levels.

description:
Make an impact in your community as a social work practitioner. At Griffith, we value your commitment to making a difference. This professional qualifying degree builds on your lived experiences, equipping you with the expertise, practical skills and ethical grounding to become a confident advocate for those most in need.

You'll graduate ready to make an impact, support individuals, families and groups, strengthen communities and lead meaningful change across social and human services.

Highlights of studying the Master of Social Work
  • Study courses in social work practice, research, First Peoples and social justice, counselling, ethics and leadership, human rights, law, policy and group facilitation.
  • Gain an Australian Association of Social Workers (AASW) accredited qualification, meeting Australian Social Work Education and Accreditation Standards (ASWEAS).
  • Develop as an ethical, innovative thinker, communicator and leader, ready to drive positive change in complex professional environments.
Build practical skills through social work field placements

Start making a difference while you study and apply your learning through two extensive field placements. You'll complete a minimum 1,000 hours of practice-based learning in human service organisations, guided by qualified social work supervisors.

Across both placements, you'll progressively develop the skills, knowledge and professional mindset required for effective practice. The first 500-hour placement introduces you to the realities of the profession, while the second 500-hour placement builds on this foundation with more advanced responsibilities and deeper critical reflection. Placements are designed so you'll gain the confidence and capability to graduate as a skilled, socially responsible practitioner ready to make an impact in diverse social work settings.

description:
Queensland's #1 university for marine and ocean engineering. (ShanghaiRanking's Global Ranking of Academic Subjects 2026)

Turn your passion for the ocean into a career with real impact. Study where the ocean meets the classroom at our Gold Coast campus and combine cutting-edge research with hands-on fieldwork in some of Australia's most iconic marine environments. With direct access to Moreton Bay, Gold Coast waterways and Heron Island, you'll gain practical experience in a living laboratory - building the skills and networks that open doors in marine science careers worldwide.

Through a broad, interdisciplinary curriculum spanning marine biology, chemistry and physical sciences, you'll graduate as a well-rounded marine science professional ready to meet industry needs. With strong industry links and opportunities to join research projects and sustainability initiatives, you'll graduate with confidence, experience and professional connections.

Highlights of studying the Bachelor of Marine Science
  • Tackle critical ocean challenges such as climate change, pollution and sustainable fisheries management, supporting healthy marine ecosystems and industries.
  • Small cohorts, approachable lecturers and a supportive learning community ensure you're guided every step of the way.
  • Develop practical skills through hands-on experience with industry-relevant tools and approaches, including GIS, ecological modelling, environmental economics and data analysis.
  • Gain valuable professional experience through marine industry placement in areas such as fisheries, aquaculture, marine conservation, coastal management or coastal engineering.
  • Build a strong science foundation in your first year before customising your studies and specialising in your area of passion in second and third year, with the flexibility to switch majors.
  • Participate in extensive fieldwork at unforgettable locations including Heron Island, Stradbroke Island, Moreton Bay and Gold Coast waterways such as Tallebudgera Creek, Burleigh Headlands, Hastings Point and the Broadwater.
Lead the way in marine science

Environmental scientists are in high demand across every sector, and this degree opens pathways well beyond marine science alone. You'll develop versatile, future-focused skills valued globally, from marine fieldwork and ecological monitoring to data analysis and applied research. Studying at Griffith's Gold Coast campus - surrounded by beaches, wetlands and diverse coastal systems - gives you immediate access to real-world learning opportunities guided by leading researchers and educators. 

Our marine science program is highly regarded, with strong industry recognition and collaborations that enhance your employability. Through research projects, volunteering and student societies, you'll build professional networks that support your career long after graduation.

Honours 

From the end of your third year, eligible students can apply for an honours program and complete an honours research project. You'll apply your skills in real marine environments through unique experiences that strengthen pathways into research and advanced marine science careers.

Majors 

Marine and coastal conservation: Learn how to understand and protect vulnerable ocean and shoreline ecosystems. You'll study the dynamics of sandy beaches, wetlands, coral reefs and other key habitats, particularly those along Australia's eastern coast. You'll explore the impacts of pollution, climate change and human development while gaining practical skills in ecosystem modelling, GIS mapping, environmental monitoring and resource management.  

With practical experience through fieldwork and lab activities, you'll be prepared for careers in marine conservation, coastal planning, environmental policy or ecosystem restoration. If you're passionate about sustaining our oceans for future generations, this major offers the knowledge and tools to make a real difference.

Marine chemistry and biotechnology: Explore the chemical makeup of marine environments and the innovative use of marine organisms in science, industry and conservation. Study topics like aquatic chemistry, environmental pollutants, marine biodiscovery and the advanced analytical techniques used to assess ecosystem health and unlock bioactive compounds from the ocean.

Gain practical skills through fieldwork and lab-based training in spectroscopy, ecotoxicology, water quality testing and chemical analysis. You'll be prepared for roles in environmental monitoring, pharmaceuticals, marine biotechnology or coastal water management.

Marine ecology: Explore the intricate relationships between marine organisms and their environments, from coastal wetlands to coral reefs and open oceans. You'll examine topics like estuarine dynamics, reef biodiversity, marine megafauna and ecological monitoring, alongside the impacts of pollution, habitat loss and climate change.

Combine fieldwork, lab experience, and ecological theory to develop skills in research, species monitoring and conservation strategy. You'll gain firsthand experience in coastal and offshore ecosystems-including humpback whale surveys-and study how human and environmental factors shape marine systems. Ideal for those passionate about protecting marine life, this major opens pathways into research, conservation, marine park management and ecological consultancy.

description:
From Trimester 1 2027, the primary pathway for admission to the Bachelor of Film and Screen Media Production is via ATAR/Rank.

Applicants who achieve an ATAR/Rank of 75.00 (or higher) are guaranteed admission into the program for 2027. ATAR/Rank Guarantees apply until the main offer round in December and/or until places are filled.

Develop your skills as an innovative content creator with access to state-of-the-art facilities, strong industry connections and embedded engagement opportunities. In the Bachelor of Film and Screen Media Production, you'll learn to collaborate in teams to bring your vision to life, while building a solid foundation in film history, practice, critical analysis and emerging technologies like virtual production.

This hands-on, production-focused degree provides the skills, knowledge and studio experience to thrive in a dynamic, competitive and constantly evolving field.

Highlights of studying the Bachelor of Film and Screen Media Production
  • Learn by doing in our on-campus film production facilities, with access to high-end, industry-grade digital cinema cameras and dollies, LED lighting and sound recording equipment.
  • Develop your skills and your own vision alongside a cohort of inspired, collaborative Griffith Film School students from a range of creative disciplines.
  • Showcase your work in film festivals and awards and collaborate with animators and game designers from Griffith Film School, creatives from the Queensland College of Art and Design and musicians from Queensland Conservatorium.
  • Take your creativity on the road, with the option to undertake various domestic and international study tours.
Create in facilities designed for the future of film

Work on sound stage, multi-camera, motion capture and virtual production projects. Complete them in our post-production suites and recording studios, then host viewings in our own 95-seat cinema.

Industry focus

Take advantage of our workshop, seminar and master class programs delivered by local and international experts.

Griffith Film School is an active member of, and has a strong reputation within, the World Film School Association (CILECT), a group of 160 International Film Schools, as well as other international partners including:

  • APSA
  • NEP Group
  • World Congress of Science and Factual Producers
  • Gobelins L'école De L'image
  • BFA.

These industry links and international connections mean you'll have the opportunity to practise the art of filmmaking under the guidance of the best in the world and make critical contacts that you'll draw upon at university and beyond.

Majors
Film production

Prepare for the modern production landscape by developing advanced skills in cameras, lighting, sound and editing tools, enabling you to transform scripts into captivating visual narratives.

Streaming television

Gain experience in the dynamic landscape of digital streaming and television. You'll learn how to leverage various platforms, analyse industry trends and audiences, and develop content, while refining your skills in single and multi-camera studio and location productions.

Writing and development

Write and develop ideas for any screen medium, from linear screenplays to narrative design.

Virtual production and VFX

Discover how to create content through innovative virtual production methods, including motion capture, LED wall technology, photogrammetry, camera tracking and virtual lighting through real-time game engines.

3D art and environments

Learn to interpret visual concepts and artistic styles to create appealing 3D characters, props, vehicles, and environments for games, film and animation.

Post-production

Develop skills in the creative application of advanced compositing techniques including animated typography, motion graphics and green screen concepts, as well as mastering compositing workflows, colour correction and node-based compositing tools.

description:
Empower communities and transform lives through health knowledge. Health science provides an understanding of the human body and the science underpinning being a health practitioner. This degree provides a high level of flexibility with a range of majors leading to many rewarding career paths.

With five-star ratings for skills development, student support and teaching quality*, you'll be equipped to take advantage of a growing job market or further health specialisation.

Highlights of studying the Bachelor of Health Science
  • In your first year, explore health issues and build a solid foundation in human biology including chemistry, cell biology, anatomy, physiology, genetics, microbiology, health management, nutrition, infection and toxicology.
  • Expand your knowledge in years two and three, refining your skills in analysis, evaluation, and communication. 
  • Tailor your studies by selecting a major, as well as a wide range of electives.
  • Take advantage of our connections for industry placements and practical experience.
Industry connections and experience

The BioHealth Projects capstone course provides an authentic learning experience, working directly with industry partners on real projects. As a final-year Health Science student, you'll apply your knowledge to solve practical problems, while building valuable connections for your future career.

You'll gain practical experience, develop your problem-solving and project management skills, and receive mentorship from both industry professionals and Griffith staff. It's a great opportunity to showcase your skills, enhance your CV, and work on projects that could lead to future job opportunities. As part of a diverse cohort, you'll bring together expertise across a range of health science fields. Make an impact, expand your professional network and prepare for a successful career in health and biosciences.

Study Health Science in immersive environments 

Learn in state-of-the-art facilities, with immersive simulated teaching environments, virtual reality technology and clinical labs. We've invested in world-class research, facilities and some of Australia's most highly awarded academics. When you choose to study health science at Griffith, you're joining a forward-thinking, future-ready university that shares your passion for making a difference that matters.

*Good Universities Guide (2024)

Majors

Data Management and Analytics: Gain the skills to transform complex health data into meaningful insights. You'll learn to collect, process, visualise and analyse data from sources such as electronic records and social media, using modern analytics tools to support evidence-based decision-making in health environments.

Health Communication: Learn how to effectively communicate complex health and science information to diverse audiences across a range of platforms. With a focus on media relations, ethical and legal frameworks, crisis communication and global storytelling, you'll develop the practical and strategic skills needed to influence public understanding and support informed decision-making.

Pharmaceutical Science: Build a strong foundation in the science of drug action, formulation and delivery, combining key principles from chemistry, biology and pharmacology. Learn how medicines are developed, how they interact with the body and how they are safely and effectively delivered.

Honours

The Bachelor of Health Science (Honours) (2101) is available as an additional year of study.

description:
Take the final step towards a career as a registered dentist with the Master of Dentistry. Building on the knowledge and skills developed in the Bachelor of Dental Health Science, this program provides the professional training required to apply for registration as a dentist in Australia. 

Note: students can only enter this program if they have successfully completed the Bachelor of Dental Health Science (or the Bachelor of Oral Health in Dental Science) at Griffith University.

Highlights of studying the Master of Dentistry
  • Develop specialist skills in dentistry, including oral surgery, orthodontics, prosthodontics, periodontics, paediatrics and special needs dentistry.
  • Refine clinical techniques and simulate private practice to build confidence managing patients in real-world settings.
  • Lead innovation through a group research project, analysing and applying emerging knowledge in dental science.
Exciting clinical placements 

Gain advanced clinical and research expertise in oral health through placements in metropolitan, regional and rural communities. You'll work in diverse community settings across Queensland, providing much-needed services while preparing for the realities of dental practice.

You may also undertake extensive clinical work in our purpose-built Griffith Dental Clinic. Through a combination of simulated practice, applied learning and research, you'll graduate with the confidence and expertise to provide high-quality patient care across a wide range of clinical contexts.

Build precision, compassion and confidence in dental care 

Dentistry involves blending clinical precision with compassionate patient care. Throughout your studies, you'll learn how to diagnose, manage and treat complex dental conditions while building strong communication and problem-solving skills essential for professional practice.

description:
This degree will commence in Trimester 1, 2027.

This degree is pending dual accreditation with the Queensland College of Teachers (QCT) and the Australian Children's Education & Care Quality Authority (ACECQA).

Everyone has that one teacher who believed in them. Be that teacher - one who inspires confidence, nurtures curiosity and helps shape a brighter future for the next generation.

This dual qualification prepares you to become an early childhood teacher and primary school teacher. You'll gain the skills and experience to make a difference across early learning and primary education settings.

Highlights of studying the Bachelor of Early Childhood and Primary Education
  • Stand out with a four-year dual qualification recognised and valued by the education sector. Designed to meet the growing need for high-quality teachers, this degree opens the door to a rewarding career supporting children's learning, development and success.
  • A shared foundation year prepares you for your chosen degree: Bachelor of Early Childhood and Primary Education, Bachelor of Primary Education, or Bachelor of Secondary Education. The foundation year introduces key educational theories and includes your first professional experience.
  • Benefit from our strong relationships with schools and industry partners. During your degree, you'll undertake a total of 110 days of supervised professional experience organised by the placement team.
  • Once the degree is accredited, graduates will be eligible to apply for Queensland teacher registration and will be qualified to teach in both early childhood settings and primary schools.
Create safe, inclusive and supportive learning environments

Teacher education at Griffith University has a focus on wellbeing, inclusive education and child safety, ensuring you enter classrooms and early childhood settings with the skills and confidence to make a difference.

In line with our belief that education should be for everyone, you'll develop strategies and resources to support learners from diverse academic, cultural and personal backgrounds. You'll explore the importance of building strong partnerships with families, understand the frameworks that guide early childhood practice, and develop knowledge of young children's learning and development.

Throughout your studies, you'll build your confidence to plan, deliver and evaluate meaningful learning experiences aligned with curriculum requirements, early childhood learning frameworks and the Queensland Kindergarten Learning Guideline. You'll graduate with the practical skills and professional knowledge to support children's growth, learning and wellbeing across early childhood and primary education settings.

Meet your mathematics entry prerequisite

Ready to study a teaching degree but don't have the mathematics entry prerequisite? Successfully completing Griffith's Bridging Maths for Aspiring Educators course will meet your mathematics entry requirements for entry into our education degree and you could start your studies in the next available trimester. This course is delivered over six weeks in on-campus and online modes.

description:
Join one of Australia's leading music schools and develop the skills to become a versatile and creative musician, ready to make your mark and enter professional life. In the Bachelor of Music, you'll explore your chosen specialisation while being immersed in diverse styles including classical, contemporary, jazz, popular, electronic, experimental and world music.

Highlights of studying the Bachelor of Music
  • Audition for multiple instruments or specialisations and grow your skills across different musical and creative areas.
  • From your first year, you'll refine your artistry through performance, collaboration and critical listening, laying the groundwork to succeed in the evolving music industry.
  • Explore diverse styles and choose majors from your second year: performance, contemporary creative practices, production and entrepreneurship, or community education.
  • Further develop your artistry through expert mentorship, studio training and live performance opportunities across multiple genres.
Discover your potential at Queensland Conservatorium 

Study at Queensland Conservatorium Griffith University and discover your artistic identity in a welcoming and supportive environment. You'll learn from award-winning educators, perform alongside peers in ensembles and cross-genre projects and gain practical experience through internships, music industry collaborations and project-based studies.

With access to world-class facilities and global alumni networks, you'll be well positioned to transition seamlessly into a career in music, continue into further study or a graduate entry teacher preparation program.

Majors
Performance

Grow as an artist and professional by developing advanced skills in classical, contemporary and/or jazz performance. This major has a strong focus on high performance levels, effective collaboration with peers and the expression of a distinct artistic identity.

Contemporary Creative Practices

Incorporating elements of composition, creative music technology and popular music, you'll have the opportunity to create original music as a composer, digital practitioner, songwriter and/or sound artist. You'll also gain a strong grounding in the role of computing in modern music-making.

Production and Entrepreneurship

Collaborate with students from diverse disciplines, including musicians, singers, performers, composers, engineers and producers, to bring works to life, whether on the stage, film, online or live.

Education and Community

For students seeking to develop the artistic, pedagogical, and leadership skills needed to guide participatory music-making in schools, community organisations, and public cultural settings.

Step into a rewarding career transforming lives with the Master of Speech Pathology. This program equips you with the advanced knowledge, clinical skills and professional experience required to become a competent, evidence-based speech pathologist. Develop critical thinking and problem-solving skills through small-group, problem-based learning.

Build confidence and competence via hands-on, workplace-based placements in hospitals, schools, aged care and private practice.

Collaborate with allied health professionals, including occupational therapists, dietitians and physiotherapists, to deliver holistic, person-centred care.

Practical, inquiry-based learning

description:
Develop expertise in physical, biomedical, and psychological sciences to launch your career in exercise science. Learn the role of exercise in health maintenance and rehabilitation and how it can be applied to create interventions that improve health, fitness, wellbeing and performance.

Highlights of studying the Bachelor of Exercise Science
  • Study courses in anatomy, physiology, psychology, biomechanics, nutrition and more.
  • Learn how the body moves and how to assess human performance through exercise.
  • Build skills to boost performance, prevent injuries, manage health risks and promote the benefits of exercise.
  • Gain experience through placements in our on-campus clinics, or with big names like Swimming Australia, Gold Coast Titans and Queensland Academy of Sport.
  • Graduate ready for careers in sport, health, fitness and rehab, or continue into further study like physiotherapy or clinical physiology.
Learn to lead in collaborative care

The best outcomes for patients and health professionals rely on a collaborative, inclusive approach to health. At Griffith, we prepare you for the future of healthcare by learning alongside students and staff from the full range of clinical areas, building crucial skills for multidisciplinary teams.

The Gold Coast's home of health

Griffith Health has a major presence within the Gold Coast Health and Knowledge Precinct, across the road from the Gold Coast University Hospital. Our state-of-the-art labs provide an unrivalled learning experience, including our $150 million Griffith Health Centre, immersive virtual learning environment, and on-site professional clinics for student placements in allied health, occupational and physical therapy labs for practical experience.

Placements may also be available in Northern NSW Tweed Valley Hospital, offering the latest state-of-the-art learning and teaching hub for hands-on experience.

description:
Make an impact as a medical scientist. Play a vital role in improving patient health by conducting diagnostic tests and recommending treatment options. As a medical scientist, you will perform tests on blood, tissues and other bodily fluids to help doctors diagnose a range of diseases, including glandular fever, diabetes, swine flu and cancer. You could also contribute to the success of clinical trials and advance healthcare innovations that will shape the future of medicine.

Highlights of studying the Bachelor of Medical Laboratory Science
  • Build your knowledge in core subjects like chemistry, cell biology, anatomy and physiology to understand how the body works in health and disease.
  • From second year, focus on specialised areas and learn how to diagnose diseases while building deeper knowledge in lab science.
  • In your final year, put your skills into practice with full-time clinical placements where you'll work on real medical cases and graduate job ready.
  • Enter a booming job market, projected to grow over 6.5 per cent by 2028*.
Hands-on experience across every area of medical laboratory science

Gain practical experience across all six key areas of the discipline: blood transfusion and immunology, clinical biochemistry, haematology, histopathology, microbiology and molecular diagnosis. This broad foundation ensures you are well-prepared for diagnostic work and diverse roles in healthcare, including hospital and private pathology labs, public health, blood transfusion services and research institutions.

Take your career overseas

As the only Australian medical science degree with international accreditation, this program opens global career pathways, allowing you to work in the UK and other Commonwealth countries after graduation and giving you the flexibility to take your skills wherever your career leads you.

*Jobs and Skills Australia

Queensland's #1 university for political science. (ShanghaiRanking's Global Ranking of Academic Subjects, tied position, 2026)

A Bachelor of Political Science and International Relations will provide you with a deep understanding of policy, politics and power in the domestic and international spheres. You'll learn about political movements and institutions, processes of law making, diplomacy and global politics.

Highlights of studying the Bachelor of Political Science and International Relations
  • Start your journey to becoming a global leader in politics and international relations.
  • Learn about political systems, institutions and global diplomacy, gaining a deep understanding of the forces shaping local and global politics.
  • Explore how democracy thrives, or struggles to survive, and the strategies authoritarian leaders increasingly use to maintain their grip on power.
  • Take your studies overseas with international internships, study abroad programs and global partnerships. You'll build cultural awareness, grow your professional network and gain a competitive edge for your future career.
Learn from globally recognised experts  

This degree is taught by academics who are leaders in their fields, including specialists in diplomacy, global governance and international security. Our world class teachers have links to Australian and international governments, as well as key organisations like the UN, World Bank, WTO and IMF. You'll benefit from their deep knowledge, active research and real-world policy experience, ensuring your studies are informed by the latest developments and global perspectives.

Majors

International Relations: Explore how power, conflict, cooperation and ideology shape global affairs. You'll examine the forces influencing diplomacy, security, migration, foreign policy and global governance. Courses cover theoretical frameworks and great power politics, to emerging issues like terrorism, climate change and religious resurgence.

Political Science and Public Policy: Examine how power is exercised, how decisions are made, and how political systems shape society. Explore key domestic and international issues like elections, governance, Indigenous politics, media influence and environmental policy. You'll gain a deep understanding of policy development, democratic systems and authoritarian regimes, with a strong focus on political dynamics. If you're passionate about influencing change, understanding political behaviour, or shaping public debate, this major offers the tools to become a thoughtful analyst, policymaker or advocate in the public sphere.

Security, Conflict and Human Rights: Explore how global power struggles, political violence and human rights intersect. You'll examine key issues such as terrorism, authoritarianism, human rights in global politics and the role of international organisations in peacekeeping and conflict resolution. You'll analyse the security strategies of major powers like China, investigate the rise of populism and study how governments and movements respond to threats and crises.

Enhance your studies by adding a second major:

  • Chinese Language  
  • Economics  
  • French Language*  
  • German Language*  
  • Indonesian Language*  
  • International Business 
  • International Relations 
  • Islam-West Relations  
  • Italian Language  
  • Japanese Language  
  • Korean language*
  • Political Science and Public Policy
  • Security, Conflict and Human Rights
  • Spanish Language  

*Available via cross-institutional study at the University of Queensland. These languages are offered only to students enrolled at Brisane South (Nathan).

Honours

The Bachelor of Advanced Political Science and International Relations (Honours) (1665) is available through an additional year of study.

The Brisbane South (Nathan) offering of this program is scheduled to be delivered at the Treasury Building at our Brisbane City campus in 2027. If scheduled opening is delayed, courses may be delivered all or in part at our other Brisbane locations.

Queensland's #1 university for law and criminology. (ShanghaiRanking's Global Ranking of Academic Subjects 2026)

Prepare for a rewarding legal career with Griffith's Juris Doctor, a graduate-entry program designed for students from diverse academic backgrounds. Whether your goal is to practise law, work in government or influence policy, this degree provides the knowledge, skills and practical experiences to succeed. 

Highlights of studying the Juris Doctor 
  • Future-proof your career with the option of completing a major in Canadian law, international law, or migration law.  
  • Study crime, contracts, torts, constitutional and property law while building skills in reasoning, advocacy, research and ethics. 
  • Choose from a wide range of electives that match your career aspirations ranging from environmental law, digital media, cyber law, family law, competition and consumer law, human rights and international arbitration. 
  • This program can be completed in two years by taking courses across each trimester. 
Practical legal experience from day one 

Work alongside experienced lawyers and participate in immersive, practical experiences including law clinics and the Innocence Project, where you'll apply your knowledge to real cases. These opportunities ensure you graduate with the confidence to navigate both the courtroom and complex legal systems. 

A world-class legal education

Ranked among the world's top law schools, we're recognised for our commitment to social justice, ethical practice and innovation in legal education. You'll learn from leading academics and practising lawyers who bring real-world expertise into the classroom. The Juris Doctor integrates theory with practical experience, ensuring you're not just studying the law, you're learning how to use it to create impact.

The Juris Doctor is an AQF Level 9 Masters Extended degree. 

Majors 
Canadian Law 

Prepare for legal practice in Canada's common law provinces while preparing to meet the National Committee on Accreditation (NCA) requirements. This major covers the foundations of Canadian law, Indigenous-settler legal relations and the role of law in society. Core courses in constitutional, administrative, and criminal law, plus professional responsibility, provide a strong grounding in Canada's principles, institutions and ethical frameworks. You'll graduate with the knowledge, adaptability and practical skills to pursue legal careers in Canada or internationally.

International Law 

Gain advanced knowledge of the legal frameworks, institutions and disputes that shape the global order, with a focus on applying principles in cross-border contexts. Study the United Nations, international negotiations, and build skills in diplomacy and cross-cultural dispute resolution. Core areas include international criminal, human rights, environmental and trade law. You can also tailor your studies to your specific goals and interests with specialist options including investor-state arbitration, international family law, transitional justice and cyber law. Graduates are prepared for careers in international organisations, government, NGOs, law firms and multinational corporations.  

Migration Law 

Prepare for a career in one of Australia's most complex and fast-evolving legal fields. You'll study migration law, practice, and Australia's visa system, gaining expertise in applications, legislative requirements and client advice. Office simulations embed practice in realistic scenarios, while courses in visa compliance, cancellation, review and advocacy prepare you for tribunal work, submissions and representation. Graduates are equipped for roles as migration agents, or in legal practices, government or non-government organisations.
