description:
Some courses in this program are scheduled to be offered at the Treasury Building at our Brisbane City campus in 2027. If scheduled opening is delayed, courses may be delivered all or in part at our other Brisbane locations.

Prepare to lead complex projects, manage teams and deliver innovative solutions across industries. This double degree brings together the technical depth of engineering with the strategic insight of business. With a strong focus on hands-on learning, industry experience and career-ready skills, you'll graduate with a unique combination of expertise, giving you an edge in these competitive fields.

Highlights of studying the Bachelor of Engineering (Honours)/Bachelor of Business
  • Learn by solving engineering and business challenges through practical projects, fieldwork and collaborative workshops.
  • Choose from a range of engineering and business majors to tailor your study to your interests and future career.
  • Gain extensive industry experience through placements, consulting projects and the Industry Affiliates Program.
  • Build strong networks through active student societies, field trips, mentoring and more than 150 business and industry partners.
  • Study in smaller engineering cohorts with personalised support from experienced academics and industry-connected teaching staff.
Majors

Engineering majors

  • Civil Engineering
  • Electrical and Electronic Engineering
  • Environmental Engineering
  • Electronic Engineering
  • Mechanical Engineering

Business majors

  • Logistics and Supply Chain Management
  • Management
  • Real Estate and Property Development 
Hands-on experience across disciplines 

From your first year, you'll apply engineering theory to practical problems through labs, design studios and real industry briefs. You'll learn how to collaborate in teams and see how engineering solutions work in practice. In business, you'll explore sustainability and decision-making in real scenarios, while building a strong foundation in strategy, analytics and organisational skills.

In your final year, you may complete a capstone project through the Industry Affiliates Program. This immersive experience gives you more than 400 hours working on genuine engineering and business challenges with an external organisation. You can also broaden your perspective through internships, consulting opportunities and global study experiences.

description:
Take the next step in your leadership journey and position yourself for career advancement with a Graduate Certificate in Leadership and Business Management. Designed for experienced managers without an undergraduate degree, this program builds your capability across essential areas of business while preparing you to progress into the Master of Business Administration. 

Gain a fresh perspective on leadership and management through our focus on three values that shape business success in the 21st century: responsible leadership, sustainable business practices, and a global outlook. You'll strengthen your decision-making skills, expand your understanding of business strategy and economics, and learn how to deliver outcomes that create long-term value for your organisation and society. 

Developed in conjunction with industry professionals, this degree is focused on practical organisational challenges. You'll learn about contemporary management and leadership practice and apply this knowledge to current scenarios from your workplace. 

You'll develop an understanding of the different types and purposes of teams, and learn how to boost team performance through effective leadership. You'll hone your creative thinking skills and be equipped to convert great ideas into reality through collaboration and positive risk-taking. As a graduate, you'll have the skills and knowledge to showcase your responsible leadership abilities and effectively manage transformation in your organisation. 

Highlights of studying the Graduate Certificate in Leadership and Business Management

  • Build core skills in accounting, marketing, and economics - taught through the lens of embedding sustainable business practices and social responsibility. 
  • Learn how to hone your skills in leading high impact teams, balancing performance with wellbeing and long-term success. 
  • Explore sustainability and systems thinking, and find how to integrate ethical, adaptive and resilient practices into organisational strategy. 
  • Benefit from a flexible study format designed to fit around your work and life commitments.  
  • Gain access to a pathway into the Griffith MBA, one of Australia's most respected business leadership programs. 

Study with a future-focused business school  

This program challenges conventional business thinking, giving you the tools to innovate, lead responsibly and create sustainable competitive advantage. You'll work on real case studies, apply problem-solving and critical thinking to complex challenges, and develop the skills to respond to the changing business landscape with confidence.

description:
Become a future-ready engineer and computing specialist. This double degree equips you with the practical skills, technical knowledge and industry experience to design innovative systems, solve problems and work at the forefront of emerging technologies. With hands-on learning embedded from your first year, you'll graduate ready to make your mark across industries, transforming how the world lives, works and connects.

Highlights of studying the Bachelor of Engineering (Honours) / Bachelor of Computer Science
  • Solve real industry problems through practical engineering projects, app development, systems design and computing challenges from year one.
  • Specialise in your chosen engineering field and complement it with advanced skills in AI, data science, algorithms or computing.
  • Build strong professional networks through industry placements, global mobility opportunities, collaborative research, student clubs and Griffith's active engineering and tech communities.
  • Gain experience through work-integrated learning, including major final-year capstone projects and placements with local and global partners.
  • Access world-class facilities including engineering labs, robotics spaces and the Griffith App Factory, where you can work with real clients and develop a strong professional portfolio.
  • Graduate with two in-demand qualifications recognised by industry, including Engineers Australia accreditation.
Hands-on learning across two disciplines

In engineering, you'll apply theory to practical projects, work in purpose-built facilities and collaborate through placements, research experiences and the Industry Affiliates Program. Whether you're interested in renewable energy, the development of smart systems or emerging technologies, you'll learn by doing every step of the way.

In computer science, you'll build confidence in programming, software engineering, AI, algorithms, machine learning, big data and intelligent systems. You'll tackle complex problems using modelling, design thinking and creative computational solutions, while developing the technical foundations needed to succeed in one of the world's fastest-growing industries.

Majors
Engineering majors 

Electrical and Electronic Engineering: The key role of an electrical and electronic engineer is to drive the development and application of emerging technologies, particularly in the fast-growing energy sector. These engineers collaborate with a range of professionals across industries, from civil and mechanical engineers to computer scientists. You could help integrate renewable energy into traditional systems, reducing costs, conserving energy and lowering greenhouse gas emissions.

Mechanical Engineering: With specialised skills across both electronic and mechanical engineering, mechanical engineers are prepared for work in the design, development and production of smart engineering systems and products. You will find career opportunities across many industries including manufacturing, mining, transport and defence and emerging fields such as medical and assistive technology, smart cities, precision agriculture and robotics.

Computer Science majors

Algorithms and Computing: With a focus on the design, analysis, and implementation of efficient computational solutions, this major explores advanced programming in C++, deep learning, AI, systems programming and the theoretical foundations of computation. You'll gain the skills to solve complex problems across domains such as cryptography, machine learning and distributed systems.

Data Science and Artificial Intelligence: Gain the skills to extract insights from complex data and build intelligent systems that can learn, reason and adapt. Through studies in machine learning, deep learning, computer vision, robotics and big data analytics, you'll learn the tools and techniques to solve real problems across industries using data-driven and AI-powered approaches.

description:

Queensland's #1 university for law and criminology. (ShanghaiRanking's Global Ranking of Academic Subjects 2026)

This double degree gives you the ultimate advantage for a future-proof career: legal knowledge backed by hands-on cyber security training. You'll gain the legal and technical skills needed to tackle some of the biggest challenges facing our digital world. From data breaches to cyber crime, online privacy to emerging tech regulation, you'll learn how to protect people, organisations and communities while understanding the laws that guide the digital age.

With a strong mix of practical learning, industry experience and engagement, you'll graduate ready to take on complex problems at the intersection of law, justice and cyber security.

Highlights of studying the Bachelor of Laws (Honours) / Bachelor of Cyber Security
  • Build a strong foundation in programming, networking, data management and system security before progressing into ethical hacking, digital forensics, cryptography, incident response and AI.
  • Explore the legal side of cyber security, including privacy law, data protection, intellectual property and cyber crime legislation.
  • Develop essential legal skills in negotiation, advocacy, legal writing and critical analysis while learning how these principles apply to digital environments.
  • Train in cutting-edge facilities like our Cyber Range and work through real simulations that mirror live cyber incidents.
  • Learn from cyber specialists trusted by government and major financial institutions, as well as practising legal academics, judges in residence and industry partners.
  • Investigate how global legal systems respond to cyber threats and emerging technologies, preparing you for careers across multiple sectors.
  • Build data analysis and visualisation skills to interpret trends in both cyber threats and legal cases.
Hands-on experience

You'll be supported to apply your learning from the very beginning. Through internships, industry projects, moots, the Griffith Legal Clinic program and our Cyber Range simulations, you'll work with real clients, real cases and real cyber incidents. These experiences help you build confidence, sharpen your problem-solving skills and develop the networks that lead to career opportunities.

description:
Build your future by combining the creative thinking of architectural design with the entrepreneurial drive of business to create inspiring and sustainable spaces that people need.

Highlights of studying the Bachelor of Architectural Design/Business
  • Combine architecture and business to graduate with unique expertise in creative, strategic and commercial decision-making.
  • Develop advanced design and problem-solving skills in small, expert-led studios, working on projects for urban, coastal and tropical contexts.
  • Build sustainable, ethical and inclusive practices for both the business and built environment sectors.
  • Learn business fundamentals including strategic decision-making, economics, communication and innovation.
  • Gain hands-on experience through design studios, industry placements and business initiatives, such as consulting projects and professional development programs.
  • Choose from a wide range of business majors in your second year.
Hands-on experience in design and enterprise 

From your first year, you'll build your creative and technical confidence through focused practice in our architectural design studios.

You'll also explore sustainable design, construction materials and architectural documentation, learning how to balance aesthetics, function and user needs. Your business courses will introduce you to purpose-driven organisations, decision-making and the future of work.

Graduate with the ability to evaluate feasibility, manage budgets, assess risk and communicate design concepts in commercial environments.

Double your opportunities 

By studying both architecture and business, you'll gain a competitive advantage in the property, construction and creative industries. You'll understand how to connect design intent with commercial realities, contributing to projects that are innovative, financially viable and needed in the market.

Your capstone course will help you develop links to industry partners, building your professional network and giving you hands-on experience before you graduate.

This degree provides a pathway to the Master of Architecture (5558), the postgraduate qualification required for those seeking to become a registered architect.

description:
Build the skills to lead across the full property and construction lifecycle, from development feasibility and investment decisions through to design coordination, project delivery, asset management and business leadership.

 This double degree combines the technical, practical and professional strengths of construction management with specialist business knowledge in real estate and property development. You will learn how buildings and infrastructure are planned, financed, delivered, managed and adapted to meet the changing needs of communities, industry and the environment.

  • You will graduate prepared for diverse careers across construction, property development, real estate, project management, consulting, government, investment and entrepreneurial ventures.

  • Access Griffith Business School's BusinessPLUS program, which offers career development opportunities including workshops, events, mentoring and tailored employability support.
  • This degree is developed in close consultation with the Real Estate Institute of Queensland, the Property Council of Australia and the Urban Development Institute of Australia.

description:
Suicide prevention in theory and practice. Explore the practical, policy and research issues in the field of suicide prevention in this graduate certificate. You'll gain a basic understanding of the key themes that emerge in suicide research and contemporary suicide prevention practice.

The foundations of suicide and its prevention are explored through examination of historical, cultural, epidemiological, and practical theory and practice elements, providing a 360-degree perspective of the phenomena and its complexities. The role of lived experience is also emphasised given the critical role of the 'voice' of those who have been impacted by suicide loss or suicidality for informing suicide and its prevention.

Industry and expert connections As a student of this program, you'll learn alongside student peers who share your interest in suicide prevention. Many will be working in the suicide prevention or mental health sectors already, allowing you to build a wider network of professional connections as you learn. You will have an opportunity to connect with people in online seminars or meetings as well as. Throughout, you will be guided through the course materials by leading experts in suicidology.

Graduate outcomes The flexibility within this degree equips you for careers in the multi-disciplinary fields of health, social sciences, education, welfare, correctional services, emergency services and volunteer-peer based suicide prevention work- force. You will also benefit from specialist capabilities, enabling employment in suicide prevention and/ or mental health workforce including policy, academia, education, and non-clinical/clinical practice-based settings.

Flexibility

Study anytime, anywhere - This degree is available online through our Digital campus, giving you more room to fit university with your work and social life.

Pursue further study

The courses in this graduate certificate may be credited towards a related graduate diploma or masters degree. Griffith's innovative Credit Precedent Database allows you to find out what credit decisions have been made in the past, which will give you an idea of what you can expect.

description:

description:
Become a leader in the planning and building of infrastructure and landscapes that shape how people live, work and thrive. By combining architecture and construction management, you'll blend creative design with project management and business skills.

Our double degree focuses on hands-on design experience, professional development and industry projects, so you can design inspiring spaces and manage its construction from concept to completion.

Highlights of studying the Bachelor of Architectural Design/Construction Management (Honours)
  • Combine the related disciplines of architectural design and construction to graduate with expertise across the entire lifecycle of any construction project.
  • Learn creative and technical skills in purpose-built design studios, working on projects in urban, coastal and tropical contexts.
  • Build your foundation in construction materials, sustainability, site operations, construction law, ethics and business management.
  • Master industry-standard software and digital technologies used for architectural documentation, procurement and project management.
  • Get professional experience with field trips and a 12-week industry placement.
  • Do a research project focused on contemporary challenges and innovations in the built environment sector.
Hands-on experience in architecture and construction

Immerse yourself in our design studios in your first year, build your creative confidence and learn how structures work, materials perform and how buildings exist in context.

As you progress, learn the technical skills and commercial knowledge to lead complex projects. You'll explore sustainable construction, project management, construction economics and contract administration.

You'll learn to balance aesthetics, functionality and environmental responsibility, using green technologies and sustainable practices to design resilient buildings.

You'll develop expertise in estimating, tendering, cost planning, procurement and site operations-critical skills to coordinate teams, manage risk and deliver projects on time and on budget.

Double your opportunities

As a graduate, you'll collaborate effectively with architects, engineers, consultants and contractors - a vital link between design vision and built reality.

Graduates can progress to the Master of Architecture (5558), the required postgraduate qualification for those seeking to become a registered architect. Combined with professional pathways in construction management, this creates flexible career opportunities across design studios, development firms and construction companies.

description:
The EmpowerED University Preparation Program provides a pathway for applicants who don't meet the formal entry requirements for an undergraduate degree at Griffith. A free, comprehensive preparatory program, EmpowerED gives you the opportunity to experience university life while building your confidence and academic study skills.

In EmpowerED, you'll gain fundamental knowledge and skills, including the essentials of critical reading, writing and referencing, in a supportive learning environment. Choose from our flexible study options: on campus or online through timetabled classes or our on-demand online program that you can work through at your own pace, in a way that works for you.

You'll be set up for success through courses covering university preparation, academic study skills, communication and academic research, and mathematics essentials. You'll even be able to start shaping your future career now with a personalised employability plan.

From start to finish, EmpowerED offers strong student support, valuable learning experiences and dedicated academic assistance to keep you engaged and motivated. Plus, when you complete the program, you'll be granted guaranteed entry to your preferred Griffith degree in the next trimester (subject to entry requirements) as well as gaining credit towards your degree.

We've built EmpowerED with you in mind to be your bridge to success. If you're ready to start your journey to uni, apply now and be empowered to achieve your academic and personal goals.

professionalAccreditation:
In Australia, professional accreditation of entry to practice engineering programs is the responsibility of Engineers Australia and is normally carried out on a five-yearly cycle. Griffith University underwent this review in August 2015.

Accreditation ensures academic institutions consistently meet national and international benchmarks and engineering graduates of an accredited program are assured membership with Engineers Australia at the relevant career grade and enjoy reciprocal privileges by equivalent professional bodies overseas.

Countries such as the United States of America, United Kingdom, Hong Kong (SAR), New Zealand, Canada, South Africa and others that are co-signatories to international agreements on joint recognition offer international recognition.

The Washington Accord, the Sydney Accord and the Dublin Accord recognise the substantial equivalence of accreditation systems and accredited programs across international boundaries at the Professional Engineer, Engineering Technologist and Engineering Associate levels respectively. Please refer to the International Engineering Alliance (IEA) website for more details.
Please see the Engineers Australia website for the most recent list of accredited programs.

description:
With this double degree, you can tackle environmental issues with knowledge across both engineering and science. With specialist skills in the social, applied and natural sciences, you'll be well prepared to find solutions to pressing environmental issues.

With a strong practical focus, you'll develop skills in the planning, design, management, construction and maintenance of engineering projects as well as a solid foundation in biological, physical and social sciences and critical analysis.

This is your opportunity to make a real difference to the big environmental issues facing the planet, bringing a fresh perspective and proven skills to the challenges ahead.

Industry and expert connections

From year one, you'll be learning from industry experts and like-minded teachers. Hands-on experience is key to this double degree, and in your final year you can enhance your knowledge through an industry-based project or placement.

Graduate outcomes

You'll have several options available when you graduate as either an engineer or an environmental scientist. This degree could lead to a career in civil, environmental, mechanical or electrical engineering. Your environmental science degree will offer up rewarding careers such as an environmental officer, environmental consultant, wildlife biologist, conservation ecologist or environmental chemist.

Majors

Changes effective for students commencing from Trimester 2 2020 onwards:

Engineering

  • Civil Engineering
  • Electrical and Electronic Engineering
  • Mechanical Engineering

Environmental Science

  • Ecology and Conservation
  • Environmental Management
  • Soil and Water Science
  • Urban Environments

Flexibility

Tailor your timetable - Even if you study full-time on-campus, you may still be able to customise your degree to suit your needs. From a range of tutorial times to online access to lectures and other course material, we're here to help you fit study in with your work and life commitments.

Global mobility

Students may be eligible to do an international field trip, organised by the academic staff. This may count towards a component of the degree. Visit Go Global Griffith for more information.

description:
Combine the creativity of industrial design with the technical precision of engineering to bring ideas to life. This double degree gives you the skills to design, develop and deliver innovative solutions that make everyday life smarter, safer and more sustainable. Learn to blend design thinking with engineering know-how to create products and systems that solve real problems.

Highlights of studying the Bachelor of Engineering (Honours)/Bachelor of Industrial Design
  • Get more than just hands-on experience; work alongside engineers and designers from day one to solve real industry challenges.
  • Learn how things work and how to make them better, from materials and mechanics to design, concept development, prototyping and project management.
  • Connect with top Queensland companies to build your skills and industry contacts.
  • Bring your ideas to life through hands-on projects, workshops and design studios that mirror professional environments.
  • Learn from experts and engineers leading the way in sustainable design and new technology.
  • Study your way with flexible timetables and the chance to travel with international field trips.
Hands-on experience from day one

Work in design studios and engineering labs where you'll tackle real industry projects and develop creative solutions to practical problems. Launch your career with a double degree that blends scientific discovery with business strategy while you study on living lab campuses where nature becomes your classroom. You'll develop the analytical mindset of a scientist and the commercial insight of a business professional preparing you to succeed across industries at the intersection of innovation, technology, sustainability and enterprise.

Whether your interests lie in protecting ecosystems, developing new technologies, tackling global health or environmental challenges or driving sustainable business practices, this double degree gives you the knowledge and practical experience to make an impact.

Highlights of studying the Bachelor of Science/Bachelor of Business
  • Build strong skills in science, data analysis, critical thinking and business strategy.
  • Tailor your degree with a wide choice of flexible science and business majors.
  • Get hands-on experience on our living lab campuses, in modern labs, in the field and through real industry projects.
  • Boost your employability with internships, research opportunities and access to 150+ industry partners.
  • Explore how science and business drive innovation across health, tech, environment and more.
  • Learn within communities that have your back, with supportive lecturers and approachable staff.
  • Take advantage of global study options, our BusinessPLUS program, mentoring and events to grow your professional network and career confidence.
Hands-on learning from day one

In your science studies, you'll be immersed in nature on our campuses, learn in labs and out in the field with access to specialist equipment, advanced analytical tools and real research environments. From marine and environmental fieldwork to genomic testing and experimental physics, you'll build the skills to engage with real scientific challenges.

In your business studies, you'll build practical experience through applied projects, business simulations, the Griffith Tax Clinic, the Student-Managed Investment Fund and internships with industry partners. Your first-year foundation courses will build confidence in problem-solving, decision-making and sustainable business strategy.

Double your opportunities

description:
Take the first step towards influencing public decisions and leading with purpose. The Bachelor of Arts/Master of Public Policy and Leadership is a four-year vertical degree that fast-tracks your pathway from undergraduate study into a specialised masters qualification, giving you a competitive edge in government, consulting and not-for-profit sectors.

Highlights of studying the Bachelor of Arts/Master of Public Policy and Leadership
  • Graduate with both a bachelors and masters degree in just four years.
  • Combine interdisciplinary arts study with advanced public policy and leadership training.
  • Build practical skills in research, writing, analysis and project management.
  • Engage in internships, industry projects and real case studies.
  • Learn from leading researchers and experienced practitioners in government and international relations.
Build the foundations, lead the change

In the Bachelor of Arts, you'll build work-ready skills in critical thinking, research, communication and analysis while choosing from a wide variety of majors. You'll develop cultural awareness and a deep understanding of social, political and economic systems preparing you to navigate complex local and global challenges.

You'll progress seamlessly into the Master of Public Policy and Leadership, where you'll gain advanced expertise in policy analysis, program evaluation, public administration, leadership and strategic planning. Learn how decisions are made, how public institutions operate and how to lead with integrity in complex environments. Develop capabilities in data analysis, stakeholder engagement, advocacy and evidence-based decision-making that are highly valued across the public sector and beyond.

Real experience and professional networks

Work-integrated learning is embedded throughout this degree. You'll collaborate with industry partners, undertake internships and apply your knowledge to contemporary policy challenges. These experiences help you build a professional network and practical portfolio before you graduate, enhancing your employability in public policy careers.

Become a global politics expert with a Graduate Certificate in International Relations. Designed for professionals seeking to deepen their understanding of international affairs, you'll learn the analytical, research and policy skills to work effectively in international relations.

Highlights of studying the Graduate Certificate in International Relations
  • Develop advanced knowledge of international security, diplomacy, global governance and political economy.
  • Explore contemporary global issues including human rights, religion and identity politics, environment and development.
  • Learn critical thinking, academic writing and research skills for postgraduate success.
  • Engage with practitioner-focused learning and real case studies.
  • Graduate with a postgraduate qualification in just one year of part-time study.
Deepen your understanding of global politics

You'll begin with a strong foundation in international relations theory, history and key concepts such as power, order, justice, peace and diplomacy. Through scenario-based workshops and experiential learning, you'll explore defence strategy, economic diplomacy and the practical realities of international negotiation. You'll also analyse pressing global challenges, from sustainable development and environmental pressures to the evolving relationship between government and business in a globalised economy.

A pathway to further study 

Whether you're returning to university, changing career direction, or preparing for a masters degree, this graduate certificate offers a supported and flexible entry into postgraduate study, with completed courses often gaining credit toward the full masters degree.

description:
The Diploma of Applied Financial Advice is a pathway program designed to help you transition into the Financial Adviser Standards approved program, Bachelor of Applied Financial Advice. You'll develop foundational knowledge and skills in a supportive learning environment, setting you up for success in your future studies.

As an emerging profession, financial advice continues to evolve, with a shift towards progressive, innovative workplace practices to manage the needs of clients and financial advice businesses in the context of dynamic financial markets, financial technology, regulation and beyond. You will be exposed to modern business practices, such as adaptability, creativity, diversity, and sustainability, along with foundational theoretical and technical financial planning knowledge. The Diploma of Applied Financial Advice focuses on learning by doing, developing your communication skills and professional competencies to enable you to take advantage of the increasing employment opportunities ahead in financial advice and broader business contexts.

You'll study an academic foundation course that prepares you for your university studies, as well as courses on the purpose of business and grand challenges for business, with additional support and access to a dedicated First Year Coordinator and (PASS), run by high-achieving students. You'll also complete courses introducing you to the financial planning process, ethics, technology and regulatory environment and the various areas of financial advice including investments, insurance and risk management, and superannuation and retirement.

description:
This degree is designed to empower you to excel in the global English language teaching field. Gain the skills to teach English to speakers of other languages effectively, and be prepared to step into leadership roles, guiding teams and shaping the future of language education worldwide.

Highlights of studying the Master of Teaching English to Speakers of Other Languages and Leadership
  • Study twelve TESOL courses (1.5 years) with a focus on teaching English, plus four additional courses (0.5 years) covering global business, educational leadership and international education-giving you a well-rounded skill set for success in the global teaching industry.
  • Study courses like Wellbeing, Global Business Strategy, Corporate Entrepreneurship, and Marketing Foundations, preparing you for roles in diverse educational settings.
  • Acquire skills in guiding educational initiatives, navigating global teaching challenges and integrating sustainable business practices.
  • Understand how second and foreign languages are learned in a variety of contexts with a strong focus on the Asia-Pacific region.
  • Undertake an internship, in which you'll practice English language classroom teaching.

An alternative, shorter 1.5-year Master of Teaching English to Speakers of Other Languages (5757) is also available.

Please note that this program does not lead to teacher registration with the Queensland College of Teachers.

BUILD A BODY OF RESEARCH.

Following on from the Bachelor of Sport Development, this Honours degree allows you to undertake advanced study and supervised research work. You'll delve deeper into the specialisation you've chosen and work within a team of other like-minded students and academics to further your research. 

Industry and expert connections

We've designed this Honours degree to give you the teamwork skills required for further research. Graduate outcomes

description:
Some courses in this program are scheduled to be offered at the Treasury Building at our Brisbane City campus in 2027. If scheduled opening is delayed, courses may be delivered all or in part at our other Brisbane locations.

Designed for future problem-solvers, this double degree brings together scientific knowledge, analytical thinking and the technical skills needed to understand and respond to complex environmental challenges. As global datasets grow and environmental issues become increasingly data driven, you'll be equipped with the tools to interpret information, make evidence-based decisions and contribute to meaningful change.

You'll benefit from flexible study pathways, tailored academic support and mentoring as you develop practical skills in unique natural environments. At Griffith, you'll learn in a living lab, as our campuses are surrounded by bushland, waterways and marine ecosystems, giving you direct exposure to real environmental systems with sustainability and environmental responsibility embedded throughout your studies.

Highlights of studying the Bachelor of Environmental Science/Bachelor of Data Science
  • Learn how to collect, analyse and interpret environmental data using industry-standard modelling, programming and visualisation tools.
  • Build strong foundations in environmental systems through extensive fieldwork and practical learning, including labs, ecology surveys, water and soil studies, GIS and immersive field trips.
  • Gain hands-on experience through applied research, industry projects, internships and opportunities to learn in living labs and unique environments, from bushland and waterways on our very own campuses to fieldwork on Heron Island.
  • Develop in-demand data and analytical capabilities valued by employers across government, industry and research.
  • Study an interdisciplinary curriculum spanning ecology, chemistry, data science, management and policy, supported by our long-standing expertise in environmental science education.
Double your opportunities with hands-on learning

Your studies in environmental science begin with core scientific courses and progress into areas such as biodiversity, climate change, water resources, environmental modelling, data analytics and land management. Fieldwork and practical learning are embedded throughout your degree, helping you make a real impact through sustainability and environmental problem-solving and ensuring you are career-ready.

In your data science studies, you'll develop technical and analytical capabilities in programming, machine learning, statistics, data wrangling and predictive modelling. You'll work with real datasets, build solutions to authentic industry challenges and learn how data can inform decisions that protect environments and support sustainable policy.

In your final year, you'll complete a capstone project, with the option to engage in research, undertake extended fieldwork in your major or complete an industry placement. Supported by strong industry and research connections, you'll graduate with in-demand skills, professional networks and accreditation and training aligned with industry expectations, easing the transition into roles in conservation, policy and research.

Majors

Choose from a range of majors to tailor your degree:

Ecology and Conservation - explore ecosystems, biodiversity and conservation science through practical ecological surveys and monitoring. Available at Gold Coast and Brisbane South (Nathan).

Environmental Chemistry - investigate the chemical processes that shape natural systems and pollutants, with advanced lab and analytical skills. Available at Gold Coast and Brisbane South (Nathan).

Soil and Water Science - study the management of Australia's critical soil and water resources through fieldwork, catchment studies and ecology. Available at Brisbane South (Nathan) only.

Urban and Social Environments - examine the relationship between people, cities and nature, with a focus on sustainability, planning and community engagement. Available at Gold Coast and Brisbane South (Nathan).

Tackle the legal, social and scientific challenges of our world. This double degree combines legal knowledge with a deep understanding of environmental systems, preparing you to make a real impact. You'll gain the skills to influence policy, protect natural resources and drive change, supported by hands-on science projects and strong industry connections across both disciplines.

Highlights of studying the Bachelor of Laws (Honours)/Bachelor of Environmental Science
  • Develop in-depth knowledge of legal principles and practices while connecting law to ethics, Indigenous issues and global perspectives, preparing you to navigate complex regulatory and policy environments.
  • Gain practical legal skills in negotiation, advocacy, critical analysis, research and legal writing.
  • Explore environmental systems, sustainability, policy and management through an interdisciplinary curriculum spanning ecology, chemistry, data science, management and policy.
  • Choose from specialised environmental science majors to shape your degree, supported by tailored academic advice, mentoring and approachable lecturers who guide you every step of the way.
  • Learn in a living lab as our campuses are surrounded by bushland, waterways and marine ecosystems.
Environmental Science majors

Ecology and Conservation - Explore ecosystems, biodiversity and conservation science through hands-on ecological surveys and monitoring. Available at Gold Coast and Brisbane City.

Environmental Chemistry - Investigate the chemical processes that shape natural systems and pollutants, using industry-aligned analytical tools and advanced laboratory skills. Available at Gold Coast and Brisbane City.

Soil and Water Science - Study the management of Australia's critical soil and water resources through fieldwork, catchment studies and environmental research. Available at Brisbane City only.

Urban and Social Environments - Examine the relationship between people, cities and nature, with a focus on sustainability, planning and community engagement. Available at Gold Coast and Brisbane City.

Make an impact with industry-backed experience 

Gain experience and build professional connections through our strong industry and research partnerships that open doors to networking, volunteering and valuable experience across government, NGOs, legal professionals and environmental organisations.

In law, you'll have access to hands-on learning through moots, court visits and the Griffith Legal Clinic program. In environmental science, you'll study where nature is your classroom, undertake fieldwork, lab experiments, ecological surveys, data modelling, professional placements and capstone projects, including immersive experiences on Heron Island. You'll also learn the tools industry uses, ensuring your skills align with employer expectations and easing the transition into professional roles.

description:
Bring creative ideas to life through design and communication. This double degree prepares you to create compelling visual experiences and communicate ideas that inform, influence and inspire. You'll graduate with the creative, strategic and technical skills to design meaningful experiences and deliver powerful stories across digital, print and emerging media. 

Highlights of studying the Bachelor of Design/Bachelor of Communication 

  • Gain practical skills in visual communication, branding, user experience, content creation, journalism, strategic communication and digital storytelling.  
  • Learn through studio projects, industry collaborations, internships and professional placements to build your experience and confidence. 
  • Study in innovative design studios and access industry-level communication facilities including digital television and radio studios, editing suites, journalism newsrooms and media production spaces.  
  • Learn from award-winning designers, journalists, communication specialists and researchers with extensive experience.  
  • Build critical thinking, creative problem-solving and persuasive communication skills valued across a wide range of industries.  
  • Explore ethical practice, sustainability and First Nations perspectives while developing solutions that create positive social impact.  
  • Take your learning global through international study tours and exchange opportunities.  


Creativity meets communication 

Great ideas have the biggest impact when they're communicated effectively. Combine creative design thinking with advanced communication practice, giving you the skills to design engaging experiences, build compelling brands and connect with audiences across multiple platforms. 

You'll gain hands-on experience using industry-standard technologies while working on real projects that strengthen your portfolio and professional networks. Whether you're creating visual identities, digital experiences, strategic campaigns or multimedia content, you'll graduate ready to collaborate across creative industries and adapt to emerging technologies, including AI-enabled creative tools. 

Double your career opportunities 

Graduating with qualifications in both design and communication provides a unique combination of creative, strategic and communication expertise valued by employers. You'll be equipped to work across multidisciplinary teams, leading projects that combine design, storytelling, branding and audience engagement across commercial, government and community sectors. 

Design majors 

Visual communication design: Learn to create powerful visual and graphic designs that inform, persuade and inspire. Build industry-ready skills in branding, print, digital media, motion and UX/UI while exploring the social and environmental impact of design.

Interior design: Design creative, sustainable and inclusive spaces that shape how people live, work and connect. Gain hands-on experience in architectural and digital design while developing strong analytical and critical thinking skills.

Product and user experience design: Use the latest digital technologies to design innovative products and experiences. Gain practical skills in 3D printing, virtual modelling, simulation and digital fabrication.

Communication majors 

Journalism: Build core reporting and writing skills across print, digital and broadcast platforms, from hard news to long-form features. You'll explore investigative techniques, global reporting and human rights journalism, gaining experience with tools like data visualisation, Freedom of Information processes and multimedia storytelling. With a focus on ethical, solutions-driven reporting, this major prepares you for a dynamic media landscape, whether in traditional newsrooms, digital media or independent journalism.

Strategic communication: Learn how to shape messages that influence, engage and inspire. This major prepares you to craft persuasive, ethical communication across industries, from media relations and public campaigns to health, crisis and entertainment communication. You'll gain practical experience developing strategy, managing media and responding to real scenarios including political campaigns and emergency events. Whether you're promoting a brand, managing reputation or navigating public discourse, you'll be equipped with the skills to lead communication in an evolving media landscape.

professionalAccreditation:
In Australia, professional accreditation of entry to practice engineering programs is the responsibility of Engineers Australia and is normally carried out on a five-yearly cycle. Griffith University underwent this review in August 2015.

Accreditation ensures academic institutions consistently meet national and international benchmarks and engineering graduates of an accredited program are assured membership with Engineers Australia at the relevant career grade and enjoy reciprocal privileges by equivalent professional bodies overseas.

Countries such as the United States of America, United Kingdom, Hong Kong (SAR), New Zealand, Canada, South Africa and others that are co-signatories to international agreements on joint recognition offer international recognition.

The Washington Accord, the Sydney Accord and the Dublin Accord recognise the substantial equivalence of accreditation systems and accredited programs across international boundaries at the Professional Engineer, Engineering Technologist and Engineering Associate levels respectively. Please refer to the International Engineering Alliance (IEA) website for more details.
Please see the Engineers Australia website for the most recent list of accredited programs.

description:
With this double degree, you can tackle environmental issues with knowledge across both engineering and science. With specialist skills in the social, applied and natural sciences, you'll be well prepared to find solutions to pressing environmental issues.

With a strong practical focus, you'll develop skills in the planning, design, management, construction and maintenance of engineering projects as well as a solid foundation in biological, physical and social sciences and critical analysis.

This is your opportunity to make a real difference to the big environmental issues facing the planet, bringing a fresh perspective and proven skills to the challenges ahead.

Industry and expert connections

From year one, you'll be learning from industry experts and like-minded teachers. Hands-on experience is key to this double degree, and in your final year you can enhance your knowledge through an industry-based project or placement.

Graduate outcomes

You'll have several options available when you graduate as either an engineer or an environmental scientist. This degree could lead to a career in civil, environmental, mechanical or electrical engineering. Your environmental science degree will offer up rewarding careers such as an environmental officer, environmental consultant, wildlife biologist, conservation ecologist or environmental chemist.

Majors

Engineering

  • Civil Engineering
  • Electronic Engineering
  • Environmental Engineering
  • Mechanical Engineering

Environmental Science

  • Ecology and Conservation
  • Environmental Management
  • Soil and Water Science
  • Urban Environments

Flexibility

Tailor your timetable - Even if you study full-time on-campus, you may still be able to customise your degree to suit your needs. From a range of tutorial times to online access to lectures and other course material, we're here to help you fit study in with your work and life commitments.

Global mobility

Students may be eligible to do an international field trip, organised by the academic staff. This may count towards a component of the degree. Visit Go Global Griffith for more information.

description:
Study urban planning and science together to design livable communities combining sustainable development and environmental management. Develop the scientific knowledge and planning expertise to respond to population growth, climate change, biodiversity loss and other infrastructure demands across Australia and overseas.

Highlights of studying the Bachelor of Urban Planning (Honours)/Bachelor of Science
  • Learn advanced skills in urban design and planning, sustainable development, transport systems, ecology, marine and wildlife biology and geography.
  • Build foundations in scientific research, data analysis and evidence-based decision-making.
  • Learn in design studios, advanced labs and real-world field environments. Our campuses are living laboratories offering natural settings to explore environmental science.
  • Experience a culture of support, with strong peer networks, personalised study help and lecturer mentoring.
  • Get professional experience with an industry placement or industry project and build your network before you graduate.
  • Complete an independent research project under expert supervision.
Hands-on experience in planning and science 

From your first year, you'll use planning theory and scientific principles to solve real challenges for growing cities and regions.

In studio settings, you'll create transport strategies, design resilient neighbourhoods and evaluate land use proposals. In science laboratories and field sites, you'll investigate ecosystems, analyse environmental data and develop solutions based on rigorous research.

You'll be taught by lecturers and industry practitioners with experience across the public sector, consulting and environmental management. Collaborative projects and site visits connect you to the profession, helping you build confidence as you study.

Your final year honours project strengthens your analytical skills and prepares you for roles needing high-level research abilities. It's also a direct pathway into postgraduate research at university, urban planning research or environmental public policy.

Double your opportunities

With an urban planning and science double degree, you'll have a competitive edge among other graduates, with employers increasingly seeking interdisciplinary expertise.

Employers value professionals who can interpret scientific evidence, understand policy frameworks and translate complex data into pragmatic solutions.

Get ready for careers bridging environmental science and urban development. Enjoy flexibility working across public and private sectors and make a positive impact on designing sustainable communities.

Majors

With the Bachelor of Science, you can choose from majors in:

  • Geography
  • Marine Biology
  • Wildlife Biology.

The Bachelor of Urban Planning covers:

  • environmental planning
  • regional and strategic planning
  • urban design
  • transport planning
  • community engagement
  • planning policy and sustainable development.

description:
The Brisbane South (Nathan) offering of this program is scheduled to be delivered at the Treasury Building at our Brisbane City campus in 2027. If scheduled opening is delayed, courses may be delivered all or in part at our other Brisbane locations.

The Graduate Diploma of Law Research Studies is an 80 credit point program designed to provide graduates in the Law discipline with the opportunity to undertake advanced study in research methodology and to undertake supervised research work, in the discipline area appropriate to their research trajectory.

The program provides the necessary preparation for entry into a higher degree research program (Doctor of Philosophy (PhD), Master of Philosophy (MPhil), or equivalent program) for applicants who do not possess the required qualifications for direct admission into these programs.

Upon successful completion of the program, students will be eligible to apply for admission to MPhil or PhD candidature, subject to fulfilment of the requirements for candidature as specified in the Higher Degree Research Policy . The grade achieved will determine eligibility for admission to either a Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) or Master of Philosophy (MPhil) candidature.

The Program Director will be responsible for the overall supervision of students in the program and for monitoring their progress throughout the program.

Students may choose to exit the Graduate Diploma program (after successfully completing the specified courses) with the Graduate Certificate in Law Research Studies.

description:
Increase system resilience in the face of climate change.

Gain a sound interdisciplinary knowledge of climate change, and tools that increase society's resilience to its impacts, in this graduate certificate. Designed for professionals from any background, this certificate provides the ability to analyse impacts of climate change while also developing the creative skills needed to build durability against those impacts across society and the environment.

This includes the ability to develop and deploy adaptation strategies to protect communities, businesses, government agencies, infrastructure, and natural assets. These skills can be applied at the local, national and international levels in the private, community, and public sectors.

As a student, you will be empowered to get involved in improving the planning of urban areas, providing better services to the public to improve wellbeing. In the process, you'll support the transformation of economic development, the creation of new management plans to conserve biodiversity, the development of treaties to protect major earth systems, and more.

Industry and expert connections

Through collaboration in group projects, you'll have the opportunity to use your disciplinary background and skills to delve deeper into some aspect of this key global issue while working alongside student peers from a variety of professions. The interactive nature of this graduate certificate will ensure you can make connections with fellow students and our academics, which will be valuable additions to your professional network in this burgeoning field of climate change adaptation.

Graduate outcomes

The global commitment to mitigate climate change requires structural changes in the global economy, and that means knowledge in this area will be increasingly relevant not only in the environmental sciences but also in other disciplines, such as business, engineering, planning, and public health. Climate influences all aspects of the earth's systems, including ecosystem function and structure, human health, agricultural productivity and our overall socio-economic well-being. This graduate certificate also offers a pathway to further study in our Master of Climate Change Adaptation.

Flexibility

Study anytime, anywhere - This degree is available online through our Digital campus, giving you more room to fit university with your work and social life.

Pursue further study

The courses in this graduate certificate may be credited towards a related graduate diploma or masters degree. Griffith's innovative Credit Precedent Database allows you to find out what credit decisions have been made in the past, which will give you an idea of what you can expect.

description:
Some courses in this program are scheduled to be offered at the Treasury Building at our Brisbane City campus in 2027. If scheduled opening is delayed, courses may be delivered all or in part at our other Brisbane locations.

Queensland's #1 university for AI research. (ShanghaiRanking's Global Ranking of Academic Subjects, tied position, 2026)

Combine analytical thinking with tech skills in the Bachelor of Science/Bachelor of Information Technology double degree. This future-focused degree equips you with the scientific knowledge and digital expertise to tackle challenges across health, environment, industry and beyond, while benefiting from academic support and mentoring from supportive, approachable lecturers.

Explore fundamental science and computing concepts in your first year before choosing from a range of majors and electives that reflect your interests and career goals. Whether you're coding intelligent systems, solving complex scientific problems, or analysing environmental data, this double degree prepares you to lead in research, innovation and technology-driven industries.

Highlights of studying the Bachelor of Science/Bachelor of Information Technology
  • Graduate with two highly valued qualifications with just one extra year of study.
  • Build a personalised skillset by pairing a science major with a complementary IT major.
  • Get hands-on experience in state-of-the-art labs and work on real projects with major industry and research partners.
  • Study science where nature is your classroom: our campuses are living laboratories, offering direct access to bushland, waterways and marine ecosystems. Gain experience through fieldwork, research placements or internships with local and global organisations.
  • Flexible study options with intakes in Trimester 1, 2 and 3.
Built for cross-disciplinary innovation

This double degree opens the door to a wide range of careers across science, technology, research and industry. You'll graduate ready to work in health informatics, environmental modelling, biotech, defence, smart systems or research and development. The combination of science and IT gives you the tools to analyse data, design solutions and lead change.

Learn from experts and apply your learning in industry settings

Your learning is guided by leading academics and researchers with deep industry connections. In your final year, you'll apply your skills through hands-on research projects, placements or collaborative industry experiences. These experiences will sharpen your problem-solving and teamwork skills, build your professional network and enhance your graduate portfolio.

Information Technology majors
  • Networks and Cyber Security
  • Software Development

description:
The Master of Integrated Water Management creates water leaders by drawing on international teaching and research from many fields to provide a trans-disciplinary, whole-of-water-cycle approach to water management.

The program aims to build the capacity of future leaders in water management, with an emphasis on professionals working in Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) and development, urban water management, across water, land and people and in water finance for the achievement of sustainable development goals. The program equips students with practical tools and skills for developing and managing the adoption of innovative solutions to local, regional, national and international water management issues. Students will develop the strategic, managerial and technical skills they need to advance in the water sector.

The program is managed and led by the International WaterCentre (IWC). The IWC is a key capacity building organisation in the global water sector and dedicated to providing education and training to promote whole-of-water cycle approaches to integrated water management around the world.

description:
The Brisbane South (Nathan) offering of this program is scheduled to be delivered at the Treasury Building at our Brisbane City campus in 2027. If scheduled opening is delayed, courses may be delivered all or in part at our other Brisbane locations.

The Diploma of International Tourism and Hotel Management is a pathway program designed to help you transition into the Bachelor of International Tourism and Hotel Management. You'll develop foundational knowledge and skills in a supportive learning environment, setting you up for success in your future studies.

The tourism and hospitality industry is evolving, with a shift towards progressive, innovative workplace and industry practices. You'll learn the skills, values and opportunities future industry leaders will need to succeed. The Diploma of International Tourism and Hotel Management will teach you modern business practices, such as adaptability, creativity, diversity, and sustainability, along with foundational marketing and business management theory the industry needs.

You'll study an academic foundation course that prepares you for your university studies, as well as courses on business decision making, fundamentals of hospitality, global tourism system, interpreting tourism management information, and why money matters, with additional support and access to a dedicated First Year Coordinator and (PASS), run by high-achieving students.

description:
Prepare for a rewarding career helping people reach their potential. This degree combines a solid foundation in psychological science with advanced training in rehabilitation counselling, giving you the knowledge and skills to make a real difference in people's lives.

Highlights of studying the Bachelor of Psychological Science/Master of Rehabilitation Counselling
  • Study psychological theory and practice, including research methods, assessment, behaviour change, counselling skills and positive psychology.
  • Gain specialist knowledge in rehabilitation counselling, learning how to support people with disability, injury or vocational disadvantage.
  • Develop practical experience through a minimum of 200 hours supervised practicum placement in real rehabilitation or clinical settings.
  • Learn how to integrate psychological principles with applied counselling and case management to deliver meaningful outcomes for clients.
  • Engage in research, dissertation work and advanced projects to deepen your understanding of human behaviour and professional practice.
  • Prepare for professional accreditation, further study and future career pathways in psychology, rehabilitation, health, social services and related fields.
Learn the skills to understand, support and empower others

You'll begin by exploring the many facets of psychology, from cognitive, biological and social psychology to development, health and organisational behaviour. You'll gain practical skills in research, assessment, counselling and group facilitation. As you progress, you'll dive deeper into rehabilitation counselling, learning about injury management, vocational assessment, job placement, disability studies and applied counselling.

description:
Study at the intersection of science and communication and share big ideas in ways the world can understand. In this double degree, you'll build scientific expertise while learning how to craft stories, reports, campaigns and media content that informs, inspires and influences.

Study science where nature is your classroom on our living lab campuses surrounded by bushland, waterways and marine ecosystems, and develop the skills to communicate complex ideas with clarity and impact. Whether you're explaining climate data, producing a health campaign, or reporting on breakthrough research, you'll graduate ready to engage diverse audiences across platforms.

Highlights of studying the Bachelor of Communication/Bachelor of Science
  • Build a strong foundation in scientific knowledge while developing communication, writing, media production skills and content development for diverse audiences.
  • Be supported by approachable lecturers with tailored academic support and mentoring in a collaborative learning environment.
  • Explore how media, technology and global communication shape the way science is understood.
  • Get hands-on experience through lab work, data analysis, fieldwork, video and audio storytelling and digital content production.
  • Study in living laboratory environments across our nature-filled campuses.
  • Tailor your studies with majors that match your interests and career goals.
  • Boost your employability with strong industry connections and placement opportunities, including an industry internship, practical communication projects and a science capstone experience.
Turn scientific insight into stories, strategies and impact

Work with real scientific data, experiment in advanced labs and create multimedia projects that bring science to life. From social media strategy and public writing to investigative journalism and ethical communication, you'll gain the tools to navigate today's media landscape. Graduates are prepared for careers in science communication, journalism, public relations, health promotion, environmental communication, government, research support roles and any field where scientific understanding and communication expertise come together.

description:
Successful design leaders need to understand technology, culture and business. Deepen your creative practice and learn how to become a leader in the design industry with a Graduate Certificate in Design.

Highlights of studying the Graduate Certificate in Design
  • Explore emerging design practice, strategy and innovation.
  • Develop expertise in experience design, visual language and advanced technologies.
  • Build your skills in visual communication, prototyping and spatial design.
  • Engage with real design challenges and socially responsive practice.
  • Complete a postgraduate qualification in as little as six months full-time.
Expand your creative and strategic capability

Investigate global issues influencing design and learn how to respond to complex social, economic and environmental contexts. Refine your communication skills to effectively share your ideas across digital and interactive platforms, while also developing advanced skills in usability, visual hierarchy, 2D/3D design and creative visualisation. Through hands-on learning, you'll learn emerging tools, digital fabrication techniques, and spatial design concepts, allowing you to work across physical and virtual environments.

A pathway to the Master of Design

Whether you're returning to study, transitioning from another discipline or preparing for the Master of Design (5720), this graduate certificate provides a focused path into postgraduate design study. Strengthen your creative thinking, research capability, academic writing, critical analysis skills and digital fluency while building a portfolio that reflects advanced design knowledge and contemporary practice.

description:
The Brisbane South (Nathan) offering of this program is scheduled to be delivered at the Treasury Building at our Brisbane City campus in 2027. If scheduled opening is delayed, courses may be delivered all or in part at our other Brisbane locations.

Advance your leadership impact with an Executive Master of Public Administration (EMPA) and prepare to lead at the highest levels of government and the public sector. Delivered in conjunction with the Australian and New Zealand School of Government (ANZSOG), this degree equips you with the strategic management, policy and financial expertise needed to navigate complexity, drive reform and deliver measurable public value.

This degree blends academic rigour with practical application. You'll strengthen your ability to lead public sector change, design evidence-based policy and manage organisations in demanding environments.

Highlights of studying the Executive Master of Public Administration
  • Develop advanced skills in public policy, public sector management and public financial management.
  • Build expertise for decision-making in uncertainty by using quantitative analysis, modelling and evidence-based approaches.
  • Learn to design and evaluate public policies and programs that balance economic, social and environmental priorities.
  • Examine how government operates within a market economy, with a strong focus on Australian and New Zealand contexts.
  • Strengthen your leadership capability through dedicated study in public sector change, ethics, accountability and governance.
  • Learn directly from experienced practitioners and lecturers with deep experience in government, policy and administration.
Applied learning for executive leaders

Explore the real tensions between political imperatives and bureaucratic processes through interactive teaching, case-based discussions and collaborative learning with your peers. You'll critically examine your own management philosophy, refine your leadership approach and expand your capacity to guide teams through reform and uncertainty.

Work-based projects that deliver real impact

A defining feature of this degree is the emphasis on strong workplace application. You'll tackle complex challenges drawn from your own professional context. Your capstone experience will give you an opportunity to present evidence-based recommendations with the clarity and delivery expected from executive leaders. Working in cross-jurisdictional teams and supported by project advisors and agency sponsors, you'll design and deliver solutions that respond to pressing policy issues or organisational challenges.

description:
Our river basins or catchments have been progressively transformed over time. We've built cities, we've cleared land for food production and this has had profound consequences for our catchments.

With this specialist degree you'll learn to combine and use scientific, engineering and economic knowledge to planning ways to protect, restore and rehabilitate our catchments. You'll develop the leading edge knowledge and skills needed to make a difference in this rapidly developing area of professional practice. The Master of Catchment Science is the only catchment-dedicated postgraduate degree in the world. Hosted by the International WaterCentre and developed and delivered in collaboration with Griffith University.

Industry and expert connections

We've spoken to the industry about the kinds of skills they're looking for to fill the roles required. This degree provides the right mix of new knowledge, covering natural sciences, monitoring, data analysis, modelling and economics. We offer consistent opportunities for work-integrated learning along with a week-long study field trip.

Graduate outcomes

This is an opportunity to accelerate your position in the planning of projects related to the protection, maintenance or restoration of catchments. You'll have the latest skills in data sensing, analysis and computer modelling, underpinned by robust scientific knowledge and be ready to further your career in the planning and design of green infrastructure in urban and non-urban contexts.

Create, innovate and collaborate with industry as you build your future in design and technology. This double degree combines creative design practice with technical IT capability, giving you the skills to imagine, prototype and deliver engaging digital products, services and experiences. 

This degree addresses the growing need for designers who can respond to complex challenges creatively, ethically and sustainably. When combined with information technology, you'll gain the technical skills to bring your ideas to life across digital platforms and interactive environments. 

You'll build practical capability across areas such as user experience, digital product design, software development, data, emerging technologies and interactive systems. With access to Griffith's advanced IT and design facilities, you'll learn how to turn creative concepts into functional, user-centred digital solutions. 

 Highlights of studying the Bachelor of Information Technology/Bachelor of Design 

  • Work with industry experts to tackle real challenges and develop innovative, practical solutions. 
  • Learn hands-on to build strong creative and technical skills, combining digital design with IT knowledge to deliver real-world outcomes. 
  • Specialise in your chosen areas, choosing one major in Design and one in IT. 
  • You'll study in innovative studio spaces at the Queensland College of Art and Design, with access to world-class facilities including galleries, maker spaces fabrication workshops, and purpose-built design studios. 
  • Access advanced IT facilities, including virtual and augmented reality, Cyber Range, Big Data Visualisation Lab and Cisco Networking Lab. 
  • Build industry experience through internships, studio projects, industry projects and possible paid placement opportunities such as with Griffith's App Factory. 
  • Develop critical and strategic thinking and learn to communicate your ideas clearly and persuasively. 
  • Learn from award-winning designers and educators with experience across diverse design fields. 
  • Study in an inclusive program that values social impact, sustainability and First Nations perspectives. 
  • Take your learning global with overseas study opportunities ranging from short programs to extended exchange. 
  • Graduate with two complimentary degrees that broaden your career options across design, technology, digital product development and user experience.

description:
The Graduate Diploma of Criminological Research Studies is an 80 credit point program designed to provide graduates in the criminology and criminal justice discipline with the opportunity to undertake advanced study in research methodology and to undertake supervised research work in the discipline area appropriate to their research trajectory.

The program provides the necessary preparation for entry into a higher degree research program (Doctor of Philosophy (PhD), Master of Philosophy (MPhil) or equivalent program) for applicants who do not possess the required qualifications for direct admission into these programs.

Upon successful completion of the program, students will be eligible to apply for admission to MPhil or PhD candidature subject to fulfilment of the requirements for candidature as specified in the Higher Degree Research Policy. The grade achieved will determine eligibility for admission to either a PhD or MPhil candidature.

The Program Director will be responsible for the overall supervision of students in the program and for monitoring their progress throughout the program.

Students may choose to exit the Graduate Diploma program (after successfully completing the specified courses) with the Graduate Certificate in Criminological Research Studies.

description:
The Brisbane South (Nathan) offering of this program is scheduled to be delivered at the Treasury Building at our Brisbane City campus in 2027. If scheduled opening is delayed, courses may be delivered all or in part at our other Brisbane locations.

Become an asset for businesses with the Graduate Certificate in Research Studies in Business. Designed for aspiring researchers, future PhD candidates and professionals seeking to deepen their research expertise, this program offers rigorous training in research methods, sought after within business, economics and finance.

Highlights of studying the Graduate Certificate in Research Studies in Business
  • Learn advanced skills in research methods and design for the business and finance sectors.
  • Build expertise in quantitative analysis, econometrics and qualitative research.
  • Develop your statistical capability using business analytics and data tools.
  • Learn how to translate research into journal publications, industry reports and conference papers.
  • Be supported by experienced researchers, offering mentoring and guidance as you refine your research topic.
  • Graduate with a postgraduate qualification in just six months of full-time study.
Build advanced research skills for business and economics

Quality research is central to innovation, effective decision-making and strategic leadership. You'll learn how to align research questions with appropriate methodologies. Explore experimental design, case studies and theory-driven inquiry while developing critical thinking and academic writing skills essential for success.

Beyond research methodology, you'll learn how to translate research into meaningful outputs. You'll develop the communication skills to share findings with academic, industry and media audiences.

Gain a deeper understanding of the research publication process by learning how to identify high-quality outlets and strategies for positioning your work for selection by conferences and peer-reviewed journals.

A pathway to higher degree research

Whether you're preparing for PhD study or seeking promotion into research-focused roles within industry, this graduate certificate gives you the confidence, research literacy and methodological depth to succeed in higher-level research.

On graduating, you may also be eligible to progress to the Graduate Diploma of Research Studies in Business (4160) or into a PhD.
